  - A Jan 28 2025 blog post said App Store and Flatpak builds were not supported and the minimum version was 2025.1.2 (https://bitwarden.com/blog/ssh-agent/). The current help page lists both, so it wins.
- **Socket paths:**
  - macOS App Store: `~/Library/Containers/com.bitwarden.desktop/Data/.bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock`
  - macOS .dmg: `~/.bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock`
  - Linux: `~/.bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock`
  - Snap: `~/snap/bitwarden/current/.bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock`
  - Flatpak: `~/.var/app/com.bitwarden.desktop/data/.bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock`
- **Windows:** pipe `\\.\pipe\openssh-ssh-agent` (`PIPE_NAME` in https://github.com/bitwarden/clients/blob/main/apps/desktop/desktop_native/ssh_agent/src/server/listener/windows.rs). You must first set the "OpenSSH Authentication Agent" service to Disabled.
- **Prompts:** the setting "Ask for authorization when using SSH agent". A locked vault asks to unlock, then to authorize.
- **Key types:** Ed25519 and RSA. Imports must be OpenSSH or PKCS#8; PuTTY keys don't work. `ssh-add` can't manage the agent, and it tries every vault key in turn (https://bitwarden.com/help/about-ssh/).
- **Agent v2 (Mar 26 2026):** an internal rebuild with "UX isn't changing" (https://community.bitwarden.com/t/ssh-agent-whats-changing-and-what-to-expect/95308).

**b. Generating in the app:** yes. New → SSH key → name → Save. "At this time, Bitwarden can only generate ED25519 type SSH keys" (https://bitwarden.com/help/about-ssh/).

**c. `bw` CLI**
- Type 5 = SSH Key is documented, but the CLI docs say nothing about generating keys (https://bitwarden.com/help/cli/).
- **No `item.sshKey` template.** The `getTemplate` switch in https://github.com/bitwarden/clients/blob/main/apps/cli/src/commands/get.command.ts (main branch) has no such case.
- The export model has `privateKey`, `publicKey` and `keyFingerprint`. `toView` requires `privateKey`, and also requires the public key and fingerprint unless feature flag `PM40201_DeriveSSHKeys` is on (https://github.com/bitwarden/clients/blob/main/libs/common/src/models/export/ssh-key.export.ts, used in `apps/cli/src/vault/create.command.ts`).
- **The CLI can't generate keys.** The caller must supply the private key bytes, so a plaintext key passes through your process (keep it in memory).
- Likely shape: `bw get template item | jq '.type=5 | .login=null | .sshKey={privateKey:..., publicKey:..., keyFingerprint:...}' | bw encode | bw create item`. The top-level `sshKey` property name is inferred from the model; **UNVERIFIED end to end**.
- **SDK:** `generate_sshkey(KeyAlgorithm)` supports Ed25519, RSA 3072/4096 and ECDSA P-256/384/521, and returns an OpenSSH private key, public key and fingerprint. It is exposed through wasm/uniffi, not `bw` (https://github.com/bitwarden/sdk-internal/blob/main/crates/bitwarden-ssh/src/generator.rs).
- **`bws` (Secrets Manager CLI):** no generation found. **UNVERIFIED**

## 2. 1Password
- **Sockets** (https://www.1password.dev/ssh/get-started/):
  - macOS: `~/Library/Group Containers/2BUA8C4S2C.com.1password/t/agent.sock` (or a symlink at `~/.1password/agent.sock`)
  - Linux: `~/.1password/agent.sock`
  - Windows: `\\.\pipe\openssh-ssh-agent`, after disabling the OpenSSH agent service
- **Key types:** Ed25519 or RSA only. Every request needs explicit approval. Linux Flatpak and Snap installs aren't supported (https://www.1password.dev/ssh/agent/).
- **CLI** (https://www.1password.dev/cli/ssh-keys/, needs `op` 2.20.0+):
  - Generate: `op item create --category ssh --title "..."` (Ed25519 by default), or `--ssh-generate-key RSA,2048|3072|4096`. The exact lowercase value `ed25519` is **UNVERIFIED**.
  - Public key: the `public key` field, e.g. `op read "op://&lt;vault&gt;/&lt;item&gt;/public key"`.
  - Private key: `?ssh-format=openssh`.
  - Importing an existing key needs the desktop app.
- `op` isn't installed on this Mac.

## 3. macOS built-ins
**a. Apple Passwords:** no SSH key support (https://sixcolors.com/post/2026/01/wish-list-ssh-keys-in-passwords/; not an Apple source, but Apple's docs list no SSH keys).

**b. Secure Enclave through `/usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib`**
- Local `man 8 ssh-keychain`: it provides CryptoTokenKit identities, "RSA for PKCS#11 and ecdsa256 for Secure Key module".
- Local `man sc_auth`: `sc_auth create-ctk-identity -l label -k p-256|...|p-256-ne|p-384-ne [-t bio|none]` ("-ne" = non-exportable).
- Flow (https://gist.github.com/arianvp/5f59f1783e3eaf1a2d4cd8e952bb4acf):
  1. `sc_auth create-ctk-identity -l ssh -k p-256-ne -t bio`
  2. `ssh-keygen -w /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib -K -N ""`. This writes an `id_ecdsa_sk_rk` stub plus `.pub`.
  3. Or `ssh-add -K -S /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib`.
  4. Use it with `SecurityKeyProvider /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib` or `SSH_SK_PROVIDER`.
- **Limits:** ecdsa-sk (P-256) only, no ed25519-sk; resident-style only; no attestation; comments can't be edited; a label-overwrite bug. `SSH_SK_PROVIDER` works in Apple ssh but not Homebrew ssh (https://lists.mindrot.org/pipermail/openssh-unix-dev/2024-July/041451.html, Jul 2024).
- **Which macOS versions:** the dylib exists here (macOS 26.6.2). The first version with SK support is **UNVERIFIED** (the gist says Tahoe and Sequoia; there is no Apple doc).

**c. Keychain passphrases:** local `man ssh-add` documents `--apple-use-keychain` / `--apple-load-keychain`; `man ssh_config` documents `UseKeychain` (default no). Only the passphrase is stored; the encrypted key file stays on disk.

**d. Secretive** (https://github.com/maxgoedjen/secretive; latest v3.0.4, 2025-11-27)
- Secure Enclave keys can't be exported or backed up, and keys are 256-bit EC only (FAQ.md).
- Touch ID / Apple Watch access control; a smart card (YubiKey) fallback for Macs without a Secure Enclave; `brew install secretive`.
- **Socket:** `~/Library/Containers/com.maxgoedjen.Secretive.SecretAgent/Data/socket.ssh` (https://github.com/maxgoedjen/secretive/issues/402).
- Keys are generated in the GUI. **No CLI found. UNVERIFIED**

**e. Apple ssh-keygen with a YubiKey:** no built-in USB HID support.
- `ssh -Q key` lists the sk types, but `otool -L` shows no libfido2.
- `/usr/libexec/ssh-sk-helper` contains the string "internal security key support not enabled".
- Yubico: macOS OpenSSH "is not compiled with libfido2"; use Homebrew openssh (https://developers.yubico.com/SSH/Securing_SSH_with_FIDO2.html).

## 4. YubiKey / FIDO2 (same Yubico page)
- `ed25519-sk` needs firmware 5.2.3+; `ecdsa-sk` works on all FIDO2 YubiKeys.
- `-O resident` needs 5.2.3+ and a PIN; `ssh-keygen -K` recovers keys (OpenSSH 8.3+).
- `-O verify-required` needs OpenSSH 8.4+.
- `-O application=ssh:NAME` keeps multiple resident keys apart.
- The key file "does not contain your private key, only a reference" (a key handle).
- **PIV:** `yubico-piv-tool -s 9a -a generate` then selfsign; `ssh-keygen -D libykcs11.dylib -e`; `ssh -I libykcs11`. RSA 3072/4096 needs firmware 5.7+ (https://developers.yubico.com/PIV/Guides/SSH_with_PIV_and_PKCS11.html).

## 5. Linux
- **KeePassXC:** keys are attachments in the encrypted database. They're added to the agent on unlock and removed on lock, with confirm/lifetime options; it can generate keys and works with OpenSSH, Pageant and gpg-agent (https://keepassxc.org/docs/KeePassXC_UserGuide#_ssh_agent). The decrypted key does sit in agent memory.
- **ssh-tpm-agent** (https://github.com/Foxboron/ssh-tpm-agent): ECDSA P-256 and RSA; `ssh-tpm-keygen` makes `.tpm` keys; `--print-socket`; `--install-user-units`; can import existing keys; PIN; proxy mode; TPM 2.0 on Linux.
- **gpg-agent:** `enable-ssh-support` (plus win32-openssh/putty options); sshcontrol is deprecated (https://www.gnupg.org/documentation/manuals/gnupg/Agent-Options.html). The OpenPGP card flow and `gpgconf --list-dirs agent-ssh-socket` are **UNVERIFIED** (the Arch wiki was blocked).
- **gnome-keyring / gcr-ssh-agent** and **tpm2-pkcs11:** not researched. **UNVERIFIED**

## 6. Windows
- **Built-in agent:** `ssh-agent` service, disabled by default; enable with `Set-Service -StartupType Automatic` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/openssh/openssh_keymanagement, updated 2026-04-21). The pipe name is confirmed only through Bitwarden and 1Password sources.
- **FIDO:** Win32-OpenSSH 8.9.0.0+ (the 8.9.0.0 MSI has a bug). `ssh-keygen -t ecdsa-sk [-O resident]`; downloading resident keys needs an elevated terminal (https://github.com/PowerShell/Win32-OpenSSH/wiki/FIDO---U2F-usage).
- **Windows Hello / TPM:** non-resident ecdsa-sk works with Windows Hello, per a non-vendor blog (https://svrooij.io/2024/01/01/secure-ssh-windows-hello/). The webauthn.dll detail is **UNVERIFIED** from vendor docs. Issue #2279 reports external-key failures on 24H2.
- **WinCryptSSHAgent:** uses CryptoAPI certificates and PIV cards over named pipe, Unix socket, Pageant or XShell, with WSL support (https://github.com/buptczq/WinCryptSSHAgent).

## 7. Comparison

| Provider | OSes | Key generated where | Private key leaves device? | Socket/pipe | Non-interactive CLI generation? | Maturity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bitwarden agent | mac/Linux/Win | Desktop app (Ed25519) or imported | Synced in encrypted vault; loaded in app memory | See 1a; Win `\\.\pipe\openssh-ssh-agent` | No; `bw` needs caller-supplied key | GA since 2025.1.2; v2 rebuild 2026 |
| 1Password agent | mac/Linux/Win | `op` or app (Ed25519/RSA) | Synced in encrypted vault | See 2 | Yes: `op item create --category ssh` | Mature |
| Apple SE + ssh-keychain.dylib | macOS | Secure Enclave (`sc_auth`) | No (`-ne`) | none (provider dylib) or system agent | Yes (`sc_auth` + `ssh-keygen -K`); Touch ID at use | New, rough edges |
| Secretive | macOS | Secure Enclave | No | `~/Library/Containers/com.maxgoedjen.Secretive.SecretAgent/Data/socket.ssh` | No (GUI) | Stable, v3.0.4 |
| YubiKey FIDO2 (`-sk`) | all (mac needs Homebrew openssh) | On the key | No | stub file / any agent | Yes, but needs a touch | Mature |
| YubiKey PIV (PKCS#11) | all | On the key | No | `PKCS11Provider` | Yes (`yubico-piv-tool`) | Mature |
| KeePassXC | all | App or imported | Stays in database; decrypted into agent | system agent / Pageant | No | Mature |
| ssh-tpm-agent | Linux | TPM | No (sealed) | `--print-socket` | Yes (`ssh-tpm-keygen`) | Active |
| Win OpenSSH FIDO / Hello | Windows | Security key or Hello (TPM) | No | `\\.\pipe\openssh-ssh-agent` | Needs Hello/touch prompt | 8.9+, some bugs |
| gpg-agent + OpenPGP card | all | On the card | No | gpg agent-ssh socket | Partly | Mature |

**For your macOS setup:** stock `/usr/bin/ssh-keygen -t ed25519-sk` won't talk to a YubiKey. Your built-in options are Apple Secure Enclave keys (ecdsa-sk only) or an agent socket from 1Password, Bitwarden or Secretive. For Bitwarden, the only way to create keys without a person in the loop is the SDK, not `bw`.</result>

Both investigations are back, and I've checked the Secure Enclave provider and the Bitwarden CLI myself. The findings:
- **Bitwarden:** the desktop app can create Ed25519 keys and serve them from its SSH agent. The `bw` CLI has no command that generates a key: you'd have to hand it the private key yourself.
- **1Password:** its `op` CLI can generate SSH keys directly in the vault.
- **macOS:** the built-in `/usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib` can create non-exportable Secure Enclave keys, but only of the ECDSA type. The system's OpenSSH can't talk to a YubiKey; that needs Homebrew openssh.
- **Apple Passwords:** doesn't support SSH keys.

## Design asks
Propose phases in dependency order, each shippable:
P1 Custom name/location/comment: TUI generate path editable (e.g. generate choice opens a path form prefilled with default, keeping Generate=true; plus comment), CLI picker asks optional comment; clear errors for parent dir rules (offer to create a missing subdirectory under ~/.ssh with 0700? evaluate against "nested dirs require preparation" rule).
P2 Agent providers: named agent discovery (Bitwarden/1Password/Secretive known socket list per OS, plus custom path) as KeyCatalogRequest extra sockets; picker groups "Bitwarden agent: <key>"; selecting an agent key stores `IdentityAgent <socket>` (+ IdentitiesOnly yes + optional IdentityFile pointing to a public-key file? consider writing the .pub for exact identity selection) in the managed fragment; decide compatibility strategy for new directives (additive v1 vs v2 header; how older binaries react; foreign aliases: cannot write, must explain manual IdentityAgent). Proof/policy-mismatch interplay. TUI support for agent keys (OnboardRequest needs fingerprint/socket rather than path). Doctor/diagnostics: detect provider installed but agent disabled (Bitwarden case here).
P3 Hardware-backed generation: key types in KeyRequest/KeyPlan (ed25519, ed25519-sk, ecdsa-sk), sk options (resident, verify-required, application), provider selection: YubiKey via a libfido2-capable ssh-keygen (detect Homebrew `/opt/homebrew/bin/ssh-keygen` capability; how to probe without a device), macOS Secure Enclave via `sc_auth` + `ssh-keygen -w /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib -K` and fragment `SecurityKeyProvider`. Post-generation checks for stubs, interactive touch/PIN, no-replace publication of stub files, bootstrap using the stub.
P4 Vault-created keys: 1Password `op item create --category ssh` (key never on disk; then agent key selection via 1Password socket); Bitwarden: evaluate (a) guided hand-off (create in app, enable agent, then dev picks from Bitwarden agent) vs (b) in-memory Go generation (golang.org/x/crypto/ssh MarshalPrivateKey) + `bw create item` type 5 over stdin with verification by listing the Bitwarden agent — note unverified JSON shape, locked vault, never write bytes to disk, ErrUnknown handling; recommend which to ship first.
Also: where provider preferences live (new [ssh] config or none), tuiissue/doctor entries, docs + skill + CHANGELOG sync, and a recommendations table for docs. Flag decisions that need the user and risks (can't test hardware locally; agent approval prompts; Windows pipe).

100	## Behavioral contracts
101	
102	- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`. READY/REVIEW/MERGED/RETIRED are action readiness or result milestones, never extra persisted states.
103	- Persisted intent, observed facts, and guarded action plans are separate layers. Unknown, failed, skipped, loading, or stale observations never become a false clean/closed fact.
104	- Use an explicit base for branch/worktree creation. Do not infer a safe base from whichever branch happens to be checked out.
105	- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
106	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
107	- Submodule initialization uses committed gitlinks, never implicitly advances to `main`. Whole child-clone disposal requires explicit recursive approval and fresh recovery proof for its private refs/objects; outer and shared canonical repositories are retained. Local graph refresh never performs remote proof. Child task/runtime/artifact claims block parent disposal.
108	- A taskflow Plan is bound to the exact task revision and repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact identities shown at Plan time. Apply must lock, reload, and revalidate those identities; a changed revision or authority produces a stale-plan result with no new effect.
109	- Managed rows receive only legal mode/state lifecycle actions. An unmanaged linked checkout may be adopted by metadata-only task creation or removed only when exact, clean, unclaimed, non-harness, and branch-preserving; canonical, harness-owned, ambiguous/conflicting, locked, prunable, or incompletely observed rows fail closed for destructive actions.
110	- Local repository refresh must not contact remotes. Fetching refs and querying a forge are explicit network actions, and review evidence is run-local manual evidence limited to portable existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time fields; never infer review decisions or checks.
111	- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, command-level `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews. `dev flow` is plan-first regardless of the adapted command's normal CLI interaction.
112	- Raw Git and configured external tools remain outside dev-mediated locks, revalidation, and safety guarantees. Existing expert CLI flags remain compatibility surface even when the preview flow deliberately omits them.
113	- A recognized agent in a canonical checkout occupies it regardless of whether its status is working, idle, done, or unknown. Shared-writer overrides require coordinated disjoint ownership.
114	- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.
115	- `dev ls --json` is an external automation contract. Add fields rather than renaming/removing existing fields; apply the same compatibility care to other documented structured output.
116	- Quick notes attach to the canonical repository through catalog identity. Markdown is durable, note deletion requires confirmation, and clearing/rebuilding note FTS must never delete source files.
117	- Explicit SSH format/organize and fleet profile rename/remove are plan-first exceptions for user-selected files; retain comments, Include order, original metadata and private recovery. Never activate dormant files with a new broad Include. Herdr machine add may prepare/start a remote server; leave native approvals native, and remove/disable never stops remote sessions.
118	- SSH initialization is report-before-apply; managed host changes are confined to canonical dev-owned fragments. Full bootstrap requires an explicit existing key or explicit generation, registers fleet only when explicitly selected, and reports interrupted remote installation as unknown rather than pretending to roll it back.
119	- SSH wizard permission preflight may separately review and apply metadata-only tightening on exact current-user-owned canonical/selected paths. Local key listing evaluates OpenSSH only behind explicit `--alias`; selected key material remains service-bound and is revalidated before configuration changes and bootstrap.
120	- `dev ssh key doctor` exposes the same permission Plan/Apply with bounded metadata-only key discovery; `--key` restricts the reviewed scope, and `--fix` requires a complete safe plan plus confirmation. Default doctor never mutates, reads private contents, or queries agents/remotes. Batch repairs revalidate the whole reviewed union and retain successful tightening on partial failure.
121	- Source-aware SSH setup can use `--auth existing` without installing a key, and registers only explicitly selected `--to fleet|herdr|both` destinations. Tailscale SSH advertisement is advisory; its port-22 endpoint is not an authorized_keys bootstrap target. Preserve the key-authentication guard and never treat Tailscale policy login as proof that a selected public key worked. Names, ports and cached observations never authorize machine merges; binding/source changes invalidate reviewed plans.
122	- Fleet-source SSH discovery selects explicit hosts without recursive fleet traversal. Normal SSH errors retain child exit status.

126	## Versioning and changelog
127	
128	The current published baseline is `v0.2.37` (2026-09-14). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
129	
130	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
131	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
132	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
133	
134	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
135	
136	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
137	
138	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
139	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
140	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
141	
142	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.
143	
144	For a release:
145	
146	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
147	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
148	3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
149	4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
150	5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, create the GitHub release, and publish the matching Homebrew formula. The repository secret `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` must be a fine-grained token with Contents write access to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`; a tap publication failure fails the release job so it can be retried instead of leaving Homebrew users stale.
151	
152	If the Homebrew step needs a retry or an older stable release needs a one-time backfill, run `gh workflow run publish-homebrew.yml -f version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. The manual workflow verifies that the release exists and republishes only the formula; it does not create or move a tag or GitHub release.
153	
154	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.
155	
156	## Keep implementation, skill, and docs aligned
157	
158	`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.
159	
160	| Change | Required synchronization |
161	|---|---|
162	| Cobra command name, `Use`, `Short`, flag, or global option | Run `make skill-sync`, inspect `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`, then run `make skill-check`. Never edit the generated block by hand. |
163	| Task modes/states/defaults or lifecycle preconditions | Update `SKILL.md`, `references/task-lifecycle.md`, README, embedded help, relevant English and zh-TW workflow/mental-model/compatibility pages, and transition tests. |
164	| Worktree placement, provisioning, include rules, strategies, or safety checks | Update `references/worktree-ownership.md`, README/public worktree docs, config examples, and focused `wt` tests. |
165	| Runtime protocol, fallback order, activation, agent collision, exact-pane launch, or cleanup behavior | Update `references/runtime-herdr.md`, `references/parallel-agents.md`, compatibility docs, and runtime/lifecycle tests. Keep the boundary clear: `dev start` prepares a checkout/runtime surface; it does not launch an agent. |
166	| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |
167	| Config fields/defaults or structured output | Update generated command help where applicable, authored reference pages and both locales, examples, and compatibility tests. |
168	| Quick-note storage, identity, search, structured output, or TUI behavior | Update README, embedded help, `SKILL.md`, `references/notes.md`, and paired English/zh-TW mental-model, workflow, TUI, commands/config, compatibility, and freshness pages. |
169	| Any user-visible feature or fix | Update `CHANGELOG.md`; update README/help/MkDocs/skill wherever they make the affected claim. |
170	
171	`make skill-check` proves only that generated command syntax matches the Cobra tree. It cannot detect drift in lifecycle semantics, JSON schemas, safety claims, examples, README, embedded help, or authored skill references; review those manually. Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.
172	
173	English and zh-TW MkDocs pages are maintained as a pair. Run the strict documentation checks above after changing either locale, navigation, snippets, or freshness metadata.
174	
175	## Hygiene and skill batch operations
176	
177	`internal/hygiene` owns per-repository setup plans and batch ledgers. REPOS and
178	`hygiene manage` are adapters; JSON batch management previews only. Keep legacy
179	artifact finalizers until their independent lifecycle is replaced. Cached machine
180	privacy imports use only bounded local cache readers and revalidate their source.
181	`internal/agentskill` owns selected-removal policy: exact native names/agent scopes
182	or bundled manifests, source/ownership/dependency proof and postconditions under
183	the provider lease. Never infer complete Windows validation from an advisory
184	step's success conclusion; inspect logs and require the dedicated native gates.
185	
186	## Agent history policy
187	
188	`dev help ai-artifacts` separates source retention, archive location, protection
189	and distribution. New configuration is opt-in. Sources are SpecStory Markdown or
190	explicit files; provider IDs name the originating agent. Do not infer writer exit
191	from byte stability or close agents to finalize evidence. Archive mode verifies
192	ignored bytes before cleanup; existing tracked intents retain their original lane.
193	`git-filter-repo` only operates on new verified copies. Ordinary migration never
194	rewrites source refs or published tags, and raw backups are not secret audits.

```text
150	func RenderManaged(definition ManagedDefinition) ([]byte, error) {

166		writeConfigDirective(&body, "IdentityFile", definition.IdentityFile)

169			if *definition.IdentitiesOnly {

171			}

173		}

175	}

177	func writeConfigDirective(body *strings.Builder, name, value string) {
178		if value == "" {
179			return
180		}
181		body.WriteString("    ")
182		body.WriteString(name)
183		body.WriteByte(' ')
184		body.WriteString(quoteConfigValue(value))
185		body.WriteByte('\n')

188	func quoteConfigValue(value string) string {
189		safe := value != ""
190		for _, r := range value {
191			if unicode.IsSpace(r) || unicode.IsControl(r) || strings.ContainsRune("#\"'\\", r) {
192				safe = false
193				break
194			}
195		}
196		if safe {
197			return value
198		}
199		value = strings.ReplaceAll(value, `\`, `\\`)
200		value = strings.ReplaceAll(value, `"`, `\"`)
201		return `"` + value + `"`
202	}

204	// ParseManaged accepts only canonical v1 content. A valid-looking block with
205	// comments, reordered directives, duplicates, or unknown text is manual drift.
206	func ParseManaged(data []byte) (ManagedDefinition, error) {
207		if bytes.ContainsRune(data, 0) || bytes.HasPrefix(data, []byte{0xef, 0xbb, 0xbf}) {
208			return ManagedDefinition{}, fmt.Errorf("managed file has a BOM or NUL: %w", ErrNotManaged)
209		}
210		lines := strings.Split(string(data), "\n")
211		if len(lines) < 3 || lines[0] != ManagedHeader || lines[len(lines)-1] != "" {
212			return ManagedDefinition{}, fmt.Errorf("managed file has no canonical v1 header/ending: %w", ErrNotManaged)
213		}
214		hostDirective, hostArguments, empty, err := parseConfigLine(lines[1])
215		if err != nil || empty || !strings.EqualFold(hostDirective, "Host") || len(hostArguments) != 1 {
216			return ManagedDefinition{}, fmt.Errorf("managed file must contain exactly one Host alias: %w", ErrNotManaged)
217		}
218		definition := ManagedDefinition{Alias: hostArguments[0]}
219		seen := make(map[string]bool)
220		for index, line := range lines[2 : len(lines)-1] {
221			directive, arguments, empty, err := parseConfigLine(line)
222			if err != nil || empty || len(arguments) != 1 {
223				return ManagedDefinition{}, fmt.Errorf("managed line %d is malformed: %w", index+3, ErrNotManaged)
224			}
225			key := strings.ToLower(directive)
226			if seen[key] {
227				return ManagedDefinition{}, fmt.Errorf("managed directive %s is duplicated: %w", directive, ErrNotManaged)
228			}
229			seen[key] = true
230			value := arguments[0]
231			switch key {
232			case "hostname":
233				definition.HostName = value
234			case "user":
235				definition.User = value
236			case "port":
237				port, parseErr := strconv.Atoi(value)
238				if parseErr != nil {
239					return ManagedDefinition{}, fmt.Errorf("managed Port is invalid: %w", ErrNotManaged)
240				}
241				definition.Port = port
242			case "proxyjump":
243				definition.ProxyJump = value
244			case "identityfile":
245				definition.IdentityFile = value
246			case "identitiesonly":
247				enabled := false
248				switch strings.ToLower(value) {
249				case "yes":
250					enabled = true
251				case "no":
252				default:
253					return ManagedDefinition{}, fmt.Errorf("managed IdentitiesOnly is invalid: %w", ErrNotManaged)
254				}
255				definition.IdentitiesOnly = &enabled
256			default:
257				return ManagedDefinition{}, fmt.Errorf("managed directive %s is not allowlisted: %w", directive, ErrNotManaged)
258			}
259		}
260		canonical, err := RenderManaged(definition)
261		if err != nil {
262			return ManagedDefinition{}, fmt.Errorf("validate managed file: %w", ErrNotManaged)
263		}
264		if !bytes.Equal(canonical, data) {
265			return ManagedDefinition{}, fmt.Errorf("managed file differs from canonical v1 rendering: %w", ErrNotManaged)
266		}
267		return definition, nil
268	}
```

```text
19	func (s *Service) resolveSSHKeyPath(value string) (string, error) {
20		if value == "" || strings.IndexByte(value, 0) >= 0 {
21			return "", fmt.Errorf("SSH key path is empty or contains NUL: %w", ErrUnsafePath)
22		}
23		resolved := value
24		switch {
25		case value == "~":
26			resolved = s.paths.Home
27		case strings.HasPrefix(value, "~/") || strings.HasPrefix(value, `~\`):
28			resolved = filepath.Join(s.paths.Home, filepath.FromSlash(value[2:]))
29		case value == "%d":
30			resolved = s.paths.Home
31		case strings.HasPrefix(value, "%d/") || strings.HasPrefix(value, `%d\`):
32			resolved = filepath.Join(s.paths.Home, filepath.FromSlash(value[3:]))
33		case value == "${HOME}":
34			resolved = s.paths.Home
35		case strings.HasPrefix(value, "${HOME}/") || strings.HasPrefix(value, `${HOME}\`):
36			resolved = filepath.Join(s.paths.Home, filepath.FromSlash(value[len("${HOME}/"):]))
37		case strings.HasPrefix(value, "~") || strings.ContainsAny(value, "%$"):
38			return "", fmt.Errorf("SSH key path uses unsupported expansion: %w", ErrUnsafePath)
39		}
40		if !filepath.IsAbs(resolved) {
41			absolute, err := filepath.Abs(resolved)
42			if err != nil {
43				return "", err
44			}
45			resolved = absolute
46		}
47		resolved = filepath.Clean(resolved)
48		if !s.pathWithinSSH(resolved) {
49			return "", fmt.Errorf("SSH key path is outside %s: %w", s.paths.SSHDir, ErrUnsafePath)
50		}
51		return resolved, nil
52	}

55		path = filepath.Clean(path)

58			return false
59		}
60		return relative != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(relative, ".."+string(filepath.Separator))
61	}

64		if !s.pathWithinSSH(path) {
65			return fmt.Errorf("path is outside the user SSH tree: %w", ErrUnsafePath)
66		}
67		if err := validateHomeDirectory(s.paths.Home); err != nil {
```

```text
1162	// ApplyKey consumes a source-bound plan. Native ssh-keygen receives no
1163	// passphrase in argv or environment except the explicit empty -N value required
1164	// by a noninteractive NoPassphrase generation request.
1165	func (s *Service) ApplyKey(ctx context.Context, plan KeyPlan) (KeyResult, error) {
1166		if ctx == nil {
1167			ctx = context.Background()
1168		}
1169		if plan.Action == ActionBlocked || plan.state == nil {
1170			return KeyResult{Action: plan.Action, Operation: plan.Operation}, ErrBlocked
1171		}
1172		state := plan.state
1173		if state.serviceID != s.id || !equalKeyPlans(plan, state.public) {
1174			return KeyResult{}, errors.New("key plan was not produced by this service or its public fields were modified")
1175		}
1176		switch plan.Operation {
1177		case KeyUse:
1178			if state.material == nil {
1179				return KeyResult{}, errors.New("selected key plan has no material state")
1180			}
1181			verification, err := s.verifyKeyPair(ctx, state.material, state.request.Interactive)
1182			if err != nil {
1183				return KeyResult{}, err
1184			}
1185			candidate := s.bindVerifiedKeyMaterial(state.material.safe, state.material.publicLine, verification)
1186			if state.material.agent != nil {
1187				copy := *state.material.agent
1188				candidate.state.agent = &copy
1189			}
1190			return KeyResult{Action: ActionNoop, Operation: KeyUse, Candidate: candidate}, nil
1191		case KeyDerive:
1192			return s.applyDerivedKey(ctx, plan)
1193		case KeyGenerate:
1194			return s.applyGeneratedKey(ctx, plan)
1195		default:
1196			return KeyResult{}, fmt.Errorf("unsupported key plan operation %q", plan.Operation)
1197		}
1198	}

1200	// RevalidateKeySelection checks a reviewed selection before any configuration
1201	// effect. It does not decrypt, derive, generate, write, or repair key material.
1202	// Agent selections query only their captured agent's public inventory.
1203	func (s *Service) RevalidateKeySelection(ctx context.Context, plan KeyPlan) error {
1204		if ctx == nil {
1205			ctx = context.Background()
1206		}
1207		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
1208			return err
1209		}
1210		if plan.Action == ActionBlocked || plan.state == nil {
1211			return ErrBlocked
1212		}
1213		state := plan.state
1214		if state.serviceID != s.id || !equalKeyPlans(plan, state.public) {
1215			return errors.New("key plan was not produced by this service or its public fields were modified")
1216		}
1217		switch plan.Operation {
1218		case KeyUse:
1219			if state.material == nil {
1220				return errors.New("selected key plan has no material state")
1221			}
1222			return s.revalidateSelectedKeySources(ctx, state.material)
1223		case KeyDerive:
1224			if err := s.revalidateSelectedKeyIdentity(state.identity); err != nil {
1225				return err
1226			}
1227			current, err := s.inspectPublicDestination(plan.PublicPath)
1228			if err != nil {
1229				return err
1230			}
1231			if current.exists != state.expectedPublic.exists {
1232				return ErrKeyCollision
1233			}
1234			return nil
1235		case KeyGenerate:
1236			parent := filepath.Dir(plan.IdentityFile)
1237			if err := s.validateKeyParent(parent); err != nil {
1238				_, statErr := os.Lstat(parent)
1239				if !samePath(parent, s.paths.SSHDir) || !errors.Is(statErr, fs.ErrNotExist) {
1240					return err
1241				}
1242				if err := validateHomeDirectory(s.paths.Home); err != nil {
1243					return err
1244				}
1245			}
1246			for _, path := range []string{plan.IdentityFile, plan.PublicPath} {
1247				if _, err := os.Lstat(path); err == nil {
1248					return ErrKeyCollision
1249				} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
1250					return err
1251				}
1252			}
1253			return nil
1254		default:
1255			return errors.New("unsupported key selection operation")
1256		}
1257	}
```

```text
485	func appendFreshSSHOptions(args []string, batch bool) []string {
486		args = append(args,
487			"-S", "none",
488			"-o", "ConnectTimeout="+sshConnectTimeout,
489			"-o", "ServerAliveInterval="+sshServerAliveInterval,
490			"-o", "ServerAliveCountMax="+sshServerAliveCountMax,
491		)
492		if batch {

494		}

498	func (s *Service) runSSHProof(ctx context.Context, hop routeHopState, selector keySelector, exact bool) (bool, error) {
499		if !exact {
500			result, err := s.runHopSSH(ctx, hop, true, "exit 0", nil, false, "ssh authentication proof")
501			if err != nil {
502				return false, err
503			}
504			return result.ExitCode == 0, nil
505		}
506		if selector.identity == "" {
507			return false, errors.New("exact SSH proof requires an identity selector")
508		}
509		if selector.agent != nil {
510			value := firstEffectiveValue(hop.effective, "identityagent")
511			configured, enabled, err := s.resolveIdentityAgent(value)
512			if err != nil || !enabled || configured != "" && configured != selector.agent.socket {
513				return false, errors.Join(ErrUnprovenAuthentication, ErrAgentPolicyMismatch)
514			}
515			if err := s.revalidateAgentKey(ctx, selector.agent, selector.fingerprint); err != nil {
516				return false, err
517			}
518		}
519		configPath, destination, cleanup, err := s.prepareExactProofConfig(hop, selector)
520		if err != nil {
521			return false, err
522		}
523		defer cleanup()
524		log, err := createStagedFile(s.paths.SSHDir, nil, nil)
525		if err != nil {
526			return false, fmt.Errorf("prepare private authentication proof: %w", err)
527		}
528		defer log.discard()
529		logPath := filepath.Join(log.dir, log.name)
530		// -E confines the client authentication evidence to this process. Unlike
531		// -v, LogLevel does not propagate verbosity into implicit ProxyJump clients.
532		args := appendFreshSSHOptions([]string{"-F", configPath, "-E", logPath, "-o", "LogLevel=DEBUG1"}, true)
533		args = append(args, destination, "exit 0")
534		// A captured socket is scoped to the target stanza. ProxyJump children must
535		// retain the ambient agent selected by their own ordinary configuration.
536		result, err := s.runner.Run(ctx, RunRequest{
537			Name: "ssh", Args: args, Env: []string{"LC_ALL=C"}, Display: "ssh selected-key-only authentication proof",
538		})
539		if err != nil {
540			return false, err
541		}
542		snapshot, err := readSecureFileAt(log.root, log.name, logPath, false)
543		if err != nil || !snapshot.exists || !os.SameFile(log.snapshot.info, snapshot.info) {
544			return false, ErrUnprovenAuthentication
545		}
546		return selectedKeyAuthentication(snapshot.data, result.ExitCode)
547	}

549	func (s *Service) prepareExactProofConfig(hop routeHopState, selector keySelector) (string, string, func(), error) {
550		route := append([]proofRouteHop(nil), hop.proofRoute...)
551		if len(route) == 0 {
552			hostName := hop.safe.HostName
553			if hostName == "" {
554				hostName = hop.destination
555			}
556			route = []proofRouteHop{{
557				alias: hop.destination, reference: hop.safe.Reference, hostName: hostName,
558				user: hop.safe.User, port: hop.safe.Port, effective: cloneEffective(hop.effective),
559			}}
560		}
561		content, destination, err := renderExactProofConfig(route, selector)
562		if err != nil {
563			return "", "", func() {}, err
564		}
565		staged, err := createStagedFile(s.paths.SSHDir, content, nil)
566		if err != nil {
567			return "", "", func() {}, err
568		}
569		return filepath.Join(staged.dir, staged.name), destination, func() { _ = staged.discard() }, nil
570	}

572	func renderExactProofConfig(route []proofRouteHop, selector keySelector) ([]byte, string, error) {
573		return renderSelectedConnectionConfig(route, selector, false)
574	}

576	func renderSelectedConnectionConfig(route []proofRouteHop, selector keySelector, interactive bool) ([]byte, string, error) {
577		if len(route) == 0 || selector.identity == "" {
578			return nil, "", errors.New("exact SSH proof has no route or identity")
579		}
580		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(route))
581		counts := make(map[string]int, len(route))
582		for index, hop := range route {
583			if err := validateRouteLookupAlias(hop.alias); err != nil {
584				return nil, "", err
585			}
586			key := foldAlias(hop.alias)
587			seen[key] = struct{}{}
588			counts[key]++
589			if index < len(route)-1 {
590				reference := hop.reference
591				if reference == "" {
592					reference = hop.alias
593				}
594				spec, err := parseJumpSpec(reference)
595				if err != nil || !equalAlias(spec.host, hop.alias) {
596					return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("exact SSH proof has an ambiguous ProxyJump reference %q for %q: %w", reference, hop.alias, ErrUnsupportedRoute)
597				}
598			}
599		}
600		destination := "dev-cli-exact-selected-key"
601		for suffix := 2; ; suffix++ {
602			if _, exists := seen[foldAlias(destination)]; !exists {
603				break
604			}
605			destination = "dev-cli-exact-selected-key-" + strconv.Itoa(suffix)
606		}
607	
608		var body strings.Builder
609		body.WriteString(exactProofConfigPreamble)
610		configReferences := make([]string, len(route))
611		for index, hop := range route {
612			hostName := hop.hostName
613			if hostName == "" {
614				hostName = hop.alias
615			}
616			if !validUTF8NoControl(hostName) || !validUTF8NoControl(hop.user) || hop.port < 0 || hop.port > 65535 {
617				return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("exact SSH proof endpoint %q is unsafe: %w", hop.alias, ErrUnsupportedRoute)
618			}
619			configAlias := hop.alias
620			configReference := hop.reference
621			if configReference == "" {
622				configReference = hop.alias
623			}
624			if index == len(route)-1 {
625				configAlias = destination
626			} else if counts[foldAlias(hop.alias)] > 1 {
627				configAlias = "dev-cli-route-hop-" + strconv.Itoa(index+1)
628				for suffix := 2; ; suffix++ {
629					if _, exists := seen[foldAlias(configAlias)]; !exists {
630						break
631					}
632					configAlias = "dev-cli-route-hop-" + strconv.Itoa(index+1) + "-" + strconv.Itoa(suffix)
633				}
634				seen[foldAlias(configAlias)] = struct{}{}
635				configReference = configAlias
636			}
637			configReferences[index] = configReference
638			body.WriteString("Host ")
639			body.WriteString(quoteConfigValue(configAlias))
640			body.WriteByte('\n')
641			writeConfigDirective(&body, "HostName", hostName)
642			writeConfigDirective(&body, "User", hop.user)
643			if hop.port != 0 {
644				writeConfigDirective(&body, "Port", strconv.Itoa(hop.port))
645			}
646			writeConfigDirective(&body, "ConnectTimeout", sshConnectTimeout)
647			writeConfigDirective(&body, "ServerAliveInterval", sshServerAliveInterval)
648			writeConfigDirective(&body, "ServerAliveCountMax", sshServerAliveCountMax)
649			batch := "yes"
650			if interactive {
651				batch = "no"
652			}
653			writeConfigDirective(&body, "BatchMode", batch)
654			writeConfigDirective(&body, "ControlMaster", "no")
655			writeConfigDirective(&body, "ControlPath", "none")
656			writeConfigDirective(&body, "ControlPersist", "no")
657			if err := writeExactHostKeyPolicy(&body, hop.effective, configAlias != hop.alias); err != nil {
658				return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("preserve host-key policy for %q: %w", hop.alias, err)
659			}
660			if index == len(route)-1 {
661				if index > 0 {
662					writeConfigDirective(&body, "ProxyJump", strings.Join(configReferences[:index], ","))
663				}
664				if err := writeSelectedAuthentication(&body, hop.effective, selector, interactive); err != nil {
665					return nil, "", err
666				}
667			} else if err := writeOrdinaryProxyAuthentication(&body, hop.effective); err != nil {
668				return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("preserve proxy authentication for %q: %w", hop.alias, err)
669			}
670		}
671		return []byte(body.String()), destination, nil
672	}

674	func writeExactHostKeyPolicy(body *strings.Builder, effective EffectiveConfig, syntheticEndpoint bool) error {
675		strict := firstEffectiveValue(effective, "stricthostkeychecking")
676		if strict == "" {
677			strict = "yes"
678		}
679		writeConfigDirective(body, "StrictHostKeyChecking", strict)
680		for _, option := range []struct {
681			key       string
682			directive string
683		}{
684			{key: "addressfamily", directive: "AddressFamily"},
685			{key: "ciphers", directive: "Ciphers"},
686			{key: "macs", directive: "MACs"},
687			{key: "kexalgorithms", directive: "KexAlgorithms"},
688			{key: "checkhostip", directive: "CheckHostIP"},
689			{key: "hashknownhosts", directive: "HashKnownHosts"},
690			{key: "hostkeyalias", directive: "HostKeyAlias"},
691			{key: "verifyhostkeydns", directive: "VerifyHostKeyDNS"},
692			{key: "updatehostkeys", directive: "UpdateHostKeys"},
693			{key: "nohostauthenticationforlocalhost", directive: "NoHostAuthenticationForLocalhost"},
694			{key: "revokedhostkeys", directive: "RevokedHostKeys"},
695			{key: "hostkeyalgorithms", directive: "HostKeyAlgorithms"},
696			{key: "casignaturealgorithms", directive: "CASignatureAlgorithms"},
697			{key: "requiredrsasize", directive: "RequiredRSASize"},
698		} {
699			if value := firstEffectiveValue(effective, option.key); value != "" {
700				if !validUTF8NoControl(value) || syntheticEndpoint && option.key == "hostkeyalias" && strings.Contains(value, "%") {
701					return ErrUnsupportedRoute
702				}
703				writeConfigDirective(body, option.directive, value)
704			}
705		}
706		if command := firstEffectiveValue(effective, "knownhostscommand"); command != "" && !strings.EqualFold(command, "none") {
707			return fmt.Errorf("KnownHostsCommand cannot be replayed safely: %w", ErrUnsupportedRoute)
708		}
709		for _, option := range []struct {
710			key       string
711			directive string
712		}{
713			{key: "globalknownhostsfile", directive: "GlobalKnownHostsFile"},
714			{key: "userknownhostsfile", directive: "UserKnownHostsFile"},
715		} {
716			value := firstEffectiveValue(effective, option.key)
717			if value == "" {
718				value = "none"
719			}
720			paths, err := splitEvaluatedKnownHosts(value)
721			if err != nil {
722				return err
723			}
724			body.WriteString("    ")
725			body.WriteString(option.directive)
726			for _, path := range paths {
727				body.WriteByte(' ')
728				body.WriteString(quoteConfigValue(path))
729			}
730			body.WriteByte('\n')
731		}
732		return nil
733	}
734	
735	func splitEvaluatedKnownHosts(value string) ([]string, error) {
736		paths := strings.Fields(value)
737		if len(paths) == 0 {
738			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty known-hosts path list: %w", ErrUnsupportedRoute)
739		}
740		for _, path := range paths {
741			if strings.EqualFold(path, "none") {
742				if len(paths) != 1 {
743					return nil, fmt.Errorf("mixed none known-hosts path list: %w", ErrUnsupportedRoute)
744				}
745				continue
746			}
747			windowsProgramData := runtime.GOOS == "windows" && strings.HasPrefix(
748				strings.ToUpper(strings.ReplaceAll(path, `\`, "/")), "__PROGRAMDATA__/",
749			)
750			if !filepath.IsAbs(path) && !windowsProgramData || strings.ContainsAny(path, "\r\n\x00") {
751				return nil, fmt.Errorf("relative or whitespace-containing known-hosts paths cannot be copied safely: %w", ErrUnsupportedRoute)
752			}
753		}
754		return paths, nil
755	}
```

```text
const (
// VerifyManagedEffective compares a managed definition with parsed ssh -G
// output. Error text names mismatched fields without echoing configuration
// values that may contain command-like user input.
func VerifyManagedEffective(definition ManagedDefinition, effective EffectiveConfig) error {
	if err := ValidateManagedDefinition(definition); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	var mismatches []string
	if !equalAlias(definition.Alias, effective.Alias) {
		mismatches = append(mismatches, "Alias")
	}
	if definition.HostName != effective.HostName {
		mismatches = append(mismatches, "HostName")
	}
	if definition.User != "" && definition.User != effective.User {
		mismatches = append(mismatches, "User")
	}
	if definition.Port != 0 && definition.Port != effective.Port {
		mismatches = append(mismatches, "Port")
	}
	if definition.ProxyJump != "" && definition.ProxyJump != effective.ProxyJump {
		mismatches = append(mismatches, "ProxyJump")
	}
	if definition.IdentitiesOnly != nil && (effective.IdentitiesOnly == nil || *definition.IdentitiesOnly != *effective.IdentitiesOnly) {
		mismatches = append(mismatches, "IdentitiesOnly")
	}
	if definition.IdentityFile != "" && !containsOrderedValues(effective.IdentityFiles, []string{definition.IdentityFile}) {
		mismatches = append(mismatches, "IdentityFile")
	}
	if len(mismatches) > 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("managed SSH config does not control effective fields: %s", strings.Join(mismatches, ", "))
	}
	return nil
}
```

```text
func (s *Service) resolveIdentityAgent(value string) (path string, enabled bool, err error) {
	value = strings.TrimSpace(value)
	switch {
	case value == "", strings.EqualFold(value, "SSH_AUTH_SOCK"):
		return "", true, nil
	case strings.EqualFold(value, "none"):
		return "", false, nil
	}
	resolved := value
	switch {
	case strings.HasPrefix(value, "~/") || strings.HasPrefix(value, `~\\`):
		resolved = filepath.Join(s.paths.Home, filepath.FromSlash(value[2:]))
	case strings.HasPrefix(value, "%d/") || strings.HasPrefix(value, `%d\\`):
		resolved = filepath.Join(s.paths.Home, filepath.FromSlash(value[3:]))
	case strings.HasPrefix(value, "${HOME}/") || strings.HasPrefix(value, `${HOME}\\`):
		resolved = filepath.Join(s.paths.Home, filepath.FromSlash(value[len("${HOME}/"):]))
	case strings.HasPrefix(value, "~") || strings.ContainsAny(value, "%$"):
		return "", false, ErrUnsupportedRoute
	}
	if !filepath.IsAbs(resolved) || !validUTF8NoControl(resolved) {
		return "", false, ErrUnsafePath
	}
	return filepath.Clean(resolved), true, nil
}

func planSSHSetupKey(ctx context.Context, app *App, service *sshhost.Service, options sshSetupOptions, interactiveMode bool) (sshhost.KeyPlan, error) {
	if options.keyCandidate != nil && (options.key != "" || options.generateKey) {
		return sshhost.KeyPlan{}, errors.New("choose one existing key or key generation")
	}
	request := sshhost.KeyRequest{
		Interactive:  interactiveMode && !options.noPassphrase,
		AllowDerive:  options.yes,
		NoPassphrase: options.noPassphrase,
	}
	if options.generateKey {
		request.Operation = sshhost.KeyGenerate
		request.DestinationIdentity = options.keyPath
		request.Comment = options.comment
	} else {
		request.Operation = sshhost.KeyUse
		if options.keyCandidate != nil {
			request.Candidate = *options.keyCandidate
		} else {
			request.Path = options.key
		}
	}
	plan, err := service.PlanKey(ctx, request)
	if err != nil {
		return plan, err
	}
	if plan.Action == sshhost.ActionBlocked && hasSSHDiagnostic(plan.Diagnostics, "derive_confirmation_required") && interactiveMode && !options.dryRun {
		confirmed, promptErr := newPrompter(app).confirm("Derive and save the missing public key companion?", false)
		if promptErr != nil {
			return plan, promptErr
		}
		if !confirmed {
			return plan, errPromptCanceled
		}
		request.AllowDerive = true
		return service.PlanKey(ctx, request)
	}
	return plan, nil
}
```

```text
// openSSHKeyForm installs a key for an existing profile without editable
// connection fields, starting with the key picker.
func (m Model) openSSHKeyForm(profile sshflow.ConnectionProfile) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
	m.pauseSSHBackground()
	p := profile
	request := sshflow.OnboardRequest{Profile: &p, Alias: p.Alias, HostName: p.HostName, User: p.User, Port: p.Port, Auth: "key", RemoteOS: "posix"}
	d := sshDialog{kind: "onboard", title: fmt.Sprintf("Install SSH key for %s (%s)", p.Alias, sshProfileEndpoint(p)), onboarding: request}
	d.addField("key", "Key", "")
	d.addField("os", "Remote OS", request.RemoteOS)
	d.addField("fleet", "Fleet", "no")
	d.addField("herdr", "Herdr", "no")
	m.sshUI.dialog = d
	if m.actions.SSH.ListKeys == nil {
		return m, m.focusSSHField(0)
	}
	return m.openSSHKeyPicker()
}

func (m Model) openSSHKeyPicker() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
	parent := m.sshUI.dialog
	alias := parent.value("alias")
	if parent.onboarding.Profile != nil {
		alias = parent.onboarding.Profile.Alias
	}
	if alias == "" {
		alias = "host"
	}
	m.sshUI.generation++
	generation := m.sshUI.generation
	m.sshUI.dialog = sshDialog{kind: "keys-loading", title: "Choose SSH key for " + alias, body: "Reading local SSH keys…", parent: &parent}
	return m, func() tea.Msg {
		keys, err := m.actions.SSH.ListKeys(m.baseContext(), alias)
		return sshEventMsg{generation: generation, kind: "keys", keys: keys, err: err}
	}
}

func (m Model) chooseSSHKey(index int) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
	d := m.sshUI.dialog
	if d.parent == nil {
		return m, nil
	}
	parent := *d.parent
	if index < len(d.keys) {
		choice := d.keys[index]
		parent.applyKeyChoice(choice.Path, choice.Generate)
		m.sshUI.dialog = parent
		return m, m.focusSSHField(parent.index)
	}
	form := sshDialog{kind: "keypath", title: d.title, parent: &parent}
	path := ""
	if !parent.onboarding.GenerateKey {
		path = parent.onboarding.KeyPath
	}
	form.addField("path", "Key path", path)
	m.sshUI.dialog = form
	return m, m.focusSSHField(0)
}

func (m Model) finishSSHKeyPath() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
	d := m.sshUI.dialog
	if d.parent == nil {
		return m, nil
	}
	path := strings.TrimSpace(d.value("path"))
	if path == "" {
		m.sshUI.dialog.err = errors.New("Enter a key path, or Esc to return to the form")
		return m, nil
	}
	parent := *d.parent
	parent.applyKeyChoice(path, false)
	m.sshUI.dialog = parent
	return m, m.focusSSHField(parent.index)
}

	Targets []OnboardTarget
```

```text
# SSH key provider helpers

Status: deferred; current SSH route, registration and password-save work does not authorize vault migration or hardware provisioning.

Research updated: 2026-09-12.

The existing chezmoi `ssh-to-bitwarden` helper already imports SSH key items and
its shell configuration selects Bitwarden's agent. Reuse a native handoff before
building another vault writer. A future implementation must show key fingerprints
and provider state without logging key bytes, vault unlock data or credentials.
Audit the existing helper's name-based duplicate detection and Secure Note fallback
before treating it as a dev-supported credential transfer protocol.

YubiKey is a separate design: FIDO2-generated hardware credentials, PIV imports
and OpenPGP agent integration have different lifecycle and recovery semantics.
Do not present them as equivalent destinations for uploading an existing key.
Public key installation can reuse sshhost once a provider exposes a supported
public identity and ordinary OpenSSH authentication works.

Suggested first increment: agent/socket diagnostics, public fingerprint listing,
provider-specific prerequisites and an explicit native-tool handoff. Vault import,
hardware provisioning and credential revocation need their own reviewable plans.
No new provider execution belongs in passive SSH or fleet inventory.

Sources: [Bitwarden SSH agent](https://bitwarden.com/help/ssh-agent/),
[Yubico SSH approaches](https://developers.yubico.com/SSH/).

Herdr integration also has an upstream opportunity: metadata-only registration
and structured dry-run/apply outcomes would avoid native preparation during add.
The implemented adapter uses the current native CLI; it does not edit Herdr's
private endpoint catalog or silently answer server-replacement approvals.


## Distinct future workflows

The user requested these as later helpers, not additions to the current SSH
password-save feature. Default to explicit native-tool handoff and metadata
preview. An approved transfer may process private material in memory, but normal
setup/discovery must retain its no-private-key-transfer contract. Keep names,
public fingerprints, destination identity and verification results reviewable;
never log key bytes, passphrases, vault sessions or exported account passwords.

### Existing SSH private key to Bitwarden

Bitwarden accepts OpenSSH and PKCS#8 private-key import; its documented agent
supports Ed25519 and RSA SHA-256/SHA-512, and PuTTY input is unsupported. The SDK
can decrypt supported encrypted input with an explicit passphrase and normalize
it to OpenSSH; vault representation is encrypted. A future helper must detect
format/algorithm support rather than promise arbitrary PEM conversion.

The CLI documents SSH item type 5, but its current template switch has no SSH-key
case. Do not assume `bw get template item.sshkey` exists, or fall back silently to
Secure Note after template failure. Audit the existing chezmoi helper, pin the
supported CLI schema, use stdin rather than secret argv/clipboard where possible,
and retain the exact returned item ID and public fingerprint. Duplicate names
are not identity. Verify provider agent signing before offering separate local
key-file cleanup; import never implies source deletion or remote revocation.

Sources: [Bitwarden About SSH](https://bitwarden.com/help/about-ssh/),
[SDK import](https://sdk-api-docs.bitwarden.com/bitwarden_wasm_internal/ssh/fn.import_ssh_key.html),
[CLI schema](https://bitwarden.com/help/cli/),
[CLI template source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitwarden/clients/main/apps/cli/src/commands/get.command.ts).

### YubiKey: generate versus import

FIDO2 SSH creates a new `ed25519-sk` or `ecdsa-sk` credential and a local handle;
it is not a route for uploading the same ordinary OpenSSH private key. PIV can
import supported asymmetric private keys into selected slots, while OpenPGP uses
its own existing-PGP-key import flow. Supported algorithms depend on firmware
and application. Occupied PIV slots can irrecoverably replace an existing key,
so device/firmware/slot inventory, explicit replacement scope and recovery need
their own reviewed plan. Do not label all three paths “move this SSH key”.

	checks := make([]check, 0, 5)
	for _, binary := range []struct {
		name    string
		purpose string
	}{
		{name: "ssh", purpose: "SSH host evaluation and login unavailable"},
		{name: "ssh-keygen", purpose: "SSH key generation and derivation unavailable"},

		if path, err := exec.LookPath(binary.name); err == nil {
			checks = append(checks, check{binary.name, checkOK, path})

			checks = append(checks, check{binary.name, checkWarn, "not found — " + binary.purpose})
```

```text
// RunRequest is an argv-only subprocess request. Display is a redacted label
// for diagnostics; runners must not reconstruct diagnostics from sensitive
// argv or stdin. Interactive attaches native stdin (when Stdin is empty) and
// output to the controller terminal so ssh/ssh-keygen can own hidden prompts.
// CaptureStdout is reserved for bounded machine-readable output from an
// otherwise interactive command, such as ssh-keygen -y.
type RunRequest struct {
	Name          string   `json:"-"`
	Args          []string `json:"-"`
	Dir           string   `json:"-"`
	Env           []string `json:"-"`
	UnsetEnv      []string `json:"-"`
	Stdin         []byte   `json:"-"`
	Display       string   `json:"display,omitempty"`
	Interactive   bool     `json:"interactive,omitempty"`
	CaptureStdout bool     `json:"-"`
	// StdoutLimit opts an internal protocol into a larger bounded response.
	// Zero keeps the ordinary 1 MiB limit; stderr always retains that limit.
	StdoutLimit int `json:"-"`
	// OnStarted is a local observation hook, invoked only after the OS started
	// the process. It does not indicate authentication or command success.
	OnStarted func(time.Time) `json:"-"`
}
```

---
description: Discover OpenSSH aliases, manage only dev-owned host fragments, bootstrap public-key access, and explicitly register verified hosts in dev fleet.
authority: project
status: stable
verified_on: 2026-09-13
---

# SSH host onboarding

`dev ssh` adds a conservative lifecycle around the OpenSSH configuration you already use. OpenSSH remains connection authority; dev provides static provenance, a small owned fragment namespace, public-key bootstrap, fresh authentication proofs, and an explicit bridge into [dev fleet](remote-fleet.md).

## Authority and ownership

| Surface | Authority / owner | What dev may do |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.ssh/config`, its foreign Includes, and foreign `Host`/`Match` blocks | user + OpenSSH | read statically; evaluate with plain `ssh -G`; explicit format/organize can transform selected user files |
| `Include ~/.ssh/dev.d/*.conf` in the root config | dev, after explicit `ssh init --apply` | install once before the first `Host`, `Match`, or earlier Include; never remove automatically |
| `~/.ssh/dev.d/<alias>.conf` | `dev ssh setup/remove` | create, reconcile, or remove only canonical v1 files with an allowlisted single `Host` block |
| local key files | user + native `ssh-keygen` | validate an explicit key, derive a confirmed missing `.pub`, or generate a no-replace Ed25519 pair; never copy private bytes |
| remote `authorized_keys` | remote OpenSSH account | append one bounded normalized public record idempotently; never remove or revoke it |
| primary `remotes.toml` | user via `dev fleet config` | read and merge; never rewrite during SSH setup |
| sibling `remotes.d/ssh-<alias>.toml` | `dev ssh setup/remove --fleet` | create only after a fresh ordinary login; remove only when explicitly requested |

A foreign alias remains usable for `list`, `show`, `probe`, key bootstrap, and fleet registration, but connection flags are rejected during `setup`. Dev will not compete with its existing definition. New dev-managed aliases use a portable lowercase exact-name grammar and one deterministic file containing `HostName`, optional `User`, `Port`, `ProxyJump`, `IdentityFile`, and `IdentitiesOnly`. Arbitrary directives and wildcard/`Match` blocks are not managed.

## Command map

| Command | Exact local flags | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| `dev ssh init` | `--apply`, `--yes`, `--json` | plan by default; only `--apply` may install the dedicated Include |
| `dev ssh list` | `--json`, `--format tsv`; explicit `--tailscale`, `--lan` | static by default; optional joined machine observations |
| `dev ssh show <alias>` | `--json` | static definitions plus effective values from plain `ssh -G <alias>` |
| `dev ssh setup <alias>` | connection, key, route, fleet, plan, confirmation, and JSON flags listed below | owned local config, public-key bootstrap, optional fleet registration |
| `dev ssh probe <alias>` | `--json` | one fresh ordinary BatchMode login with sharing disabled |
| `dev ssh remove <alias>` | `--fleet`, `--dry-run`, `--yes`, `--json` | remove only canonical dev-owned SSH/fleet fragments |

`dev doctor` also reports local `ssh`/`ssh-keygen` and optional `tailscale` capabilities, static Include reachability, managed namespace permissions/ACLs, and generated fleet-fragment health. It does not run `ssh -G`, contact a host, or repair anything.

## One-time initialization is report-before-apply

```bash
dev ssh init
dev ssh init --json
dev ssh init --apply
dev ssh init --apply --yes

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and releases use [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

## [0.2.37] - 2026-09-14

### Added

- `dev ssh setup <alias>` on a terminal without `--key` or `--generate-key` opens
  one key picker listing local keys, `+ Generate a new key` and a manual path; the
  setup wizard, fleet imports and per-hop keys use the same picker. The `dev ssh`
  menu adds "Set up or install an SSH key for a host". Scripts still pass a flag.
- The dashboard SSH view's Ctrl+O offers "set up this discovered target…" with a
  form prefilled from the selected LAN/Tailscale observation, and "set up / install
  an SSH key…" for configured profiles without editing their connection settings.
  The setup form's Key field opens a key picker, and choice fields show every option.

### Fixed

- Interactive prompts with fixed answers list their choices, such as
  `Remote OS for lab (posix/windows) [posix]`, instead of revealing them only after
  an invalid answer. The discovery wizard's Target OS answer is now validated.
- LAN discovery no longer hides blocked connections behind `ready` with zero
  candidates. Reports add `probes` outcome counts and a `no_reachable_endpoints`
  warning, and `dev ssh discover`, the `dev ssh` wizard and the dashboard explain
  that macOS may be denying Local Network access to the terminal app. The wizard
```

```text
func ParseEffective(alias string, output []byte) (EffectiveConfig, error) {
	config := EffectiveConfig{Alias: alias, Values: make(map[string][]string)}
	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(bytes.NewReader(output))
	scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 4096), 2<<20)
	for scanner.Scan() {
		line := strings.TrimSpace(scanner.Text())
		if line == "" {
			continue
		}
		separator := strings.IndexFunc(line, unicode.IsSpace)
		if separator < 1 {
			return EffectiveConfig{}, fmt.Errorf("parse ssh -G output: malformed line %q", line)
		}
		key := strings.ToLower(line[:separator])
		value := strings.TrimSpace(line[separator:])
		if value == "" {
			return EffectiveConfig{}, fmt.Errorf("parse ssh -G output: %s has no value", key)
		}
		config.Values[key] = append(config.Values[key], value)
	}
	if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
		return EffectiveConfig{}, fmt.Errorf("parse ssh -G output: %w", err)
	}
	config.HostName = firstEffectiveValue(config, "hostname")
	config.User = firstEffectiveValue(config, "user")
	config.ProxyJump = firstEffectiveValue(config, "proxyjump")
	config.IdentityFiles = append([]string(nil), config.Values["identityfile"]...)
	if value := firstEffectiveValue(config, "port"); value != "" {
		port, err := strconv.Atoi(value)
		if err != nil || port < 1 || port > 65535 {
			return EffectiveConfig{}, fmt.Errorf("parse ssh -G output: invalid port %q", value)
		}
		config.Port = port
	}
	if value := firstEffectiveValue(config, "identitiesonly"); value != "" {
		var enabled bool
		switch strings.ToLower(value) {
		case "yes", "true":
			enabled = true
		case "no", "false":
			enabled = false
		default:
			return EffectiveConfig{}, fmt.Errorf("parse ssh -G output: invalid identitiesonly %q", value)
		}
		config.IdentitiesOnly = &enabled
	}
	return config, nil
}
```

# Implementation plan: custom paths, agent providers, hardware keys, and vault-created keys

I checked every fact from the brief against the code and they hold. Three more findings change the design:

1. **Setup order already fits agent keys.** `internal/cli/ssh.go:969-1024` runs ApplyKey, then ApplyManaged, then `ResolveRoute` (fresh `ssh -G`), then Bootstrap. If the managed fragment writes `IdentityAgent <socket>`, the fresh config matches the selected socket. The `ErrAgentPolicyMismatch` check (bootstrap.go:510-514) then passes without being weakened.
2. **An agent key needs its own `.pub` file.** With `IdentitiesOnly yes`, OpenSSH offers an agent key only when an `IdentityFile` matches it. So we must publish a public-only file and point `IdentityFile` at it. `prepareKeySelector` already uses `PublicPath` as the identity for keys with no private file (bootstrap.go:463-468).
3. **Paths with spaces survive `ssh -G`.** `ParseEffective` keeps the whole rest of the line, so 1Password's `Group Containers` socket works. `quoteConfigValue` already quotes spaces. `golang.org/x/crypto` is already a direct dependency.

---

## P1: Custom key name, location and comment

**Commit:** `feat(ssh): choose generated key path and comment`

**`internal/sshhost/keys.go` (`planGeneratedKey`)**
- Turn today's plain errors into blocked-plan `Diagnostic`s with a `Path`, so the pickers can show them and loop:
  - `key_path_outside_ssh`, `key_path_unsupported_expansion`, `key_name_pub_suffix`
  - `key_parent_missing`, `key_parent_unsafe` (symlink, not a directory, or not mode 0700)
- Leave `resolveSSHKeyPath` unchanged, including the "must be under `~/.ssh`" rule.
- **Parent directories (needs your decision):**
  - *Recommended:* add `KeyPlan.CreateParent string` (JSON `create_parent`). It is set only when the missing parent is a *direct child* of `~/.ssh`. Apply creates it with the existing `ensurePrivateChild(SSHDir, name, false)`, and the plan shows it. This keeps the code comment at keys.go:1117 ("arbitrary nested key directories still require preparation") true for deeper paths, which stay blocked with a hint like `mkdir -m 700 ~/.ssh/a/b`.
  - *Alternative:* never create directories; only print the hint.
  - `RevalidateKeySelection` (1235-1253) must accept a still-missing `CreateParent` and reject one that has since appeared as a non-0700 or symlinked directory.

**`internal/cli/ssh_keys.go` (`chooseSSHKeyInteractive`)**
- After the "New key path" prompt, ask `Key comment (blank = ssh-keygen default)` and store it in `options.comment`.
- Add `normalizeKeyPromptPath(home, input)`. In prompts only, a bare name with no separator becomes `~/.ssh/<name>`. The `--key-path` flag keeps its current meaning.
- Picker descriptions should show `CreateParent` when it is set.

**Dashboard (TUI)**
- `internal/tui/ssh_view.go`: add `Comment string` to `SSHKeyChoice`.
- `internal/tui/ssh_key_setup.go`:
  - `chooseSSHKey`: a `Generate` choice opens a new `keygen` dialog with a `path` field (prefilled with the default) and a `comment` field.
  - New `finishSSHKeyGenerate` calls `applyKeyChoice(path, true)` and sets `onboarding.KeyComment`.
  - `finishSSHKeyPath` stays for existing keys (`Generate=false`).
- `internal/sshflow/onboard_ui.go`: add `KeyComment` to `OnboardRequest`.
- `internal/cli/ssh_tui_onboard.go` (`prepareSSHTUIOnboarding`): pass it through to `KeyRequest.Comment`.

**Tests**
- `keys_test.go`: a custom path in an existing 0700 subdirectory; missing direct child produces `CreateParent`; missing nested directory is blocked; a subdirectory that changes after planning is rejected; argv contains `-C`.
- `ssh_setup_key_picker_test.go`: the comment prompt and bare-name normalization.
- TUI model test for the keygen form.

**Docs:** `docs/guides/ssh-hosts.md` and zh-TW (key section), `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/ssh-hosts.md`, CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`. No flag changes, so `make skill-check` should show no drift.

---

## P2: Named agent providers (Bitwarden, 1Password, Secretive, custom)

**Commit:** `feat(ssh): select keys from named SSH agents`

**New `internal/sshhost/agent_providers.go`**
- `type AgentProviderID string`: `bitwarden`, `1password`, `secretive`, `custom`.
- `type AgentProviderObservation struct{ Provider AgentProviderID; Label, Socket string; SocketPresent, AppDetected bool }`.
- `func (s *Service) ObserveAgentProviders(goos string) []AgentProviderObservation`. It only runs `Lstat`: socket mode, owned by the current user, no symlink in the socket's parent directories. It never runs a command. Socket table by OS (from your research):

| Provider | Paths checked |
|---|---|
| Bitwarden | macOS App Store and .dmg, Linux, Snap, Flatpak |
| 1Password | both macOS paths, Linux `~/.1password/agent.sock` |
| Secretive | its macOS container socket |

- App detection is also stat-only: `/Applications/Bitwarden.app`, `~/Applications/…`, `/Applications/1Password.app`, `/Applications/Secretive.app`, Snap/Flatpak directories.
- **Windows:** `\\.\pipe\openssh-ssh-agent` is one pipe that any of these agents may own, so dev cannot tell which. Report it as `windows-openssh-pipe`, not as a named provider.

**`key_types.go`**
- `KeyCatalogRequest.Agents []AgentSocketRef` (`{Provider, Socket}`, JSON `agents`).
- `KeyCandidate.Agent *AgentSocketRef` (JSON `agent,omitempty`). The socket path is not secret.
- New `KeyPublishAgent KeyOperation = "publish_agent_public"`.
- `KeyRequest.PublicDestination string`.

**`keys.go`**
- `Catalog`: after the ambient agent (lines 589-624), run `readAgentKeys` once per request socket using the existing `keyAgentContext`.
- The catalog de-duplicates by fingerprint. If a key is in more than one agent, precedence is: the alias's explicit `IdentityAgent`, then request order, then `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`. Add a non-blocking `agent_key_duplicate` diagnostic.
- `planAgentPublication`: default destination `~/.ssh/dev_agent_<provider>_<alias>.pub`, using P1 path rules.
  - The file already holds the identical normalized line: `ActionNoop`.
  - A different file is there: `key_collision`.
- `applyAgentPublication`: first run `revalidateAgentKey`, then `createStagedFile` and `commitNoReplace`. The result candidate has `PublicPath` = `IdentityFile` = the `.pub` file, and keeps `state.agent`. Only public bytes are written, so the "no private-key transfer" rule still holds.

**Managed fragment compatibility (needs your decision; recommendation below)**
- Add `IdentityAgent` and `SecurityKeyProvider` (the second is used in P3) to `ManagedDefinition` (types.go:192).
- Add `ManagedHeaderV2 = "# dev-cli managed SSH host v2"`.
- `RenderManaged` writes the **v1 header, byte-identical to today, when both new fields are empty**. Existing files never show as drift.
- `ParseManaged` accepts v1 (new directives rejected) and v2 (new directives allowed). The `bytes.Equal` re-render check stays.
- `ValidateManagedDefinition`:
  - `IdentityAgent`: absolute, clean, valid UTF-8, no `%`, `$` or `~`.
  - `SecurityKeyProvider`: `internal` or an absolute path.
- `VerifyManagedEffective` (effective.go:81) compares both new fields after running each through `resolveIdentityAgent`.
- **Effect on older binaries (v0.2.37 and earlier):** they read a v2 file as `managed_drift` or `OwnershipConflict`. `ssh` itself works, but old `dev ssh setup/remove` is blocked with "no canonical v1 header". Documented rule: upgrade every controller that shares `~/.ssh` before selecting agent or hardware keys.
- *Alternative:* add the directives to v1. That fails with the less clear "not allowlisted" and cannot be told apart from a hand edit.

**CLI**
- `ssh.go` setup (842-861) and `ssh_onboard.go` (404, 934): when the plan's candidate has `Agent`, set `definition.IdentityAgent`, `IdentityFile` = the published `.pub`, and `IdentitiesOnly = yes`.
- **Foreign alias** (can't be written): block with `identity_agent_manual`. The message prints the exact three lines to add. The proof still requires a matching `IdentityAgent`, as today.
- **Dry run:** `PlanBootstrap` sees the old config. Annotate it "pending managed IdentityAgent" instead of reporting a mismatch.
- **New flags:**
  - `dev ssh setup --identity-agent bitwarden|1password|secretive|<abs path>`
  - `dev ssh key list --agent <same>` (repeatable)
- `chooseSSHKeyInteractive` asks for the catalog with the providers that are present. Labels look like `Bitwarden agent: <comment>`.
- A detected provider whose socket is missing becomes a disabled item such as "Bitwarden installed; SSH agent disabled (Settings → Enable SSH agent)".

**TUI**
- Add `Fingerprint`, `AgentProvider`, `AgentSocket` to `SSHKeyChoice`, and `KeyFingerprint`, `KeyAgentSocket` to `OnboardRequest`.
- `listSSHTUIKeys` keeps agent keys instead of dropping them.
- `prepareSSHTUIOnboarding` re-catalogs and requires the same fingerprint and socket, otherwise `ErrSourceChanged`.
- Relax the check at `ssh_tui_onboard.go:53` so a fingerprint can stand in for `KeyPath`.

**Doctor and install guidance**
- `doctor.go` gets `sshAgentProviderChecks`. It uses `ObserveAgentProviders` (stat only; key doctor's contract says default doctor never queries agents) and warns when the app is installed but the socket is absent. That is exactly this Mac's state.
- `tuiissue/install.go` `Tools`:
  - `bw` (Brew `bitwarden-cli`, WinGet `Bitwarden.CLI`)
  - `op` (guide link only; it's a cask)
  - `ykman` (Brew `ykman`, Apt `yubikey-manager`)
- New typed issue `agent_provider_disabled`.

**Config:** none. The fragment's `IdentityAgent` is the lasting choice and discovery is just a stat call. A later `[ssh.keys]` default could be considered only if you ask for it.

**Tests**

- v1 files stay byte-identical; v2 round-trips; v1 containing `IdentityAgent` is rejected.
- `VerifyManagedEffective` with a socket path containing spaces.
