// Package sshvault creates new SSH keys in explicitly selected vaults. It never
// imports an existing private key, writes private material to disk, or manages
// an agent. Planning is explicit provider execution, not passive discovery.
package sshvault

import (
	"errors"
	"sync"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/sshcredential"
)

type Provider string

const (
	Bitwarden   Provider = "bitwarden"
	OnePassword Provider = "1password"
	PersonalVault        = "personal"
)

var (
	ErrUnsafe             = errors.New("invalid SSH vault key request")
	ErrUnavailable        = errors.New("SSH vault provider unavailable or returned invalid metadata")
	ErrLocked             = errors.New("SSH vault provider is locked or not authenticated; unlock it using its native tools")
	ErrUnsupportedVersion = errors.New("SSH vault provider version is not supported")
	ErrExperimental       = errors.New("Bitwarden in-memory SSH key generation requires explicit experimental approval")
	ErrStale              = errors.New("SSH vault key plan or destination changed; review a new plan")
	ErrPlanUsed           = errors.New("SSH vault key creation was already attempted; do not retry without reconciling the vault")
	ErrUnknown            = errors.New("SSH vault mutation outcome or destination is unknown; inspect the vault before any new creation")
	ErrPublicKey          = errors.New("SSH vault item was created but its public key could not be verified; retain the item and reconcile it")
)

// Request selects a destination, not a saved password context. OnePassword
// requires an exact vault ID; AccountID may select an exact account or be empty
// to review the current account. Bitwarden currently supports only its personal
// vault and requires Experimental. AccountID, when set, is its exact user ID.
// No unlock secret or private key belongs in this API.
type Request struct {
	Provider     Provider `json:"provider"`
	Title        string   `json:"title"`
	AccountID    string   `json:"account_id,omitempty"`
	VaultID      string   `json:"vault_id,omitempty"`
	Experimental bool     `json:"experimental,omitempty"`
}

// Destination is the reviewed provider identity. It does not authorize provider
// login, vault creation, organization selection, or native agent configuration.
type Destination struct {
	Provider  Provider `json:"provider"`
	AccountID string   `json:"account_id"`
	ServerURL string   `json:"server_url"`
	UserID    string   `json:"user_id"`
	VaultID   string   `json:"vault_id"`
	VaultName string   `json:"vault_name,omitempty"`
}

type Plan struct {
	Destination  Destination `json:"destination"`
	Version      string      `json:"version"`
	Title        string      `json:"title"`
	Experimental bool        `json:"experimental,omitempty"`
	state        *planState
}

type planState struct {
	service   *Service
	request   Request
	dest      Destination
	version   string
	operation string
	attempted bool
}

// Receipt contains only public material. Destination is the reviewed destination,
// not a claim that an external CLI could not change account while it ran. Consult
// Result.BindingStatus before relying on that association. An item ID may be
// known even when PublicLine and Fingerprint could not yet be obtained.
type Receipt struct {
	Destination
	ItemID      string `json:"item_id"`
	PublicLine  string `json:"public_line,omitempty"`
	Fingerprint string `json:"fingerprint,omitempty"`
}

const (
	StatusNotStarted = "not_started"
	StatusCreated    = "created"
	StatusUnknown    = "unknown"
	BindingVerified  = "verified"
	BindingUnknown   = "unknown"
)

// Created means that a matching creation response was verified; it never means
// the selected SSH agent serves the key. ErrPublicKey and ErrUnknown can accompany
// a created result and its retained receipt. No automatic retry is permitted.
type Result struct {
	Status        string   `json:"status"`
	BindingStatus string   `json:"binding_status,omitempty"`
	Receipt       *Receipt `json:"receipt,omitempty"`
}

type Service struct {
	runner sshcredential.CommandRunner
	mu     sync.Mutex
}

func NewService(runner sshcredential.CommandRunner) *Service {
	if runner == nil {
		runner = sshcredential.NativeRunner{}
	}
	return &Service{runner: runner}
}

1	// Package platformfs supplies narrowly scoped native filesystem capabilities.
2	package platformfs
3	
4	import (
5		"path/filepath"
6		"regexp"
7		"runtime"
8	)
9	
10	// Anchor is a verified starting directory for a guarded path walk. Android
11	// apps can stat their system ancestors but cannot open them for directory reads.
12	// Verify rechecks the complete platform prefix; callers still guard every
13	// component below Path and revalidate their held directory/file identities.
14	type Anchor struct {
15		Path   string
16		verify func() error
17	}
18	
19	func (a Anchor) Verify() error {
20		if a.verify != nil {
21			return a.verify()
22		}
23		return nil
24	}
25	
26	func filesystemRoot(path string) Anchor {
27		return Anchor{Path: filepath.VolumeName(path) + string(filepath.Separator)}
28	}
29	
30	var appDataLabel = regexp.MustCompile(`^u:object_r:app_data_file:s0(:c[0-9]+(,c[0-9]+)*)?\x00?$`)
31	
32	// KernelLabel recognizes Android's inherited app-data label. It may be observed
33	// and compared, never restored with setxattr or omitted from identity checks.
34	func KernelLabel(name string, value []byte) bool {
35		return kernelLabel(runtime.GOOS, name, value)
36	}
37	
38	func kernelLabel(goos, name string, value []byte) bool {
39		return goos == "android" && name == "security.selinux" && len(value) <= 4096 && appDataLabel.Match(value)
40	}
41	
42	// InheritedFileFlags reports read-only flags supplied by Android's filesystem.
43	// FS_ENCRYPT_FL describes transparent file encryption; dev never sets/clears it.
44	func InheritedFileFlags() uint32 {
45		if runtime.GOOS == "android" {
46			return 0x00000800
47		}
48		return 0
49	}

package sshvault

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/rand"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"net/url"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"unicode"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/sshcredential"
)

const (
	maxOutput = 1 << 20
	// This is a schema pin for the experimental implementation, not a claim of
	// live-vault validation. Broaden it only after reviewing the provider schema.
	BitwardenSchemaVersion = "2026.3.0"
)

var (
	opIDPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z0-9]{26}$`)
	bwIDPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$`)
)

func validText(value string, maxBytes int) bool {
	if value == "" || len(value) > maxBytes || value != strings.TrimSpace(value) || strings.HasPrefix(value, "-") {
		return false
	}
	for _, r := range value {
		if !unicode.IsPrint(r) || unicode.Is(unicode.Cf, r) {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

func validateRequest(request Request) error {
	if !validText(request.Title, 256) {
		return ErrUnsafe
	}
	switch request.Provider {
	case Bitwarden:
		if !request.Experimental {
			return ErrExperimental
		}
		if request.AccountID != "" && !bwIDPattern.MatchString(request.AccountID) || request.VaultID != "" && request.VaultID != PersonalVault {
			return ErrUnsafe
		}
	case OnePassword:
		if request.Experimental || !opIDPattern.MatchString(request.VaultID) || request.AccountID != "" && !opIDPattern.MatchString(request.AccountID) {
			return ErrUnsafe
		}
	default:
		return ErrUnsafe
	}
	return nil
}

func serverURL(value string, allowBareHost bool) (string, bool) {
	if !validText(value, 512) {
		return "", false
	}
	if allowBareHost && !strings.Contains(value, "://") {
		value = "https://" + value
	}
	parsed, err := url.Parse(value)
	if err != nil || parsed.Scheme != "https" || parsed.Hostname() == "" || parsed.User != nil || parsed.RawQuery != "" || parsed.Fragment != "" || parsed.Opaque != "" {
		return "", false
	}
	return strings.TrimSuffix(parsed.String(), "/"), true
}

func supportedOPVersion(value string) bool {
	parts := strings.Split(value, ".")
	if len(parts) != 3 || parts[0] != "2" {
		return false
	}
	for _, part := range parts {
		if part == "" || len(part) > 4 {
			return false
		}
		for _, c := range part {
			if c < '0' || c > '9' {
				return false
			}
		}
	}
	minor, err := strconv.Atoi(parts[1])
	return err == nil && minor >= 20
}

// run never exposes a provider's stderr, raw failure, or partial output. A
// response can contain private fields even when only public metadata was asked
// for; every caller must wipe returned bytes after its bounded, typed decode.
func (s *Service) run(ctx context.Context, name string, args []string, input []byte) ([]byte, error) {
	if s == nil || s.runner == nil {
		return nil, ErrUnavailable
	}
	body, err := s.runner.Run(ctx, name, args, input)
	if err != nil || len(body) > maxOutput {
		sshcredential.Wipe(body)
		return nil, ErrUnavailable
	}
	return body, nil
}

func (s *Service) version(ctx context.Context, provider Provider) (string, error) {
	name := "op"
	if provider == Bitwarden {
		name = "bw"
	}
	body, err := s.run(ctx, name, []string{"--version"}, nil)
	defer sshcredential.Wipe(body)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if len(body) > 64 {
		return "", ErrUnsupportedVersion
	}
	version := strings.TrimSpace(string(body))
	if provider == Bitwarden && version != BitwardenSchemaVersion || provider == OnePassword && !supportedOPVersion(version) {
		return "", ErrUnsupportedVersion
	}
	return version, nil
}

func (s *Service) observe(ctx context.Context, request Request) (Destination, string, error) {
	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
		return Destination{}, "", err
	}
	version, err := s.version(ctx, request.Provider)
	if err != nil {
		return Destination{}, "", err
	}
	var destination Destination
	switch request.Provider {
	case Bitwarden:
		destination, err = s.observeBitwarden(ctx, request)
	case OnePassword:
		destination, err = s.observeOnePassword(ctx, request)
	default:
		err = ErrUnsafe
	}
	return destination, version, err
}

func (s *Service) observeBitwarden(ctx context.Context, request Request) (Destination, error) {
	body, err := s.run(ctx, "bw", []string{"status"}, nil)
	defer sshcredential.Wipe(body)
	if err != nil {
		return Destination{}, err
	}
	var status struct {
		Status    string `json:"status"`
		UserID    string `json:"userId"`
		ServerURL string `json:"serverUrl"`
	}
	if json.Unmarshal(body, &status) != nil {
		return Destination{}, ErrUnavailable
	}
	if status.Status == "locked" || status.Status == "unauthenticated" {
		return Destination{}, ErrLocked
	}
	server, valid := serverURL(status.ServerURL, false)
	if status.Status != "unlocked" || !bwIDPattern.MatchString(status.UserID) || !valid {
		return Destination{}, ErrUnavailable
	}
	if request.AccountID != "" && status.UserID != request.AccountID {
		return Destination{}, ErrStale
	}
	return Destination{Provider: Bitwarden, AccountID: status.UserID, UserID: status.UserID, ServerURL: server, VaultID: PersonalVault, VaultName: "Personal vault"}, nil
}

func (s *Service) observeOnePassword(ctx context.Context, request Request) (Destination, error) {
	args := []string{"whoami", "--format", "json"}
	if request.AccountID != "" {
		args = append(args, "--account", request.AccountID)
	}
	body, err := s.run(ctx, "op", args, nil)
	defer sshcredential.Wipe(body)
	if err != nil {
		return Destination{}, ErrLocked
	}
	var identity struct {
		AccountID string `json:"account_uuid"`
		UserID    string `json:"user_uuid"`
		URL       string `json:"url"`
	}
	if json.Unmarshal(body, &identity) != nil {
		return Destination{}, ErrUnavailable
	}
	server, valid := serverURL(identity.URL, true)
	if !opIDPattern.MatchString(identity.AccountID) || !opIDPattern.MatchString(identity.UserID) || !valid {
		return Destination{}, ErrUnavailable
	}
	if request.AccountID != "" && request.AccountID != identity.AccountID {
		return Destination{}, ErrStale
	}
	vaultBody, err := s.run(ctx, "op", []string{"vault", "get", request.VaultID, "--account", identity.AccountID, "--format", "json"}, nil)
	defer sshcredential.Wipe(vaultBody)
	if err != nil {
		return Destination{}, err
	}
	var vault struct {
		ID   string `json:"id"`
		Name string `json:"name"`
	}
	if json.Unmarshal(vaultBody, &vault) != nil || vault.ID != request.VaultID || !validText(vault.Name, 256) {
		return Destination{}, ErrUnavailable
	}
	return Destination{Provider: OnePassword, AccountID: identity.AccountID, UserID: identity.UserID, ServerURL: server, VaultID: vault.ID, VaultName: vault.Name}, nil
}

func (s *Service) Plan(ctx context.Context, request Request) (Plan, error) {
	if err := validateRequest(request); err != nil {
		return Plan{}, err
	}
	destination, version, err := s.observe(ctx, request)
	if err != nil {
		return Plan{}, err
	}
	var nonce [16]byte
	if _, err = rand.Read(nonce[:]); err != nil {
		return Plan{}, ErrUnavailable
	}
	request.AccountID, request.VaultID = destination.AccountID, destination.VaultID
	return Plan{Destination: destination, Version: version, Title: request.Title, Experimental: request.Experimental, state: &planState{service: s, request: request, dest: destination, version: version, operation: hex.EncodeToString(nonce[:])}}, nil
}

func (s *Service) Apply(ctx context.Context, plan Plan) (Result, error) {
	result := Result{Status: StatusNotStarted}
	if s == nil || plan.state == nil || plan.state.service != s || plan.Destination != plan.state.dest || plan.Version != plan.state.version || plan.Title != plan.state.request.Title || plan.Experimental != plan.state.request.Experimental {
		return result, ErrStale
	}
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	state := plan.state
	if state.attempted {
		return result, ErrPlanUsed
	}
	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
		return result, err
	}
	destination, version, err := s.observe(ctx, state.request)
	if err != nil {
		return result, err
	}
	if destination != state.dest || version != state.version {
		return result, ErrStale
	}
	if err = ctx.Err(); err != nil {
		return result, err
	}
	// No retry can be authorized after the mutating command is attempted, even
	// if its response is lost or the native provider reports an error.
	if state.dest.Provider == Bitwarden {
		result, err = s.createBitwarden(ctx, state)
	} else {
		state.attempted = true
		result, err = s.createOnePassword(ctx, state)
	}
	if result.Status != StatusCreated {
		return result, err
	}
	current, currentVersion, observationErr := s.observe(ctx, state.request)
	if observationErr != nil || current != state.dest || currentVersion != state.version {
		result.BindingStatus = BindingUnknown
		return result, ErrUnknown
	}
	result.BindingStatus = BindingVerified
	return result, err
}

package cli

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/sshhost"
)

var errSSHFleetImportAgent = errors.New("named-agent keys are not supported while importing connection or hop profiles FROM fleet; import with existing controller authentication or --config-only, then run regular dev ssh setup <local-alias> to select its agent key. Registering a regular alias TO fleet with --to fleet|both remains supported")

func validateSSHAgentOptions(options sshSetupOptions) error {
	selected := options.identityAgent != "" || options.agentRef != nil || options.keyCandidate != nil && options.keyCandidate.Agent != nil || options.keyPlan != nil && options.keyPlan.Agent != nil
	if !selected {
		return nil
	}
	if options.generateKey || options.configOnly || options.auth != "" {
		return errors.New("--identity-agent selects an existing agent key and cannot be combined with --generate-key, --config-only or --auth")
	}
	if options.identityFileChanged || options.identitiesOnlyChanged && !options.identitiesOnly {
		return errors.New("a named-agent key supplies its own public IdentityFile and IdentitiesOnly=yes; do not combine it with --identity-file or --identities-only=false")
	}
	if options.fleetImportKeyPicker || strings.HasPrefix(options.from, "fleet:") || strings.HasPrefix(options.from, "fleet-ssh:") {
		return errSSHFleetImportAgent
	}
	return nil
}

// prepareSSHAgentPublication keeps the selected agent as durable controller
// intent. An existing public copy never turns it into a local private signer.
func prepareSSHAgentPublication(ctx context.Context, service *sshhost.Service, alias, class string, options sshSetupOptions, plan sshhost.KeyPlan, definition *sshhost.ManagedDefinition) (*sshhost.KeyPlan, error) {
	if plan.Agent == nil {
		return nil, nil
	}
	if err := validateSSHAgentOptions(options); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if options.keyCandidate == nil {
		return nil, errors.New("agent key selection has no catalog candidate; select the key again")
	}
	publicPath := service.DefaultAgentPublicPath(plan.Agent.Provider, alias)
	if class == "foreign" {
		if options.dryRun {
			return nil, sshAgentManualError(alias, *plan.Agent, publicPath)
		}
		if err := service.VerifyAgentKeyPolicy(ctx, alias, *options.keyCandidate); err != nil {
			return nil, errors.Join(sshAgentManualError(alias, *plan.Agent, publicPath), err)
		}
		return nil, nil
	}
	publication, err := service.PlanKey(ctx, sshhost.KeyRequest{Operation: sshhost.KeyPublishAgent, Candidate: *options.keyCandidate, PublicDestination: publicPath})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if !publication.Ready() {
		return nil, sshKeyPlanBlockedError(publication)
	}
	definition.IdentityFile, definition.IdentityAgent = publication.PublicPath, plan.Agent.Socket
	enabled := true
	definition.IdentitiesOnly = &enabled
	return &publication, nil
}

func sshAgentPreview(item sshOnboardItem) []string {
	if item.KeyPlan == nil || item.KeyPlan.Agent == nil {
		return nil
	}
	ref := item.KeyPlan.Agent
	notes := []string{fmt.Sprintf("Selected %s SSH agent: %s", sshhost.AgentProviderLabel(ref.Provider), ref.Socket)}
	if publication := item.AgentPublicPlan; publication != nil {
		notes = append(notes,
			fmt.Sprintf("Public key only: %s %s (no private key file is created).", publication.Action, publication.PublicPath),
			"Managed SSH v2: IdentityAgent "+ref.Socket,
			"IdentityFile "+publication.PublicPath+"; IdentitiesOnly yes.",
			"dev v0.2.37 and older cannot manage this v2 fragment.")
	} else {
		notes = append(notes, "Existing foreign SSH agent policy matches; no SSH configuration or public key file will be written.")
	}
	return notes
}

package sshvault

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"strings"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/sshcredential"
	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh"
)

func (s *Service) createOnePassword(ctx context.Context, state *planState) (Result, error) {
	result := Result{Status: StatusUnknown, BindingStatus: BindingUnknown}
	args := []string{"item", "create", "--category", "ssh", "--title", state.request.Title, "--vault", state.dest.VaultID, "--account", state.dest.AccountID, "--format", "json"}
	body, err := s.run(ctx, "op", args, nil)
	defer sshcredential.Wipe(body)
	if err != nil {
		return result, ErrUnknown
	}
	// item create can return private fields. Do not decode them or retain its
	// complete item; the public key is fetched separately by the returned ID.
	var item struct {
		ID       string `json:"id"`
		Title    string `json:"title"`
		Category string `json:"category"`
		Vault    struct {
			ID string `json:"id"`
		} `json:"vault"`
	}
	if json.Unmarshal(body, &item) != nil || !opIDPattern.MatchString(item.ID) || item.Title != state.request.Title || item.Category != "SSH_KEY" || item.Vault.ID != state.dest.VaultID {
		return result, ErrUnknown
	}
	result.Status = StatusCreated
	result.Receipt = &Receipt{Destination: state.dest, ItemID: item.ID}
	if ctx.Err() != nil {
		return result, ErrPublicKey
	}
	publicBody, err := s.run(ctx, "op", []string{"item", "get", item.ID, "--vault", state.dest.VaultID, "--account", state.dest.AccountID, "--fields", "label=public key", "--format", "json"}, nil)
	defer sshcredential.Wipe(publicBody)
	if err != nil {
		return result, ErrPublicKey
	}
	var field struct {
		ID    string `json:"id"`
		Type  string `json:"type"`
		Value string `json:"value"`
	}
	selected := bytes.TrimSpace(publicBody)
	if len(selected) > 0 && selected[0] == '[' {
		// The CLI's selected-fields JSON may be a one-element array. Do not
		// accept multiple fields or fall back to reading the whole item.
		var fields []json.RawMessage
		if json.Unmarshal(selected, &fields) != nil {
			return result, ErrPublicKey
		}
		defer func() {
			for _, raw := range fields {
				sshcredential.Wipe(raw)
			}
		}()
		if len(fields) != 1 {
			return result, ErrPublicKey
		}
		selected = fields[0]
	}
	if json.Unmarshal(selected, &field) != nil || field.ID != "public_key" || field.Type != "STRING" {
		return result, ErrPublicKey
	}
	line, fingerprint, err := publicIdentity(field.Value)
	if err != nil {
		return result, ErrPublicKey
	}
	result.Receipt.PublicLine, result.Receipt.Fingerprint = line, fingerprint
	return result, nil
}

func publicIdentity(line string) (string, string, error) {
	if len(line) > 4096 {
		return "", "", ErrPublicKey
	}
	line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
	if strings.ContainsAny(line, "\r\n\x00") {
		return "", "", ErrPublicKey
	}
	key, _, options, rest, err := ssh.ParseAuthorizedKey([]byte(line + "\n"))
	if err != nil || len(options) != 0 || len(bytes.TrimSpace(rest)) != 0 || key.Type() != ssh.KeyAlgoED25519 {
		return "", "", ErrPublicKey
	}
	// Provider comments are not identity and are not needed in a public-only
	// receipt. Return only the canonical algorithm and public blob.
	return strings.TrimSpace(string(ssh.MarshalAuthorizedKey(key))), ssh.FingerprintSHA256(key), nil
}

package sshvault

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/ed25519"
	"crypto/rand"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/json"
	"encoding/pem"
	"strings"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/sshcredential"
	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh"
)

const vaultKeyOwner = "dev-cli:ssh-key:v1"

type bwField struct {
	Name  string `json:"name"`
	Value string `json:"value"`
	Type  int    `json:"type"`
}

// Unknown custom fields might contain secrets. Decode only our two public
// ownership fields, not arbitrary field values from a provider response.
type bwResponseField bwField

func (field *bwResponseField) UnmarshalJSON(body []byte) error {
	var header struct {
		Name string `json:"name"`
		Type int    `json:"type"`
	}
	if json.Unmarshal(body, &header) != nil {
		return ErrUnavailable
	}
	field.Name, field.Type = header.Name, header.Type
	if header.Name != "dev-owner" && header.Name != "dev-operation" {
		return nil
	}
	var value struct {
		Value string `json:"value"`
	}
	if json.Unmarshal(body, &value) != nil {
		return ErrUnavailable
	}
	field.Value = value.Value
	return nil
}

func (s *Service) createBitwarden(ctx context.Context, state *planState) (Result, error) {
	result := Result{Status: StatusNotStarted}
	input, publicLine, fingerprint, err := bitwardenInput(state)
	defer sshcredential.Wipe(input)
	if err != nil {
		return result, err
	}
	if err = ctx.Err(); err != nil {
		return result, err
	}
	state.attempted = true
	result.Status, result.BindingStatus = StatusUnknown, BindingUnknown
	body, err := s.run(ctx, "bw", []string{"create", "item"}, input)
	defer sshcredential.Wipe(body)
	if err != nil {
		return result, ErrUnknown
	}
	// The type-5 response may contain the entire private key. It stays in the
	// bounded response buffer and is deliberately absent from this decoder.
	var item struct {
		ID             string            `json:"id"`
		Type           int               `json:"type"`
		Name           string            `json:"name"`
		OrganizationID *string           `json:"organizationId"`
		CollectionIDs  []string          `json:"collectionIds"`
		Fields         []bwResponseField `json:"fields"`
		SSHKey         struct {
			PublicKey      string `json:"publicKey"`
			KeyFingerprint string `json:"keyFingerprint"`
		} `json:"sshKey"`
	}
	if json.Unmarshal(body, &item) != nil || !bwIDPattern.MatchString(item.ID) || item.Type != 5 || item.Name != state.request.Title || item.OrganizationID != nil && *item.OrganizationID != "" || len(item.CollectionIDs) != 0 || !ownedBitwardenFields(item.Fields, state.operation) {
		return result, ErrUnknown
	}
	// A matching operation marker identifies the created item even if its
	// public-key receipt is incomplete. Keep the exact ID for reconciliation.
	result.Status = StatusCreated
	result.Receipt = &Receipt{Destination: state.dest, ItemID: item.ID}
	actualLine, actualFingerprint, err := publicIdentity(item.SSHKey.PublicKey)
	if err != nil || actualLine != publicLine || actualFingerprint != fingerprint || item.SSHKey.KeyFingerprint != fingerprint {
		return result, ErrPublicKey
	}
	result.Receipt.PublicLine, result.Receipt.Fingerprint = publicLine, fingerprint
	return result, nil
}

func ownedBitwardenFields(fields []bwResponseField, operation string) bool {
	if len(fields) != 2 {
		return false
	}
	owner, exactOperation := false, false
	for _, field := range fields {
		if field.Type != 0 {
			return false
		}
		switch field.Name {
		case "dev-owner":
			if owner || field.Value != vaultKeyOwner {
				return false
			}
			owner = true
		case "dev-operation":
			if exactOperation || field.Value != operation {
				return false
			}
			exactOperation = true
		default:
			return false
		}
	}
	return owner && exactOperation
}

// bitwardenInput owns all directly accessible secret buffers and wipes them on
// return. The remaining encoded stdin is also secret and its caller must wipe it.
// Go/crypto/PEM implementations and the OS can retain additional copies; this is
// best-effort cleanup, not a no-swap, no-core-dump or complete-erasure guarantee.
func bitwardenInput(state *planState) ([]byte, string, string, error) {
	public, private, err := ed25519.GenerateKey(rand.Reader)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, "", "", ErrUnavailable
	}
	defer sshcredential.Wipe(private)
	key, err := ssh.NewPublicKey(public)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, "", "", ErrUnavailable
	}
	block, err := ssh.MarshalPrivateKey(private, state.request.Title)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, "", "", ErrUnavailable
	}
	defer sshcredential.Wipe(block.Bytes)
	privatePEM := pem.EncodeToMemory(block)
	defer sshcredential.Wipe(privatePEM)
	publicLine := strings.TrimSpace(string(ssh.MarshalAuthorizedKey(key)))
	fingerprint := ssh.FingerprintSHA256(key)
	metadata := struct {
		Type           int       `json:"type"`
		Name           string    `json:"name"`
		Login          any       `json:"login"`
		OrganizationID any       `json:"organizationId"`
		CollectionIDs  []string  `json:"collectionIds"`
		Fields         []bwField `json:"fields"`
	}{Type: 5, Name: state.request.Title, CollectionIDs: []string{}, Fields: []bwField{{Name: "dev-owner", Value: vaultKeyOwner}, {Name: "dev-operation", Value: state.operation}}}
	prefix, err := json.Marshal(metadata)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, "", "", ErrUnsafe
	}
	publicJSON, _ := json.Marshal(publicLine)
	fingerprintJSON, _ := json.Marshal(fingerprint)
	// Do not convert private PEM to a Go string or feed it to encoding/json's
	// pooled buffers. Only the public metadata above uses json.Marshal.
	body := make([]byte, 0, len(prefix)+2*len(privatePEM)+len(publicJSON)+len(fingerprintJSON)+128)
	body = append(body, prefix[:len(prefix)-1]...)
	body = append(body, `,"sshKey":{"privateKey":`...)
	body = appendPEMString(body, privatePEM)
	body = append(body, `,"publicKey":`...)
	body = append(body, publicJSON...)
	body = append(body, `,"keyFingerprint":`...)
	body = append(body, fingerprintJSON...)
	body = append(body, '}', '}')
	defer sshcredential.Wipe(body)
	encoded := make([]byte, base64.StdEncoding.EncodedLen(len(body)))
	base64.StdEncoding.Encode(encoded, body)
	return encoded, publicLine, fingerprint, nil
}

// PEM is ASCII. Append its JSON representation directly so every secret buffer
// remains mutable and can receive best-effort cleanup.
func appendPEMString(destination, value []byte) []byte {
	const hexDigits = "0123456789abcdef"
	destination = append(destination, '"')
	for _, b := range value {
		switch b {
		case '"', '\\':
			destination = append(destination, '\\', b)
		case '\n':
			destination = append(destination, '\\', 'n')
		case '\r':
			destination = append(destination, '\\', 'r')
		default:
			if b < 0x20 {
				destination = append(destination, '\\', 'u', '0', '0', hexDigits[b>>4], hexDigits[b&15])
			} else {
				destination = append(destination, b)
			}
		}
	}
	return append(destination, '"')
}

# dev-cli

Git owns durable code; worktrees are local checkouts; runtimes are host-local
sessions; dev records task intent.

## Discover what you need

Use `dev <command> --help` for current syntax and flags, and `dev help <topic>`
for workflow explanations. `dev --help` lists commands; `dev help` lists topics.
Prefer supported `--json` output for automation. Read the relevant command before
mutation: some actions execute immediately, while others require preview/apply.
Do not preload manuals, repeat `dev --skill`, or run diagnostics for every task.

## Preserve these boundaries

- Opening a repository needs no task. Choose direct, branch, or worktree
  deliberately; pass an explicit `--base` for branch/worktree creation. Keep
  managed worktrees outside repositories.
- `dev start` normally prepares a checkout/runtime. Agent launch is explicit.
  Parallel writers need coordinated ownership and verified launch targets.
- Completion, artifact finalization, retirement, and branch deletion are separate.
  Finalize agent artifacts after their writer stops; retire an agent checkout
  externally. A runtime's `done` state does not mean cleanup is safe.
- Unknown or cached observations, merged PRs, and command refusals do not grant
  cleanup authority. Resolve the reported conditions; do not improvise force
  removal or bypass trust checks.

## Read a reference for advanced operations

- Worktree provisioning or cross-host lifecycle: [ownership](references/worktree-ownership.md), [lifecycle](references/task-lifecycle.md).
- Parallel agent launches or prompt transports: [agents](references/parallel-agents.md), [handoffs](references/prompt-handoffs.md).
- History retention: [artifacts](references/ai-artifacts.md).
- Agent completion or cleanup batches: [retirement](references/agent-retirement.md), [triage](references/local-triage.md).
- Repository hygiene batches, scans or redaction: [hygiene](references/hygiene.md).
- Repository hooks, publication, or physical organization: [setup](references/repository-bootstrap.md), [bootstrap](references/bootstrap.md).
- SSH dashboard, diagnosis, discovery, tests/activity, keys, credentials and registration: [SSH](references/ssh-hosts.md).
- Dotfile setup, native chezmoi operations, or FLEET host actions: [dotfiles](references/dotfiles.md).
- Skill/MCP/instruction transfers, updates or removal: [transfers](references/agent-interop.md), [maintenance](references/skills-management.md).
- Recursive Git children: [submodules](references/submodules.md).

Use command help and its workflow topic for everyday operations.

## Unexpected dev failures

Read [feedback and repair](references/feedback-and-repair.md). Preserve the
original task; extra investigation, repair, subagents and publication need
explicit consent covering scope and cost.

293	    exit 1

297	  exit $?

122	Configures a local user account to permit authentication using a supported
123	SmartCard.  Authentication is via asymmetric key (also known as
124	public-key) encryption.
125	.Ss CTK Identity
126	CTK Identity allows to create and manipulate CryptoTokenKit identities. CryptoTokenKit identities can use non-exportable or exportable private keys. The non-exportable private key is protected by the Secure Enclave and the key never leves the Secure Enclave in open form. The exportable private key is encrypted with Elliptic Curve Encryption Standard Variable IVX963 algorithm which is backed by a Secure Enclave key. CryptoTokenKit Identities and private keys can be used for TLS authentication, email protection and SSL using

17	func TestFormattingPreservesOptionsAndIsIdempotent(t *testing.T) {
18		raw := []byte("# header\r\n Host a b\r\n\tHostName=example.invalid\r\n  ProxyCommand ssh jump 'nc %h %p'\r\n  # note\r\nMatch exec \"never-run\"\r\n\tUser tester\r\n")

20		if err != nil {
21			t.Fatal(err)
22		}
23		again, err := FormatConfig(formatted, "    ")
24		if err != nil || !bytes.Equal(formatted, again) {
25			t.Fatal("not idempotent")
26		}
27		for _, value := range []string{"HostName=example.invalid", "ProxyCommand ssh jump 'nc %h %p'", "Match exec \"never-run\""} {
28			if !bytes.Contains(formatted, []byte(value)) {
29				t.Fatal("changed value", value)
30			}
31		}
32		if strings.Count(string(raw), "\r\n") != strings.Count(string(formatted), "\r\n") {
33			t.Fatal("changed line endings")
34		}
35		if _, err = FormatConfig([]byte("Host \"unterminated"), "    "); err == nil {
36			t.Fatal("accepted malformed input")
37		}
38	}

21	// FormatConfig preserves every byte after leading horizontal whitespace. It
22	// never evaluates Match, command options, Includes, keys or DNS.
23	func FormatConfig(data []byte, indent string) ([]byte, error) {
24		if indent != "  " && indent != "    " && indent != "\t" {
25			return nil, errors.New("indent must be 2, 4 or tab")
26		}
27		var out bytes.Buffer
28		inBlock := false
29		for _, line := range strings.SplitAfter(string(data), "\n") {
30			body := strings.TrimLeft(line, " \t")
31			parse := strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(body, "\n"), "\r")
32			if strings.TrimSpace(parse) == "" {
33				out.WriteString(line)
34				continue
35			}
36			key, _, comment, err := parseConfigLine(parse)
37			if err != nil {
38				return nil, err
39			}
40			if comment {
41				// Top-level comments commonly introduce the following Host block.
42				if len(body) < len(line) && inBlock {
43					out.WriteString(indent)
44				}
45				out.WriteString(body)
46				continue
47			}
48			if strings.EqualFold(key, "Host") || strings.EqualFold(key, "Match") {
49				inBlock = true
50			} else if inBlock {
51				out.WriteString(indent)
52			}
53			out.WriteString(body)
54		}
55		return append([]byte{}, out.Bytes()...), nil
56	}

124	func splitBlocks(path string, data []byte) (string, []ConfigBlock, error) {
125		lines := strings.SplitAfter(string(data), "\n")
126		var starts, hostLines []int

132			}
133			if empty {
134				if pending < 0 {
135					pending = i
136				}
137				continue
138			}
139			if strings.EqualFold(k, "Match") {
140				return "", nil, errors.New("Match sections need manual organization; formatting remains available")
141			}
142			if strings.EqualFold(k, "Host") {
143				if len(args) == 0 {
144					return "", nil, errors.New("empty Host declaration")
145				}
146				start := i
147				if len(starts) > 0 && pending >= 0 {
148					start = pending
149				}
150				starts = append(starts, start)
151				hostLines = append(hostLines, i)
152			}
153			pending = -1
154		}
155		if len(starts) == 0 {
156			return string(data), nil, nil
157		}

159		for i, start := range starts {

161			if i+1 < len(starts) {

172			}
173			blocks = append(blocks, b)
174		}
175		return strings.Join(lines[:starts[0]], ""), blocks, nil
176	}

### Read-only `bw config server`

The read path applies when:

- The setting is `server`.
- The URL is missing, null, or blank.
- None of `webVault`, `api`, `identity`, `icons`, `notifications`, or `events` is enabled.

It returns a successful `StringResponse` containing:

- `env.getUrls().base` when `environment.hasBaseUrl()` is true.
- `https://bitwarden.com` otherwise.

If the effective base URL is null, the code’s fallback payload is exactly:

`https://bitwarden.com`

The response envelope format is not defined in the supplied content, so only the contained string can be stated exactly.

### Cloud EU/US

The code does not provide the EU or US base URLs, nor does it expose how `hasBaseUrl()` distinguishes them. It would return the environment’s configured base URL when available; otherwise it returns the fallback above.

### Read keys relevant to server identity

Only `server` is recognized as a readable configuration setting. No separate read keys for region, cloud, EU, or US identity appear in the supplied code.

US is the initial default region.

## `getUrls().base` for cloud regions

For US and EU, `CloudEnvironment` receives the region’s URL object, whose `base` value is `null`. Therefore:

```ts
environment.getUrls().base === null
environment.hasBaseUrl() === false
```

A base URL is intended for self-hosted configuration. Cloud API URLs come directly from `urls.api`.

Relevant behavior: **“Unknown regions are treated as self-hosted”**. The region key must therefore be preserved separately from the URL fields.

## Fields identifying the environment

- `region`: `Region.US`, `Region.EU`, or `Region.SelfHosted`
- `urls.api`: explicit API endpoint
- `urls.base`: self-hosted base endpoint; `null` for production cloud regions
- `CloudEnvironment.config.domain`: `bitwarden.com` or `bitwarden.eu`
- `isCloud()`: true whenever the region is not self-hosted

`getApiUrl()` returns the explicit API URL when present; otherwise it derives one from the base URL or the production fallback.

## Safe CLI binding when `bw status.serverUrl` is null

Do not bind or dereference `serverUrl` unless it is non-null. Resolve the environment from the account’s stored region and URL state instead:

- For a user-facing server URL, use `getWebVaultUrl()`.
- For an API endpoint, use `getApiUrl()`.
- Do not use `getUrls().base` as the cloud server URL, because it is `null` for US and EU.

```text
## Type 5 / SSH item support
- Items are parsed as `CipherExport`.
- `FeatureFlag.PM40201_DeriveSSHKeys` controls whether derived SSH keys are enabled.
- The flag is passed to `CipherExport.toView`.
- No explicit numeric type-5 branch or SSH-specific request schema appears here.
- Organization policy may reject restricted cipher types before creation.

## Creating an item: stdin and Base64
For non-attachment objects:

1. In CLI mode, missing input is read from stdin.
2. Missing or empty input returns a bad-request response.
3. String input is decoded from Base64 as UTF-8, then parsed as JSON.
4. Non-string input is used directly.
5. Invalid Base64/JSON returns a parsing error.
6. `item` dispatches to `createCipher(req)`.

The expected item payload is therefore a `CipherExport` JSON object, encoded as Base64 when supplied as a string.

## Selected user ID and account identity
- The command always uses the active account’s ID from `activeAccount$`.
- That ID is used for cipher creation, attachment access, folder encryption, and organization lookups.
- Item creation does not accept an independent user ID from the request.
- Organization collections may specify user selections, but the default is the current organization user with management enabled.

## Output metadata and operation behavior
- Successful item creation returns `Response.success(new CipherResponse(newCipher))`.
- Successful folder creation returns a `FolderResponse`.
- Successful collection creation returns an `OrganizationCollectionResponse` containing the collection view plus server-returned groups and users.
- Failures use `Response.badRequest`, `Response.notFound`, or `Response.error`.
- The exact serialized JSON fields are not defined in this file because `Response`, `CipherResponse`, and related models are implemented elsewhere.
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
### `ssh-keychain.dylib` and `sk_enroll`

- The document reports that `/usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib` exports the OpenSSH security-key functions, including `sk_enroll`, `sk_sign`, and `sk_load_resident_keys` (verified locally with `nm`).
- Despite exporting `sk_enroll`, enrollment through the provider is unsupported. The reported result is **“requested feature not supported”**, and this direct command fails:

```sh
ssh-keygen -t ecdsa-sk -w /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib
```

- Therefore, enrollment must be performed through `sc_auth`, not `ssh-keygen`. The documented route is:

```sh
sc_auth create-ctk-identity -l ssh -k p-256-ne -t bio
```

Reference: the document’s **“Apple already ships an SE-backed sk provider”** and **“Verified end-to-end”** sections; it links to Apple’s `ssh-keychain(8)` material, OpenSSH’s `sk-api.h`, and the cited working write-up.

### Hash and identity filtering

- This command filters CTK identities to those intended for SSH and reports their SSH-compatible public-key hashes:

```sh
sc_auth list-ctk-identities -t ssh
```

- When several identities exist, the document reports that `ssh-keygen -K` gives every one the same output filename, `id_ecdsa_sk_rk`, because they share the `ssh:` application value. The proposed disambiguation is to compare each key’s `ssh-keygen -lf` fingerprint with the entries returned by `sc_auth list-ctk-identities -t ssh`.
- This is an identification workflow, not a claim that `ssh-keygen -K` provides unique filenames or an independent key-selection mechanism.

Reference: the document’s **“Verified end-to-end”** section and its references to `sc_auth(8)` and `PROTOCOL.u2f`.

### Key-format mapping

- The document distinguishes the wire types:
  - Ordinary P-256 SSH keys use `ecdsa-sha2-nistp256`.
  - OpenSSH security-key P-256 keys use `sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com`.
- Apple’s bridge is described as mapping CTK RSA identities to PKCS#11, while mapping CTK `ecdsa256` identities to the Secure Key/FIDO middleware path.
- The provider is selected with:

```sh
export SSH_SK_PROVIDER=/usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib
```

- The resulting private-key file is only a machine-specific security-key handle; it is not an exportable private key. The document relates this to OpenSSH’s `key_handle` field in `PROTOCOL.u2f`.

Reference: the document’s **“Option 2 — PKCS#11”**, **“Option 4 — FIDO middleware”**, and **“Apple already ships an SE-backed sk provider”** sections, with links to Apple’s `ssh-keychain(8)`, OpenSSH’s `sk-api.h`, and `PROTOCOL.u2f`.

### Explicit limitations

- The described behavior was verified only on macOS 15.7 with Apple `OpenSSH_9.9p2`; the document does not establish equivalent behavior on other macOS or OpenSSH versions.
- The Apple provider signs and loads resident identities but does not enroll them.
- Servers must support OpenSSH security-key types; the document identifies OpenSSH 8.2 or newer as the relevant baseline.
- Every client using the key must have the provider configured, unless the platform’s surrounding configuration supplies it.
- The document reports that `-t bio` prompts for Touch ID on each signature, while `-t none` still causes Apple’s provider to assert the user-presence flag.
- The documented route is not equivalent to plain ECDSA authentication: it uses the `sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com` format and FIDO-style application, flag, counter, and message-hash framing.

# Native Secure Enclave backed ssh keys on MacOS 

It turns out that MacOS Tahoe can generate and use secure-enclave backed SSH keys! This replaces projects like https://github.com/maxgoedjen/secretive

There is a shared library `/usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib` that traditionally has been used to add smartcard support
to ssh by implementing `PKCS11Provider` interface. However since recently it also implements `SecurityKeyProivder`
which supports loading keys directly from the secure enclave! `SecurityKeyProvider` is what is normally used to talk to FIDO2 devices (e.g. `libfido2` can be used to talk to your Yubikey). However you can now use it to talk to your Secure Enclave instead!



https://gist.github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff033694-13e1-454e-b42b-b5c19e0fb2a0


Seems this method was first discovered in https://lists.mindrot.org/pipermail/openssh-unix-dev/2024-July/041451.html

## Key setup

See `man sc_auth` and `man ssh-keychain` for all the options

To create a Secure Enclave backed key that requires biometrics, run the
following command and press TouchID:
```
% sc_auth create-ctk-identity -l ssh -k p-256-ne -t bio
```

You can confirm that the key was create with the `list-ctk-identities` command:
```
arian@Mac ssh-keychain % sc_auth  list-ctk-identities       
Key Type Public Key Hash                          Prot Label Common Name Email Address Valid To        Valid 
p-256-ne A71277F0BC5825A7B3576D014F31282A866EF3BC bio  ssh   ssh                       23.11.26, 17:09 YES
```


It also supports listing the ssh key fingerprints instead:
```
% sc_auth  list-ctk-identities -t ssh
Key Type Public Key Hash                                    Prot Label Common Name Email Address Valid To        Valid 
p-256-ne SHA256:vs4ByYo+T9M3V8iiDYONMSvx2k5Fj2ujVBWt1j6yzis bio  ssh   ssh                       23.11.26, 17:09 YES 
```

Keys can be deleted with
```
% sc_auth delete-ctk-identity -h <Public Key Hash>
```


## Usage with `ssh`

You can "download" the public / private keypair from the secure enclave using the following command:
```
% ssh-keygen -w /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib -K -N ""
Enter PIN for authenticator: 
You may need to touch your authenticator to authorize key download.
Saved ECDSA-SK key to id_ecdsa_sk_rk
% cat id_ecdsa_sk_rk.pub 
sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com AAAAInNrLWVjZHNhLXNoYTItbmlzdHAyNTZAb3BlbnNzaC5jb20AAAAIbmlzdHAyNTYAAABBBKiHAiAZhcsZ95n85dkNGs9GnbDt0aNOia2gnuknYV2wKL3y0u+d3QrE9cFkmWXIymHZMglL+uJA+6mShY8SeykAAAAEc3NoOg== ssh:
```

You can just use the empty string for PIN. For some reason `openssh` always asks for
it even if the authenticator in question does not use a PIN but a biometric.
Note that the "private" key here is just a reference to the FIDO credential. It does
not contain any secret key material. Hence I'm specifiyng `-N ""` to skip an encryption
passphrase.

Now if you copy this public key to your authorized keys file, it should work!

```
% ssh-copy-id -i id_ecdsa_sk_rk localhost
% ssh -o SecurityKeyProvider=/usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib localhost
```


## Usage with `ssh-agent`

Instead of downloading the public/private keypair to a file you can also directly
make the keys available to `ssh-agent`. For this you can use the following command:
```
% ssh-add -K -S /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib
Enter PIN for authenticator: 
Resident identity added: ECDSA-SK SHA256:vs4ByYo+T9M3V8iiDYONMSvx2k5Fj2ujVBWt1j6yzis
% ssh-add -L
sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com AAAAInNrLWVjZHNhLXNoYTItbmlzdHAyNTZAb3BlbnNzaC5jb20AAAAIbmlzdHAyNTYAAABBBKiHAiAZhcsZ95n85dkNGs9GnbDt0aNOia2gnuknYV2wKL3y0u+d3QrE9cFkmWXIymHZMglL+uJA+6mShY8SeykAAAAEc3NoOg== 
% ssh-copy-id localhost
% ssh -o SecurityKeyProvider=/usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib localhost
```


## Using the SecurityKeyProvider by default

`SecurityKeyProvider` can be configured in `.ssh/config` but I recommend setting
`export SSH_SK_PROVIDER=/usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib` in your `.zprofile` instead as
that environment variable gets picked up by `ssh`, `ssh-add` and `ssh-keygen`.

This means you can just do:

```
ssh-add -K
ssh my-server
```

or

```
ssh-keygen -K
ssh -i id_ecdsa_rk_sk my-server
```

to ssh into your server


## Exportable keys

There's also an exportable variant where the private key is encrypted using the secure enclave as opposed to generated on the secure enclave. This is might be considered less secure but is convenient for key backup.

````
% sc_auth create-ctk-identity -l ssh-exportable -k p-256 -t bio
% sc_auth list-ctk-identities
p-256    A581E5404ED157C4C73FFDBDFC1339E0D873FCAE bio  ssh-exportable ssh-exportable               23.11.26, 19:50 YES  
% sc_auth export-ctk-identity -h A581E5404ED157C4C73FFDBDFC1339E0D873FCAE -f ssh-exportable.pem
Enter a password which will be used to protect the exported items:
Verify password:
````

You can then re-import it on another device

```
% sc_auth import-ctk-identities -f ssh-exportable.pem.p12 -t bio
Enter PKCS12 file password:
```
```

## Author and context

- **Author:** Jan Schermer  
- **Date:** Thu Jul 4 22:57:39 AEST 2024  
- **Subject:** *Apple's SSH x OpenSSH (brew) x CTK x Security Key types*

## Apple `ssh-keychain.dylib` / Secure Key provider

Schermer reports that Apple’s stock SSH includes `/usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib`, which exposes certain CTK and persistent-token credentials through the SSH security-key interface.

The reported behavior is:

- `ssh-keygen -K` can discover ECDSA-SK credentials exposed by Apple’s provider.
- CTK-backed EC credentials can be used as `sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com` keys.
- The implementation appears limited to ECDSA P-256:
  - no RSA security-key support;
  - no security-key generation through this provider;
  - no ECDSA P-384 support.
- Apple’s PKCS#11 path reportedly remains RSA-only.
- A YubiKey 5C PIV credential was discovered successfully, but signing through the direct USB token path failed authentication.
- Importing the same resident credential into CTK succeeded; signing then triggered Touch ID and authentication worked.

Relevant commands:

```sh
export SSH_SK_PROVIDER=/usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib
ssh-keygen -K
ssh -i ecdsa_sk_rk user@example.com
```

The post also says Homebrew OpenSSH ignored the environment variable in this case, while the explicit option worked:

```sh
ssh -oSecurityKeyProvider=/usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib -i ecdsa_sk_rk user@example.com
```

## Direct enrollment versus `sc_auth`

The post distinguishes Apple’s CTK enrollment utility from SSH provider discovery.

For direct CTK identity creation:

```sh
sc_auth create-ctk-identity -l SSH -k p-256-ne -t bio -N username -E username@example.com
```

For importing a PKCS#12 credential:

```sh
sc_auth import-ctk-identities -f credentials.pfx -t bio
```

Schermer presents `sc_auth` as the mechanism for creating or importing CTK credentials, including Secure Enclave wrapping and biometric authorization. The SSH provider then exposes eligible existing credentials for SSH use; it is not described as an SSH key-generation interface.

The post warns that importing a login-capable certificate into CTK may affect macOS lock-screen authentication: Touch ID may be required, while password entry may become unavailable because the credential appears permanently connected.

## USB FIDO / Apple stock SSH observation

The reported USB-token test used a YubiKey 5C with a certificate in PIV slot `9a` or `9c`. Apple’s stock SSH discovered the credential through the security-key provider and prompted for user presence, but the server rejected the resulting signature.

The same credential, after CTK import, produced a successful authentication after Touch ID confirmation. Thus, the post documents working Apple-stock SSH support for a CTK-exposed security-key representation, but not reliable direct authentication through the tested USB PIV path.

95: ### SeKey — dormant
96: 
97: [SeKey](https://github.com/sekey/sekey) (Rust) pioneered the same architecture — an
98: agent on `~/.sekey/ssh-agent.ssh` using the keychain/SecKey API against the SE — but the
99: repo's last push was **November 2022** with 31 issues open. Treat it as historical prior
100: art, not a daily driver.
101: 
102: ### Prior art in the same shape on other hardware
103: 
104: The "tiny agent in front of non-exportable hardware keys" pattern is well proven
105: elsewhere: [yubikey-agent](https://github.com/FiloSottile/yubikey-agent) (PIV applet,
106: list+sign only, PIN via pinentry, touch per login, deliberately no PKCS#11) and
107: [ssh-tpm-agent](https://github.com/Foxboron/ssh-tpm-agent) (Go, Linux/Windows TPM 2.0,
108: actively maintained — the closest analog to an SE agent on the Linux side), plus
109: [pivy](https://github.com/arekinath/pivy) for PIV. All three chose the agent interface
110: over PKCS#11; that convergence is itself a data point.
111: 
112: ### Apple's own ssh-agent: no SE support
113: 
114: macOS's bundled `ssh-agent`/`ssh-add` keychain integration is **passphrase storage
115: only**: `--apple-use-keychain` stores "each passphrase … in the user's keychain" and
116: `--apple-load-keychain` re-adds file-based identities using those stored passphrases
117: (ssh-add(1) on macOS, *(verified locally)*; Apple's patched source lives in
118: [apple-oss-distributions/OpenSSH](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/OpenSSH)).
119: The private keys are ordinary files; the SE is not involved. The only way Apple's stock
120: tools touch the SE for SSH is the CTK/`ssh-keychain.dylib` path in Options 3–4.
121: 
122: ### Building it ourselves — done and verified
123: 
124: > **Update:** this was subsequently built as `enclave-ssh-ca agent` (Agent.swift,
125: > ~150 lines) and verified live: `ssh-add -l` interop, plain-key login, and
126: > certificate-only login via `TrustedUserCAKeys` against a local sshd — see
127: > `demo-agent.sh` and the self-contained writeup in `docs/agent-poc-guide.md`.
128: > The paragraph below was the pre-implementation estimate; it held up.
129: 
130: This is the smallest possible delta over what the repo already has: a unix-socket server
131: (`SOCK_STREAM`, `Network.framework` or plain BSD sockets), RFC 9987 framing, and two
132: handlers. `SSHWire.swift` provides all primitives; `SSHKeys.swift` already encodes the
133: `ecdsa-sha2-nistp256` public blob and the r‖s→mpint signature; the SE signing call is the
134: one already used by `sign`. Certificates come almost free: list the CA-signed cert blob
135: as a second identity. Realistic scope: a few hundred lines.

139: ## Option 2 — PKCS#11 (`PKCS11Provider`) — dead end for the SE
140: 
141: OpenSSH loads a PKCS#11 shared library via `ssh -I` / `PKCS11Provider` (and
142: `ssh-add -s`), and has supported ECDSA keys through PKCS#11 since
143: [OpenSSH 8.0](https://www.openssh.org/txt/release-8.0) ("Add support for ECDSA keys in
144: PKCS#11 tokens"). So the *interface* could carry a P-256 key. The problem is the module:
145: 
146: - Apple's bridge, `/usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib`, is documented in
147:   [ssh-keychain(8)](https://keith.github.io/xcode-man-pages/ssh-keychain.8.html) as "a
148:   PKCS#11 and Secure Key module replacement" that "provides identities from
149:   CryptoTokenKit tokens (SmartCards and persistent tokens)" — but only "**RSA for
150:   PKCS#11** and ecdsa256 for Secure Key module" *(man page verified locally; the dylib
151:   exports both `C_GetFunctionList` and the `sk_*` API — confirmed with `nm`)*. The SE
152:   cannot do RSA, so **the PKCS#11 half of Apple's bridge can never serve an SE key**.
153: - This precisely explains the failure documented in
154:   [Apple DevForums thread 723264](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/723264): a
155:   developer registered an SE-resident P-256 key via a CTK persistent token extension and
156:   got `pkcs11_register_provider: provider /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib returned no slots`
157:   on macOS 12.5 and 13.1 — the EC identity is invisible to the RSA-only PKCS#11 facade.
158:   The practical advice in the thread ("implement an SSH Agent that will leverage Secure
159:   Enclave") matches Option 1.
160: - Writing our own full PKCS#11 module (Cryptoki object model, sessions, slots) just to
161:   reach `C_Sign` on one key type is the heaviest possible wrapper around
162:   `signature(for:)`, and yubikey-agent's README is a good writeup of why even smartcard
163:   people avoid inflicting PKCS#11 on themselves.
164: 
165: Conclusion: real interface, wrong module ecosystem. Skip.

169: ## Option 3 — CryptoTokenKit persistent tokens
170: 
171: [CryptoTokenKit](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/cryptotokenkit) lets an app
172: ship a token extension ([`TKTokenDriver`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/cryptotokenkit/tktokendriver)
173: / `TKToken` / `TKTokenSession`) that presents keys — including SE keys — to the system
174: as a smartcard-like token: the keys appear in the keychain, any app can use them through
175: `SecKey`, and `sc_auth`/`system_profiler SPSmartCardsDataType` list them. Real examples:
176: [mwielgoszewski/SecureEnclaveToken](https://github.com/mwielgoszewski/SecureEnclaveToken)
177: (an SE-backed token driver with Touch ID protection; its README covers CSR/certificate
178: handling but never mentions SSH) and the Purebred
179: [CtkProvider](https://github.com/Purebred/CtkProvider) sample for persistent tokens.
180: 
181: Crucially, **macOS now ships this whole path built in** — no third-party extension
182: needed. [sc_auth(8)](https://keith.github.io/xcode-man-pages/sc_auth.8.html) grew a "CTK
183: Identity" command family *(verified locally on macOS 15)*:
184: 
185: ```sh
186: sc_auth create-ctk-identity -l ssh -k p-256-ne -t bio   # -ne = non-exportable (SE); -t bio = Touch ID
187: sc_auth list-ctk-identities -t ssh                      # SSH-compatible public key hashes
188: ```
189: 
190: But a CTK token — first-party or third-party — is only *storage plus SecKey access*. SSH
191: still has to reach it through one of OpenSSH's interfaces, and the only bridge is
192: `ssh-keychain.dylib`, which exposes CTK identities as: RSA → PKCS#11 (useless for SE, see
193: Option 2), **ecdsa256 → "Secure Key module"**, i.e. the FIDO middleware interface. So for
194: SE keys, the CTK route is not an independent option — it is the *enrollment front-end*
195: for Option 4. Building our own extension (app-bundled, Developer-ID signed, sandboxed,
196: CTK entitlement) buys nothing over `sc_auth` for SSH purposes; its value is elsewhere
197: (client certs, VPN, browser mTLS).
198:

200: 
201: ## Option 4 — FIDO middleware (`SecurityKeyProvider`), including Apple's built-in SE path
202: 
203: ### The interface
204: 
205: For `ecdsa-sk`/`ed25519-sk` keys, OpenSSH (client *and* server support since
206: [OpenSSH 8.2](https://www.openssh.org/txt/release-8.2)) talks to authenticators through a
207: dynamically loaded middleware defined by
208: [sk-api.h](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/master/sk-api.h): just four
209: exported functions — `sk_api_version`, `sk_enroll`, `sk_sign`, `sk_load_resident_keys`
210: (current ABI `SSH_SK_VERSION_MAJOR 0x000a0000`), with `SSH_SK_ECDSA` meaning P-256.
211: The key and signature formats are in
212: [PROTOCOL.u2f](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/master/PROTOCOL.u2f):
213: the public key blob adds an `application` string (default `"ssh:"`), and the signature is
214: computed over `SHA256(application) ‖ flags ‖ counter ‖ SHA256(message)` — deliberately
215: **not** the same bytes as a plain `ecdsa-sha2-nistp256` signature. `sshd` checks the
216: user-presence bit in `flags` unless the key's authorized_keys entry says
217: `no-touch-required`, and can demand user verification via `verify-required`
218: ([sshd(8) AUTHORIZED_KEYS options](https://man.openbsd.org/sshd#AUTHORIZED_KEYS_FILE_FORMAT),
219: *verified locally*).
220: 
221: ### Apple already ships an SE-backed sk provider
222: 
223: This is the least-known finding: `/usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib` **is** an sk middleware —
224: it exports `sk_api_version`/`sk_enroll`/`sk_sign`/`sk_load_resident_keys` *(verified
225: locally with `nm`)* — serving "ecdsa256" identities from CTK tokens, including the
226: SE-resident identities `sc_auth create-ctk-identity -k p-256-ne` creates. Apple's ssh
227: build even defaults `SecurityKeyProvider` to `$SSH_SK_PROVIDER` (visible in `ssh -G`
228: output, *verified locally*) instead of stock OpenSSH's internal USB-HID support. The full
229: native flow, per the man pages and a widely-replicated
230: [writeup with working commands](https://gist.github.com/arianvp/5f59f1783e3eaf1a2d4cd8e952bb4acf):
231: 
232: ```sh
233: sc_auth create-ctk-identity -l ssh -k p-256-ne -t bio        # key born in the SE
234: export SSH_SK_PROVIDER=/usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib
235: ssh-keygen -K -N ""       # downloads "resident keys" as key-handle stub files, or:
236: ssh-add -K -S /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib                    # load them into ssh-agent
237: ```
238: 
239: The private-key *file* this produces is only a key handle (that's true of all sk keys —
240: see the `key_handle` field in PROTOCOL.u2f), so it's useless off-machine. Zero
241: third-party software; Touch ID via `-t bio`.
242: 
243: ### Verified end-to-end (see `demo-sk.sh`)
244: 
245: The full flow was exercised live on this machine (macOS 15.7, Apple `OpenSSH_9.9p2`):
246: `sc_auth create-ctk-identity -k p-256-ne` → `ssh-keygen -K` → `ssh-keygen -Y sign`/
247: `verify` → an actual publickey login against a local `sshd`, with the key never leaving
248: the enclave. `demo-sk.sh` scripts it (and deletes its identity afterwards). Findings the
249: documentation doesn't tell you:
250: 
251: - **The user-presence flag is always set.** Apple's `sk_sign` asserts UP even for
252:   `-t none` keys (signatures verify without `no-touch-required` in allowed_signers /
253:   authorized_keys, with no prompt shown). So a server demanding a touch cannot actually
254:   distinguish a policy-free SE key from a `-t bio` one — the flag reflects Apple's
255:   claim, not an enforced gesture. `-t bio` keys pop the system Touch ID sheet on every
256:   signature, including from a plain CLI.
257: - **Enrollment must go through `sc_auth`.** The dylib exports `sk_enroll` but it
258:   returns "requested feature not supported" — `ssh-keygen -t ecdsa-sk -w
259:   /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib` fails; the provider only signs and lists resident keys.
260: - **All identities collide on one filename.** Every CTK ssh identity carries the same
261:   `ssh:` application string, so `ssh-keygen -K` writes each one to `id_ecdsa_sk_rk`,
262:   prompting to overwrite; with several identities, disambiguate by comparing
263:   `ssh-keygen -lf` fingerprints against `sc_auth list-ctk-identities -t ssh`.
264: - **Non-interactive use** of the prompting tools works with
265:   `SSH_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/true SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force`.
266: 
267: ### Structural tradeoffs of the sk route (any provider)
268: 
269: The server must speak the sk key types (OpenSSH ≥ 8.2; some managed git services and old
270: appliances still don't), the key shows up as `sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com` rather
271: than plain ECDSA, and every client that uses the key needs the provider library
272: configured. In exchange you get the flags/counter framing and server-enforceable
273: user-presence — an actual security *upgrade* over the agent route, where the server has
274: no way to know whether a touch policy exists.
275: 
276: For completeness: macOS **passkeys do not intersect** with this. The platform
279: from apps; nothing bridges it to the sk-api, and sk keys are OpenSSH-specific formats,
280: not WebAuthn credentials.
281: 
282: ### Building our own sk provider
283: 
284: Surprisingly tractable, and prior art exists for other enclaves
285: ([sk-sgx](https://github.com/mfriedl/sk-sgx) implements sk-api on Intel SGX). A Swift
286: dylib exporting the four C functions: `sk_enroll` creates a
287: `SecureEnclave.P256.Signing.PrivateKey` and returns the public key with
288: `key_handle = dataRepresentation` — the SE's wrapped-handle model is a *perfect* match
289: for the sk key-handle concept (stateless provider, machine-bound handle); `sk_sign`
290: restores the key from the handle, builds the `SHA256(application) ‖ flags ‖ counter ‖
291: SHA256(message)` blob (all encodable with this repo's `SSHWire.swift`), signs it, and
292: returns flags/counter/r/s. Main new work: the C ABI surface and getting the flag
293: semantics right. Its only real advantage over Apple's built-in provider is controlling
294: the biometry policy and flag reporting ourselves.
295: 
296: ---
297: 
298: ## Comparison
299: 
300: | | 1. Custom/3rd-party agent | 2. PKCS#11 | 3. CTK token ext. | 4a. Apple sk provider | 4b. Own sk provider |
301: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
302: | Status | **Production** (Secretive, maintained) | **Dead end for SE** (Apple bridge is RSA-only) | Real, but for SSH it just feeds 4a | Shipped in macOS (sc_auth + ssh-keychain.dylib) | Feasible, no macOS example yet (sk-sgx as prior art) |
303: | Key type on the wire | `ecdsa-sha2-nistp256` | — | — | `sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com` | same as 4a |
304: | Server requirements | **None** (any sshd) | — | — | OpenSSH ≥ 8.2, touch-flag policy | same |
305: | Client config | `IdentityAgent /path/socket.ssh` | `PKCS11Provider` | none (feeds 4a) | `SSH_SK_PROVIDER=/usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib` + stub key files | `SecurityKeyProvider=/path/lib.dylib` |
306: | Biometry | Agent's choice (Secretive: Touch ID, LAContext batching) | — | `sc_auth -t bio` | `-t bio` (verified: prompt per signature; UP flag set even for `-t none`) | fully in our control |
307: | Certificates | Yes (agent lists cert identities) | — | — | sk-cert types exist; untested with Apple's provider | possible |
308: | Agent forwarding | Yes (it *is* the agent) | n/a | n/a | via ssh-agent holding the stub key | same |
309: | Effort on top of this repo | **Low** (socket + 2 messages) | Very high | High (signed app extension) | **Zero code** | Medium (C ABI + sk blob format) |
310: 
311: ## Recommendation
312: 
313: **(a) Daily driver today: Secretive**, with the Apple-native `sc_auth` + `ssh-keychain.dylib`
314: sk route as the zero-install alternative when every server you touch runs OpenSSH ≥ 8.2.
315: Secretive wins on maturity, works against any server because it emits plain
316: `ecdsa-sha2-nistp256`, handles certificates, forwards, and has a sane biometry UX. The
317: Apple-native route is remarkably underdocumented but is the only option requiring no
318: third-party trust at all.
319: 
320: **(b) Next PoC here: the minimal ssh-agent.** It is the natural continuation of this
321: repo: RFC 9987's two required message handlers on a unix socket, reusing `SSHWire.swift`
322: and `SSHKeys.swift` unchanged, with the existing `create-ca --require-biometry` machinery
323: providing the Touch ID story — and it uniquely lets us demo the full loop of *our own SE
324: CA certifying our own SE authentication key* by serving the cert as a second identity. A
325: follow-up stretch goal with real novelty would be 4b, an SE-backed sk provider, since the
326: `dataRepresentation`-as-key-handle correspondence makes it unusually clean and nobody

Key findings (with sources)
- Apple’s bundled OpenSSH on macOS is often compiled without the security‑key provider (libfido2) middleware, so the system ssh/ssh-keygen may advertise SK key types but still fail to use real FIDO2 hardware. ([github.com](https://github.com/Yubico/libfido2/issues/464))
- Many macOS users work around this by building the OpenSSH "Security Key Provider" (sk‑libfido2.dylib) from OpenSSH Portable source and linking it to the system client, or by installing OpenSSH/libfido2 via Homebrew. There are several publicly‑shared scripts and gists that automate building/installing sk‑libfido2.dylib for macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon). ```text
- **Author/date:** stoggi opened the issue on **November 14, 2021**. It is marked closed; no closure date appears in the supplied content.
- **Apple’s bundled components:** The issue identifies macOS Monterey 12.0.1 as shipping OpenSSH **8.6p1** with LibreSSL **2.8.3**.
- **Missing built-in provider:** The author says Apple compiled OpenSSH `without --with-security-key-builtin`, so its native FIDO2 security-key support is absent.
- **Version detection:** The page states the component versions directly, but gives no version-detection command or procedure.
- **Misleading key listing:** The supplied content does **not** mention `ssh -Q key`, so it provides no evidence about whether that command misleadingly lists `ecdsa-sk` or `ed25519-sk`.
- **Observed mismatch:** Although the bundled manual pages apparently describe those key types, enrollment fails with: **“Key enrollment failed: unknown or unsupported key type”**
- **External-provider distinction:** The issue separates built-in support from an external `sk-libfido2` provider. It says that middleware was removed from libfido2 1.3.1 after related functionality entered OpenSSH, while an external provider could still connect bundled OpenSSH tools to a YubiKey.
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1: // KeyStore.swift — Secure Enclave key discovery and signing
2: //
3: // Part of EnclaveAgent — a minimal SSH agent for sc_auth Secure Enclave keys.
4: // Keys are created/managed externally via sc_auth:
5: //   sc_auth create-ctk-identity -l "my-key" -k p-256-ne -t bio
6: //   sc_auth list-ctk-identities -t ssh
7: //   sc_auth delete-ctk-identity -h <hash>
8: 
9: import Foundation
10: import Security
11: import CryptoKit
12: 
13: // MARK: - Key model
14: 
15: struct EnclaveKey {
16:     let privateKey: SecKey
17:     let ecPoint: Data      // 65-byte uncompressed P-256 EC point (0x04 + X + Y)
18:     let keyBlob: Data      // OpenSSH wire-format key blob
19:     let label: String
20: }
21: 
22: // MARK: - Key discovery
23: 
24: /// Query keychain for sc_auth-managed CryptoTokenKit keys and return usable P-256 keys.
25: /// Returns an empty array if no keys found — caller should print help and exit.
26: func loadKeys() -> [EnclaveKey] {
27:     let query: [String: Any] = [
28:         kSecClass as String:            kSecClassKey,
29:         kSecAttrKeyType as String:      kSecAttrKeyTypeECSECPrimeRandom,
30:         kSecAttrTokenID as String:      "com.apple.ctkcard:user", // keys created by sc_auth have this token ID
31:         kSecReturnRef as String:        true,
32:         kSecReturnAttributes as String: true,
33:         kSecMatchLimit as String:       kSecMatchLimitAll,
34:     ]
35: 
36:     var result: CFTypeRef?
37:     let status = SecItemCopyMatching(query as CFDictionary, &result)
38: 
39:     if status == errSecItemNotFound {
40:         return []
41:     }
42:     if status != errSecSuccess {
43:         print("keychain query error: \(status)")
44:         return []
45:     }
46: 
47:     // Normalize result to array of dictionaries
48:     let items: [[String: Any]]
49:     if let arr = result as? [[String: Any]] {
50:         items = arr
54:         return []
55:     }
56: 
57:     var keys: [EnclaveKey] = []
58:     for attrs in items {
59:         let label = attrs[kSecAttrLabel as String] as? String ?? "unknown"
60:         guard let ref = attrs[kSecValueRef as String] else {
61:             print("  skip \(label): no key reference")
62:             continue
63:         }
64:         // SecKey is a CFTypeRef — verify the type ID before using it
65:         guard CFGetTypeID(ref as CFTypeRef) == SecKeyGetTypeID() else {
66:             print("  skip \(label): invalid key reference")
67:             continue
68:         }
69:         let privateKey = ref as! SecKey
70: 
71:         guard let pubKey = SecKeyCopyPublicKey(privateKey) else {
72:             print("  skip \(label): no public key")
73:             continue
74:         }
75: 
76:         var error: Unmanaged<CFError>?
77:         guard let ecPoint = SecKeyCopyExternalRepresentation(pubKey, &error) as Data? else {
78:             print("  skip \(label): can't export public key")
79:             continue
80:         }
81: 
82:         // We only support P-256 uncompressed points: 0x04 + 32-byte X + 32-byte Y = 65 bytes
83:         guard ecPoint.count == 65, ecPoint[ecPoint.startIndex] == 0x04 else {
84:             print("  skip \(label): unsupported key format (\(ecPoint.count) bytes, expected 65-byte P-256 point)")
85:             continue
86:         }
87: 
88:         let keyBlob = opensshKeyBlob(ecPoint: ecPoint)
89:         keys.append(EnclaveKey(privateKey: privateKey, ecPoint: ecPoint, keyBlob: keyBlob, label: label))
90:         print("  loaded key: \(label)")
91:     }
92: 
93:     return keys
94: }
95: 
96: // MARK: - OpenSSH key blob
97: 
98: /// Build an OpenSSH wire-format key blob for an ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 key.
99: func opensshKeyBlob(ecPoint: Data) -> Data {
100:     var blob = Data()
101:     blob.append("ecdsa-sha2-nistp256".sshString)
102:     blob.append("nistp256".sshString)
103:     blob.append(ecPoint.sshString)
104:     return blob
105: }
106: 
107: /// Format an authorized_keys line for a P-256 key.
108: func authorizedKeysLine(ecPoint: Data, comment: String) -> String {
109:     let blob = opensshKeyBlob(ecPoint: ecPoint)
110:     return "ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 \(blob.base64EncodedString()) enclave:\(comment)"
111: }
112: 
113: // MARK: - Signing
114: 
115: /// Sign data with a Secure Enclave key, returning an OpenSSH-formatted signature.
116: /// This triggers Touch ID if the key was created with biometric protection.
117: func signWithKey(_ key: SecKey, data: Data) throws -> Data {
118:     var error: Unmanaged<CFError>?
119:     guard let derSig = SecKeyCreateSignature(
120:         key, .ecdsaSignatureMessageX962SHA256, data as CFData, &error
121:     ) as Data? else {
122:         let msg = error.map { String(describing: $0.takeRetainedValue()) } ?? "unknown error"
123:         throw AgentError.signFailed(msg)
124:     }
125: 
126:     // Use CryptoKit to parse DER → raw 64-byte r||s
127:     let signature = try P256.Signing.ECDSASignature(derRepresentation: derSig)
128:     return opensshSignature(rawRS: signature.rawRepresentation)
129: }
```

package sshvault

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"crypto/ed25519"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"

	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh"
)

const (
	bwUser = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
	bwItem = "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222"
	opAccount = "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"
	opUser = "bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb"
	opVault = "cccccccccccccccccccccccccc"
	opItem = "dddddddddddddddddddddddddd"
	privateSentinel = "PRIVATE_RESPONSE_MUST_NOT_ESCAPE"
	sessionSentinel = "SESSION_RESPONSE_MUST_NOT_ESCAPE"
)

type runStep struct {
	name string
	args []string
	body any
	run func(context.Context, []byte) ([]byte, error)
}

type scriptedRunner struct {
	t *testing.T
	steps []runStep
	calls int
	outputs [][]byte
	inputs [][]byte
}

func (runner *scriptedRunner) Run(ctx context.Context, name string, args []string, input []byte) ([]byte, error) {
	runner.t.Helper()
	if runner.calls >= len(runner.steps) {
		runner.t.Fatal("unexpected provider command")
	}
	step := runner.steps[runner.calls]
	runner.calls++
	if name != step.name || !reflect.DeepEqual(args, step.args) {
		runner.t.Fatalf("provider command metadata mismatch at step %d", runner.calls)
	}
	for _, arg := range args {
		if strings.Contains(arg, privateSentinel) || strings.Contains(arg, sessionSentinel) || strings.Contains(arg, "PRIVATE KEY") {
			runner.t.Fatal("secret in provider argv")
		}
	}
	if len(input) > 0 {
		runner.inputs = append(runner.inputs, input)
		if name != "bw" || !reflect.DeepEqual(args, []string{"create", "item"}) {
			runner.t.Fatal("unexpected stdin")
		}
	}
	var body []byte
	var err error
	if step.run != nil {
		body, err = step.run(ctx, input)
	} else if text, ok := step.body.(string); ok {
		body = []byte(text)
	} else {
		body, err = json.Marshal(step.body)
	}
	runner.outputs = append(runner.outputs, body)
	return body, err
}

func (runner *scriptedRunner) verify(t *testing.T) {
	t.Helper()
	if runner.calls != len(runner.steps) {
		t.Fatalf("provider calls = %d, want %d", runner.calls, len(runner.steps))
	}
	for _, bodies := range [][][]byte{runner.outputs, runner.inputs} {
		for _, body := range bodies {
			for _, b := range body {
				if b != 0 {
					t.Fatal("provider response or secret stdin was not wiped")
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

func bwRequest() Request {
	return Request{Provider: Bitwarden, Title: "test SSH key", Experimental: true}
}

func opRequest() Request {
	return Request{Provider: OnePassword, Title: "test SSH key", VaultID: opVault}
}

func bwStatus() map[string]any {
	return map[string]any{"status": "unlocked", "userId": bwUser, "serverUrl": "https://vault.example.test", "userEmail": sessionSentinel}
}

func bwObservation(status any) []runStep {
	return []runStep{{name: "bw", args: []string{"--version"}, body: BitwardenSchemaVersion + "\n"}, {name: "bw", args: []string{"status"}, body: status}}
}

func opObservation(account string) []runStep {
	whoami := []string{"whoami", "--format", "json"}
	if account != "" {
		whoami = append(whoami, "--account", account)
	}
	return []runStep{
		{name: "op", args: []string{"--version"}, body: "2.20.0\n"},
		{name: "op", args: whoami, body: map[string]any{"account_uuid": opAccount, "user_uuid": opUser, "url": "example.1password.com", "email": sessionSentinel}},
		{name: "op", args: []string{"vault", "get", opVault, "--account", opAccount, "--format", "json"}, body: map[string]any{"id": opVault, "name": "Test vault"}},
	}
}

func fixturePublic(t *testing.T) (string, string) {
	t.Helper()
	key, err := ssh.NewPublicKey(ed25519.PublicKey(bytes.Repeat([]byte{7}, ed25519.PublicKeySize)))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal("construct public fixture")
	}
	return strings.TrimSpace(string(ssh.MarshalAuthorizedKey(key))), ssh.FingerprintSHA256(key)
}

func assertPublicOnly(t *testing.T, value any, err error) {
	t.Helper()
	body, marshalErr := json.Marshal(value)
	if marshalErr != nil {
		t.Fatal("marshal public result")
	}
	text := string(body)
	if err != nil {
		text += err.Error()
	}
	for _, secret := range []string{privateSentinel, sessionSentinel, "PRIVATE KEY", "privateKey", "private_key", "BW_SESSION", "OP_SESSION"} {
		if strings.Contains(text, secret) {
			t.Fatal("secret or private field leaked into result")
		}
	}
}

		{Provider: OnePassword, Title: "test", VaultID: opVault, AccountID: "--account"},

		request := bwRequest()

		requests = append(requests, request)
	}
	for i, request := range requests {
		runner := &scriptedRunner{t: t}
		_, err := NewService(runner).Plan(context.Background(), request)
		if !errors.Is(err, ErrUnsafe) && !errors.Is(err, ErrExperimental) {
			t.Fatalf("request %d not rejected", i)
		}
		runner.verify(t)
	}
}

		{"malformed", "invalid JSON " + privateSentinel, ErrUnavailable},
		{"missing-user", map[string]any{"status": "unlocked", "serverUrl": "https://vault.example.test"}, ErrUnavailable},
		{"cloud-null", map[string]any{"status": "unlocked", "serverUrl": nil, "userId": bwUser}, ErrUnsupportedContext},
		{"cloud-missing", map[string]any{"status": "unlocked", "userId": bwUser}, ErrUnsupportedContext},
		{"unsafe-url", map[string]any{"status": "unlocked", "userId": bwUser, "serverUrl": "https://user:password@vault.example.test"}, ErrUnavailable},
	} {

		if _, err := NewService(runner).Plan(context.Background(), bwRequest()); !errors.Is(err, ErrUnsupportedVersion) {
