func TestPlanAuthorityRejectsTamperingAndDeserialization(t *testing.T) {
	runner := &scriptedRunner{t: t, steps: bwObservation(bwStatus())}
	service := NewService(runner)
	plan, err := service.Plan(context.Background(), bwRequest())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	assertPublicOnly(t, plan, nil)
	for _, mutate := range []func(*Plan){
		func(p *Plan) { p.Title = "different" },
		func(p *Plan) { p.Version = "2026.3.1" },
		func(p *Plan) { p.Experimental = false },
		func(p *Plan) { p.Destination.Provider = OnePassword },
		func(p *Plan) { p.Destination.AccountID = bwItem },
		func(p *Plan) { p.Destination.UserID = bwItem },
		func(p *Plan) { p.Destination.ServerURL = "https://different.example.test" },
		func(p *Plan) { p.Destination.VaultID = "other" },
		func(p *Plan) { p.Destination.VaultName = "other" },
		func(p *Plan) { p.state = nil },
	} {
		changed := plan
		mutate(&changed)
		result, err := service.Apply(context.Background(), changed)
		if !errors.Is(err, ErrStale) || result.Status != StatusNotStarted {
			t.Fatal("tampered plan accepted")
		}
	}
	body, _ := json.Marshal(plan)
	var decoded Plan
	if json.Unmarshal(body, &decoded) != nil {
		t.Fatal("decode public plan")
	}
	if _, err := service.Apply(context.Background(), decoded); !errors.Is(err, ErrStale) {
		t.Fatal("serialized plan acquired authority")
	}
	otherRunner := &scriptedRunner{t: t}
	if _, err := NewService(otherRunner).Apply(context.Background(), plan); !errors.Is(err, ErrStale) {
		t.Fatal("foreign service accepted plan")
	}
	otherRunner.verify(t)
	runner.verify(t)
}

	}
}

func TestPlanCanOnlyAttemptOneMutationConcurrently(t *testing.T) {
	steps := append(bwObservation(bwStatus()), bwObservation(bwStatus())...)
	steps = append(steps, successfulBWCreate(t, nil))
	steps = append(steps, bwObservation(bwStatus())...)
	runner := &scriptedRunner{t: t, steps: steps}
	service := NewService(runner)
	plan, err := service.Plan(context.Background(), bwRequest())
	if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
	var wait sync.WaitGroup
	outcomes := make(chan error, 2)
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		wait.Add(1)
		go func() { defer wait.Done(); _, err := service.Apply(context.Background(), plan); outcomes <- err }()
	}
	wait.Wait()
	close(outcomes)
	created, refused := 0, 0
	for err := range outcomes { if err == nil { created++ } else if errors.Is(err, ErrPlanUsed) { refused++ } else { t.Fatal("unexpected concurrent apply outcome") } }
	if created != 1 || refused != 1 { t.Fatal("plan was not single-use") }
	runner.verify(t)
}

1	# Example: CLI tool
2	
3	CLIs are the simplest case - there's usually no background process to

1	# Example: TUI / interactive terminal app
2	
3	Interactive terminal apps (text editors, REPLs, curses-based UIs) can't
4	be driven directly by an agent's bash tool - they take over the terminal.
5	The skill must show how to wrap them in `tmux` so the agent can send
6	input, capture output, and take screenshots.
7	
8	## The tmux pattern
9	
10	This is the standard approach:
11	
12	1. Start the TUI inside a detached tmux session
13	2. Send keystrokes with `tmux send-keys`
14	3. Read screen contents with `tmux capture-pane`
15	4. Clean up with `tmux kill-session`
16	
17	The skill's `SKILL.md` should present this as the primary way to drive
18	the app. A small `driver.sh` that wraps the launch+attach sequence can
19	live in the skill directory, but for most TUIs the raw tmux commands in
20	the skill body are enough.
21	
22	## Example snippet
23	
24	> ## Run (interactive, for agents)
25	>
26	> Start the TUI inside tmux:
27	>
28	> ```bash
29	> tmux new-session -d -s app -x 120 -y 40 './myapp'
30	> ```
31	>
32	> Poll until the ready marker appears (faster + more reliable than a fixed sleep -
33	> returns the instant the app is up, fails loudly if it isn't):
34	>
35	> ```bash
36	> timeout 10 bash -c 'until tmux capture-pane -t app -p | grep -q "Ready"; do sleep 0.2; done'
37	> tmux capture-pane -t app -p
38	> ```
39	>
40	> Send input (this example navigates to the Settings screen and toggles
41	> an option):
42	>
43	> ```bash
44	> tmux send-keys -t app 's'
45	> timeout 5 bash -c 'until tmux capture-pane -t app -p | grep -q "Settings"; do sleep 0.2; done'
46	> tmux send-keys -t app 'Down' 'Down' 'Space'  # navigate + toggle
47	> timeout 5 bash -c 'until tmux capture-pane -t app -p | grep -qF "[x]"; do sleep 0.2; done'
48	> tmux capture-pane -t app -p
49	> ```
50	>
51	> If you find yourself writing more than a couple of these poll lines, pull
52	> them into a `wait_for()` helper in a `driver.sh` next to the skill.
53	>
54	> Quit:
55	>
56	> ```bash
57	> tmux send-keys -t app 'q'
58	> tmux kill-session -t app 2>/dev/null || true
59	> ```
60	>
61	> ### Key reference
62	>
63	> | Key | Action |
64	> |---|---|
65	> | `j` / `k` or `Down` / `Up` | Navigate list |
66	> | `Enter` | Select |
67	> | `s` | Settings |
68	> | `q` | Quit |
69	
70	## Details worth documenting
71	
72	- **Terminal size.** Some TUIs break or hide content at small widths.
73	  Specify a known-good size in the `tmux new-session -x -y` args.
74	- **Startup time.** Poll for a ready marker (`until tmux capture-pane | grep -q X`)
75	  rather than a fixed `sleep N` - returns the instant the app is up, and fails
76	  usefully when it never does. Say what string means ready.
77	- **Keybinding reference.** A table of the main keys. This is the "API"
78	  of a TUI - an agent needs it to drive the app.
79	- **Exit cleanly.** Show the quit keystroke *and* `tmux kill-session` as
80	  a fallback.
81	- **Color/unicode quirks.** If `capture-pane` output is hard to read,
82	  note flags that help (`-e` for escape sequences, `-J` to join wrapped
83	  lines).
84	
85	## Also document the direct invocation
86	
87	For a human running the app interactively, tmux is overkill. Include
88	the one-liner too:
89	
90	> ## Run (direct, for humans)
91	>
92	> ```bash
93	> ./myapp
94	> ```
95	>
96	> Press `q` to quit.
97

18: of "user presence" for each signature operation (typically achieved
19: by requiring the user touch the key). They also offer an attestation

21: given key is backed by hardware. Finally the signature format includes
22: a monotonic signature counter that can be used (at scale) to detect
23: concurrent use of a private key, should it be extracted from hardware.
24: 
25: U2F private keys are generated through an enrollment operation,
26: which takes an application ID - a URL-like string, typically "ssh:"
27: in this case, but a HTTP origin for the case of web authentication,
28: and a challenge string (typically randomly generated). The enrollment
29: operation returns a public key, a key handle that must be used to invoke
30: the hardware-backed private key, some flags and signed attestation
31: information that may be used to verify that a private key is hosted on a
32: particular hardware instance.
33: 
34: It is common for U2F hardware to derive private keys from the key handle
35: in conjunction with a small per-device secret that is unique to the
36: hardware, thus requiring little on-device storage for an effectively
37: unlimited number of supported keys. This drives the requirement that
38: the key handle be supplied for each signature operation. U2F tokens
39: primarily use ECDSA signatures in the NIST-P256 field, though the FIDO2
40: standard specifies additional key types, including one based on Ed25519.
41: 
42: Use of U2F security keys does not automatically imply multi-factor
43: authentication. From sshd's perspective, a security key constitutes a
44: single factor of authentication, even if protected by a PIN or biometric
45: authentication.  To enable multi-factor authentication in ssh, please
55: 	sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256-cert-v01@openssh.com
56: 	sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com
57: 	sk-ssh-ed25519-cert-v01@openssh.com

59: While each uses ecdsa-sha256-nistp256 as the underlying signature primitive,
60: keys require extra information in the public and private keys, and in

63: 
64: The format of a sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com public key is:
65: 
66: 	string		"sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com"
67: 	string		curve name
68: 	ec_point	Q
69: 	string		application (user-specified, but typically "ssh:")
70: 
71: The corresponding private key contains:
72: 
73: 	string		"sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com"
74: 	string		curve name
75: 	ec_point	Q
76: 	string		application (user-specified, but typically "ssh:")
77: 	uint8		flags
78: 	string		key_handle
79: 	string		reserved

82: 
83: 	string		"sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com"
84: 	string		public key
85: 	string		application (user-specified, but typically "ssh:")
86: 
87: With a private half consisting of:
88: 
89: 	string		"sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com"
90: 	string		public key
91: 	string		application (user-specified, but typically "ssh:")
92: 	uint8		flags
93: 	string		key_handle
94: 	string		reserved
95:

99: 	string		"sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256-cert-v01@openssh.com"
100: 	string		nonce
101: 	string		curve name
102: 	ec_point	Q
103: 	string		application

111: 	string		extensions
112: 	string		reserved

119: 	string		nonce
120: 	string		public key

//go:build unix

package cli

import (
	"bytes"

)

type sshAgentSetupRunner struct {
	base      *sshCLIRunner
	agents    map[string][]byte
	effective map[string][]byte
	calls     []sshhost.RunRequest
	proofs    []string
}

func (r *sshAgentSetupRunner) Run(ctx context.Context, request sshhost.RunRequest) (sshhost.RunResult, error) {
	r.calls = append(r.calls, request)
	if request.Name == "ssh-add" {
		socket := ""
		for _, value := range request.Env {
			if strings.HasPrefix(value, "SSH_AUTH_SOCK=") {
				socket = strings.TrimPrefix(value, "SSH_AUTH_SOCK=")
			}
		}
		if key, ok := r.agents[socket]; ok {
			return sshhost.RunResult{Stdout: key}, nil
		}
		return sshhost.RunResult{ExitCode: 1}, nil
	}
	if request.Name == "ssh" && hasSSHArg(request.Args, "-G") {
		if effective, ok := r.effective[sshArgValue(request.Args, "-G")]; ok {
			return sshhost.RunResult{Stdout: effective}, nil
		}
	}
	if request.Display == "ssh selected-key-only authentication proof" {
		body, err := os.ReadFile(sshArgValue(request.Args, "-F"))
		if err != nil {
			return sshhost.RunResult{}, err
		}
		r.proofs = append(r.proofs, string(body))
	}
	return r.base.Run(ctx, request)
}

func newSSHAgentSetupFixture(t *testing.T) (*App, *sshCLIFixture, *sshAgentSetupRunner) {
	t.Helper()
	f := newSSHCLIFixture(t)
	home, err := os.MkdirTemp("/tmp", "dev-agent-home-")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = os.RemoveAll(home) })
	home, err = filepath.EvalSymlinks(home)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	f.home, f.runner.home = home, home
	f.configPath = filepath.Join(home, "config.toml")
	f.remotesPath = filepath.Join(home, ".config", "dev", "remotes.toml")
	for key, value := range map[string]string{
		"HOME": home, "USERPROFILE": home,
		"XDG_CONFIG_HOME": filepath.Join(home, ".config"),
		"XDG_DATA_HOME": filepath.Join(home, ".local", "share"),
		"XDG_CACHE_HOME": filepath.Join(home, ".cache"),
		"SSH_AUTH_SOCK": "",
	} {
		t.Setenv(key, value)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(f.configPath, []byte("[runtime]\nbackend = \"none\"\n"), 0600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	f.initSSH()
	runner := &sshAgentSetupRunner{base: f.runner, agents: map[string][]byte{}, effective: map[string][]byte{}}
	app := &App{Cfg: config.Default(), In: strings.NewReader(""), Out: io.Discard, Err: io.Discard, remotesPath: f.remotesPath, sshHostRunner: runner, interactiveCheck: func() bool { return false }}
	return app, f, runner
}

func listenSSHAgentAt(t *testing.T, path string) {
	t.Helper()
	listener, err := net.Listen("unix", path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = listener.Close() })
}

func TestSSHAgentSetupApplyKeepsProviderAfterPublicCopy(t *testing.T) {
	_, f, runner := newSSHAgentSetupFixture(t)
	socket := filepath.Join(f.home, "selected agent.sock")
	listenSSHAgentAt(t, socket)
	runner.agents[socket] = f.runner.publicLine
	ambient := filepath.Join(f.home, "ambient.sock")
	listenSSHAgentAt(t, ambient)
	t.Setenv("SSH_AUTH_SOCK", ambient)
	runner.agents[ambient] = sshCLITestPublicLine(0x18, "other-agent-key")
	metadata, err := sshhost.ParsePublicKey(f.runner.publicLine)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, alias := range []string{"first", "second", "first"} {
		args := []string{"ssh", "setup", alias, "--hostname", alias + ".example", "--identity-agent", socket, "--key", metadata.Fingerprint, "--target-os", "posix", "--yes", "--json"}
		out, stderr, err := runSSHCLIWithRunner(t, f, runner, args...)
		if err != nil || assertOneSSHJSON(t, out)["status"] != "ready" {
			t.Fatalf("%s: %v\n%s\n%s", alias, err, out, stderr)
		}
		body, err := os.ReadFile(f.managedPath(alias))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		definition, err := sshhost.ParseManaged(body)
		if err != nil || !strings.HasPrefix(string(body), sshhost.ManagedHeaderV2+"\n") || definition.IdentityAgent != socket || definition.IdentitiesOnly == nil || !*definition.IdentitiesOnly || !strings.HasSuffix(definition.IdentityFile, "dev_agent_custom_"+alias+".pub") {
			t.Fatalf("provider intent lost: %+v %v", definition, err)
		}
		if _, err := os.Stat(strings.TrimSuffix(definition.IdentityFile, ".pub")); !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
			t.Fatalf("agent selection created a private file: %v", err)
		}
	}
	if len(runner.proofs) < 3 {
		t.Fatal("successful setup never reached the real exact-proof adapter")
	}
	for _, proof := range runner.proofs {
		if !strings.Contains(proof, socket) || !strings.Contains(proof, "IdentityAgent") {
			t.Fatalf("proof lost selected socket: %s", proof)
		}
	}
	for _, call := range runner.calls {
		if call.Name == "ssh-keygen" {
			t.Fatal("agent-only setup invoked private key generation/derivation")
		}
	}
}

func TestSSHAgentSelectionIgnoresDuplicatePrivateFile(t *testing.T) {
	app, f, runner := newSSHAgentSetupFixture(t)
	private := writeSSHCLIKey(t, f, "local-copy")
	socket := filepath.Join(f.home, "agent.sock")
	listenSSHAgentAt(t, socket)
	runner.agents[socket] = f.runner.publicLine
	service, err := app.sshHosts()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	candidate, err := selectSSHAgentKey(t.Context(), service, sshhost.AgentSocketRef{Provider: sshhost.AgentProviderCustom, Socket: socket}, private+".pub")
	if err != nil || candidate.Agent == nil || candidate.Provenance.Private || candidate.Provenance.SecurityKeyStub || candidate.NeedsPermissionRepair {
		t.Fatalf("explicit agent selection retained private authority: %+v %v", candidate, err)
	}
	if _, err := selectSSHAgentKey(t.Context(), service, *candidate.Agent, private); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("--identity-agent accepted a private path instead of public metadata")
	}
	for _, call := range runner.calls {
		if call.Name == "ssh-keygen" {
			t.Fatal("agent selection touched private identity")
		}
	}
}

func TestSSHTUIAgentPublicCopyReviewAndApply(t *testing.T) {
	if runtime.GOOS != "darwin" && runtime.GOOS != "linux" {
		t.Skip("Bitwarden socket discovery is available on macOS and Linux")
	}
	app, f, runner := newSSHAgentSetupFixture(t)
	socket := filepath.Join(f.home, ".bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock")
	listenSSHAgentAt(t, socket)
	runner.agents[socket] = f.runner.publicLine
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(f.home, ".ssh", "existing-public.pub"), f.runner.publicLine, 0600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	choices, err := listSSHTUIKeys(t.Context(), app, "lab")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var selected tui.SSHKeyChoice
	for _, choice := range choices {
		if choice.AgentSocket == socket {
			selected = choice
		}
	}
	if selected.Fingerprint == "" || selected.Path != "" {
		t.Fatalf("TUI lost agent authority for local public copy: %+v", choices)
	}
	request := sshflow.OnboardRequest{Alias: "lab", HostName: "lab.example", User: "tester", Port: 22, Auth: "key", RemoteOS: "posix", KeyFingerprint: selected.Fingerprint, KeyAgentSocket: selected.AgentSocket}
	plan, err := prepareSSHTUIOnboarding(t.Context(), app, request)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	public := filepath.Join(f.home, ".ssh", "dev_agent_bitwarden_lab.pub")
	preview := strings.Join(plan.Preview().Notes, "\n")
	for _, expected := range []string{socket, public, "Public key only: create", "Managed SSH v2", "IdentitiesOnly yes", "v0.2.37"} {
		if !strings.Contains(preview, expected) {
			t.Fatalf("review omits %q: %s", expected, preview)
		}
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(public); !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
		t.Fatal("TUI preparation published key before approval")
	}
	workflow := &sshTUIWorkflow{ctx: t.Context(), app: *app, request: tui.SSHWorkflowRequest{Action: "onboard", Onboarding: plan}}
	if err := workflow.Run(); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	result := workflow.Result().Onboarding
	if result == nil || result.Status != "ready" || !result.Keys["lab"].Created || !result.Configurations["lab"].Changed {
		t.Fatalf("TUI lost real apply results: %+v", result)
	}
	body, err := os.ReadFile(f.managedPath("lab"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	definition, err := sshhost.ParseManaged(body)
	if err != nil || definition.IdentityAgent != socket || definition.IdentityFile != public {
		t.Fatalf("TUI apply differs from review: %+v %v", definition, err)
	}
	if len(runner.proofs) == 0 || !strings.Contains(runner.proofs[0], socket) {
		t.Fatal("TUI agent selection never reached selected-socket proof")
	}
}

func TestSSHAgentForeignMatchingPolicyDoesNotRewrite(t *testing.T) {
	app, f, runner := newSSHAgentSetupFixture(t)
	socket := filepath.Join(f.home, "agent.sock")
	listenSSHAgentAt(t, socket)
	runner.agents[socket] = f.runner.publicLine
	public := filepath.Join(f.home, ".ssh", "foreign.pub")
	if err := os.WriteFile(public, f.runner.publicLine, 0600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	f.appendRootConfig(fmt.Sprintf("Host foreign\n    HostName foreign.example\n    User tester\n    IdentityAgent %s\n    IdentityFile %s\n    IdentitiesOnly yes\n", socket, public))
	runner.effective["foreign"] = []byte(fmt.Sprintf("hostname foreign.example\nuser tester\nport 22\nproxyjump none\nproxycommand none\nidentityagent %s\nidentityfile %s\nidentitiesonly yes\n", socket, public))
	before, err := os.ReadFile(f.rootConfigPath())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	metadata, err := sshhost.ParsePublicKey(f.runner.publicLine)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	out, stderr, err := runSSHCLIWithRunner(t, f, runner, "ssh", "setup", "foreign", "--identity-agent", socket, "--key", metadata.Fingerprint, "--target-os", "posix", "--yes", "--json")
	if err != nil || assertOneSSHJSON(t, out)["status"] != "ready" {
		t.Fatalf("compatible foreign alias blocked: %v\n%s\n%s", err, out, stderr)
	}
	after, err := os.ReadFile(f.rootConfigPath())
	if err != nil || !bytes.Equal(before, after) {
		t.Fatal("foreign configuration was rewritten")
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(f.managedPath("foreign")); !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
		t.Fatal("foreign alias acquired a managed override")
	}
	profile := sshTUIProfileFor(t, app, "foreign")
	plan, err := prepareSSHTUIOnboarding(t.Context(), app, sshflow.OnboardRequest{Profile: &profile, Alias: "foreign", Auth: "key", RemoteOS: "posix", KeyFingerprint: metadata.Fingerprint, KeyAgentSocket: socket})
	if err != nil || !strings.Contains(strings.Join(plan.Preview().Notes, "\n"), "no SSH configuration or public key file will be written") {
		t.Fatalf("TUI matching foreign review: %v", err)
	}
	// Changing the effective policy after review must stop before any apply stage.
	runner.effective["foreign"] = []byte("hostname foreign.example\nuser tester\nport 22\nproxyjump none\nproxycommand none\nidentityagent none\nidentitiesonly yes\n")
	workflow := &sshTUIWorkflow{ctx: t.Context(), app: *app, request: tui.SSHWorkflowRequest{Action: "onboard", Onboarding: plan}}
	if err := workflow.Run(); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("foreign policy change after review was accepted")
	}
}

func TestSSHAgentOptionsRejectedBeforeSourceOrKeyOperations(t *testing.T) {
	for _, flags := range [][]string{
		{"--to", "fleet", "--generate-key", "--no-passphrase"},
		{"--from", "lan:192.0.2.1:22", "--config-only"},
		{"--to", "both", "--auth", "existing"},
		{"--from", "fleet:gateway/target", "--key", "SHA256:test"},
		{"--identity-file", "/tmp/other.pub", "--key", "SHA256:test"},
		{"--identities-only=false", "--key", "SHA256:test"},
	} {
		t.Run(strings.Join(flags, "_"), func(t *testing.T) {
			_, f, runner := newSSHAgentSetupFixture(t)
			args := append([]string{"ssh", "setup", "lab", "--identity-agent", "bitwarden", "--target-os", "posix", "--yes", "--json"}, flags...)
			_, _, err := runSSHCLIWithRunner(t, f, runner, args...)
			if err == nil || len(runner.calls) != 0 {
				t.Fatalf("conflicting provider flags ran operations: %v %+v", err, runner.calls)
			}
			if _, err := os.Stat(f.managedPath("lab")); !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
				t.Fatal("invalid agent flags wrote a managed alias")
			}
		})
	}
	_, f, runner := newSSHAgentSetupFixture(t)
	if _, _, err := runSSHCLIWithRunner(t, f, runner, "ssh", "key", "list", "--no-agent", "--agent", "bitwarden", "--json"); err == nil || len(runner.calls) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("--no-agent and --agent were not rejected before querying sources")
	}
}

func TestSSHFleetNamedAgentPlansBlockedBeforeApply(t *testing.T) {
	app, _, _ := newSSHAgentSetupFixture(t)
	for _, hop := range []bool{false, true} {
		item := sshOnboardItem{Import: &sshflow.FleetImportPlan{}}
		key := sshhost.KeyPlan{Agent: &sshhost.AgentSocketRef{Provider: sshhost.AgentProviderCustom, Socket: "/not-queried.sock"}}
		if hop {
			item.HopKeyPlans = map[string]sshhost.KeyPlan{"hop": key}
		} else {
			item.KeyPlan = &key
		}
		if _, err := planSSHOnboardItems(t.Context(), app, []sshOnboardItem{item}, false); !errors.Is(err, errSSHFleetImportAgent) {
			t.Fatalf("named agent import plan accepted: %v", err)
		}
		if _, err := applySSHFleetImportConfiguration(t.Context(), app, nil, item, nil); !errors.Is(err, errSSHFleetImportAgent) {
			t.Fatalf("named agent import apply was not blocked first: %v", err)
		}
	}
}

```text
Browse and act on your work in progress.

Shows exactly what "dev ls" shows, from the same code path, plus the ability
to open, park and annotate a task without retyping its name.

Eight lists, switched with tab:

  TASKS   change streams dev is tracking — what am I working on
  REPOS   durable repositories under the scan roots — what do I have here
  FLEET   repositories and active work across configured SSH machines
  TRY     scratch experiments and retained lifecycle history
  REMOTE  repositories visible through configured forge CLIs — what can I clone/open
  SKILLS  startup-context/global agent skills; A toggles all repositories
  MCP     startup-context static declarations; A toggles all repositories
  SSH     machine identities, aliases, cached Tailscale/LAN discovery and connections

Navigation is vim-style, with arrows and mouse alongside:

  j k        move                 ctrl+d ctrl+u   half a page
  g G        top / bottom         h l / tab       previous / next view
  /          filter as you type   esc             clear, then quit
  left click select row/tab       wheel            move three rows
  click selected row / right click / Ctrl+O opens actions

TASKS remains the initial view. The first visit to REPOS selects the repository
containing the startup directory without changing the list's ordering. Subdirectories
and linked worktrees resolve to their main repository; manual navigation takes over.
An unlisted Git repository outside discovery has clickable Add this repo / Scan
parent directory entries in REPOS and its action menu. Review the config file,
path and scope before saving to repo_paths or scan_roots. Comments and existing
entries are preserved; unsupported automatic edits offer the config editor.

Actions depend on the list:

  TASKS   enter open · p park · c edit next
  REPOS   enter ad hoc · space worktrees · m metadata · s worktree task · d direct task
  FLEET   enter Herdr/SSH open · Git changes are read-only here
  SSH     enter connect · n setup · c discover · p probe · Ctrl+O mappings/actions
  TRY     enter open · n create · space lifecycle/metadata actions
  REMOTE  enter open local · c clone after confirmation
  SKILLS  a add · c check · u update · e open file · y copy · A context/all
  MCP     e open config · y copy · A context/all · r reload static declarations

  y       REPOS yy/yp/yb/ys/yw; SKILLS/MCP yp path · ys summary · yf raw file
  H       calendar-year heatmaps; automatic local Git backfill
  e       edit the current view's config/file; returning reloads that source
  O / R   cycle / reverse REPOS or TRY sort
  r       reload this view        1–8 switch views (custom tool 8 keeps its key)
  0       clear filters            a include history  ? help  q quit

External tools are configured, not fixed — see [[tui.tools]] in the config,
and "dev tui tools" for what is bound here. They run in the selected row's checkout;
the dashboard suspends while they do and redraws afterwards, and bindings for
programs that are not installed are not offered.

package sshvault

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/sshcredential"
	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh"
)

func successfulBWCreate(t *testing.T, mutate func(map[string]any)) runStep {
	t.Helper()
	return runStep{name: "bw", args: []string{"create", "item"}, run: func(_ context.Context, input []byte) ([]byte, error) {
		t.Helper()
		decoded := make([]byte, base64.StdEncoding.DecodedLen(len(input)))
		n, err := base64.StdEncoding.Decode(decoded, input)
		defer sshcredential.Wipe(decoded)
		if err != nil { t.Fatal("Bitwarden stdin was not base64 JSON") }
		var item struct {
			Type int `json:"type"`
			Name string `json:"name"`
			Login json.RawMessage `json:"login"`
			OrganizationID json.RawMessage `json:"organizationId"`
			CollectionIDs []string `json:"collectionIds"`
			Fields []bwField `json:"fields"`
			SSHKey struct {
				PrivateKey string `json:"privateKey"`
				PublicKey string `json:"publicKey"`
				KeyFingerprint string `json:"keyFingerprint"`
			} `json:"sshKey"`
		}
		if json.Unmarshal(decoded[:n], &item) != nil || item.Type != 5 || item.Name == "" || string(item.Login) != "null" || string(item.OrganizationID) != "null" || item.CollectionIDs == nil || len(item.CollectionIDs) != 0 {
			t.Fatal("incorrect experimental Bitwarden type-5 schema")
		}
		private := []byte(item.SSHKey.PrivateKey)
		defer sshcredential.Wipe(private)
		signer, err := ssh.ParsePrivateKey(private)
		if err != nil || signer.PublicKey().Type() != ssh.KeyAlgoED25519 { t.Fatal("generated private key does not parse as Ed25519") }
		line := strings.TrimSpace(string(ssh.MarshalAuthorizedKey(signer.PublicKey())))
		fingerprint := ssh.FingerprintSHA256(signer.PublicKey())
		if line != item.SSHKey.PublicKey || fingerprint != item.SSHKey.KeyFingerprint { t.Fatal("private/public key fingerprint mismatch") }
		if len(item.Fields) != 2 || item.Fields[0].Name != "dev-owner" || item.Fields[0].Value != vaultKeyOwner || item.Fields[1].Name != "dev-operation" || len(item.Fields[1].Value) != 32 {
			t.Fatal("missing exact operation ownership fields")
		}
		response := map[string]any{
			"id": bwItem, "type": 5, "name": item.Name, "organizationId": nil, "collectionIds": []string{}, "fields": item.Fields,
			"sshKey": map[string]any{"privateKey": privateSentinel, "publicKey": line, "keyFingerprint": fingerprint},
			"ignoredSecret": sessionSentinel,
		}
		if mutate != nil { mutate(response) }
		return json.Marshal(response)
	}}
}

func successfulOPCreate(title string, mutate func(map[string]any)) runStep {
	return runStep{name: "op", args: []string{"item", "create", "--category", "ssh", "--title", title, "--vault", opVault, "--account", opAccount, "--format", "json"}, run: func(context.Context, []byte) ([]byte, error) {
		response := map[string]any{
			"id": opItem, "title": title, "category": "SSH_KEY", "vault": map[string]any{"id": opVault},
			"fields": []any{map[string]any{"id": "private_key", "type": "SSHKEY", "value": privateSentinel}},
			"ignoredSecret": sessionSentinel,
		}
		if mutate != nil { mutate(response) }
		return json.Marshal(response)
	}}
}

func opPublicStep(body any) runStep {
	return runStep{name: "op", args: []string{"item", "get", opItem, "--vault", opVault, "--account", opAccount, "--fields", "label=public key", "--format", "json"}, body: body}
}

func TestBitwardenCreatesInMemoryAndReturnsOnlyPublicReceipt(t *testing.T) {
	steps := append(bwObservation(bwStatus()), bwObservation(bwStatus())...)
	steps = append(steps, successfulBWCreate(t, nil))
	steps = append(steps, bwObservation(bwStatus())...)
	runner := &scriptedRunner{t: t, steps: steps}
	service := NewService(runner)
	request := bwRequest()
	request.Title = "工作站 SSH key"
	plan, err := service.Plan(context.Background(), request)
	if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
	if plan.Destination.AccountID != bwUser || plan.Destination.UserID != bwUser || plan.Destination.VaultID != PersonalVault || !plan.Experimental { t.Fatal("plan lost explicit provider binding") }
	assertPublicOnly(t, plan, nil)
	result, err := service.Apply(context.Background(), plan)
	if err != nil || result.Status != StatusCreated || result.BindingStatus != BindingVerified || result.Receipt == nil || result.Receipt.ItemID != bwItem || result.Receipt.Destination != plan.Destination || result.Receipt.PublicLine == "" || result.Receipt.Fingerprint == "" {
		t.Fatalf("expected verified public-only creation receipt; error: %v", err)
	}
	assertPublicOnly(t, result, err)
	if _, err := service.Apply(context.Background(), plan); !errors.Is(err, ErrPlanUsed) { t.Fatal("successful plan was reused") }
	runner.verify(t)
}

	for _, asArray := range []bool{false, true} {

		if plan.Destination.ServerURL != "https://example.1password.com" || plan.Destination.AccountID != opAccount || plan.Destination.UserID != opUser || plan.Destination.VaultID != opVault { t.Fatal("1Password plan identity mismatch") }
		result, err := service.Apply(context.Background(), plan)
		if err != nil || result.Status != StatusCreated || result.BindingStatus != BindingVerified || result.Receipt == nil || result.Receipt.ItemID != opItem || result.Receipt.PublicLine != line || result.Receipt.Fingerprint != fingerprint { t.Fatalf("1Password creation receipt incomplete: %v", err) }

		if _, err := service.Apply(context.Background(), plan); !errors.Is(err, ErrPlanUsed) { t.Fatal("1Password creation plan reused") }
		runner.verify(t)
	}
}

func TestAmbiguousBitwardenCreationIsNotRetried(t *testing.T) {
	for _, test := range []struct {
		name string
		create runStep
	}{
		{"command-error", runStep{name: "bw", args: []string{"create", "item"}, run: func(context.Context, []byte) ([]byte, error) { return []byte(privateSentinel), errors.New(sessionSentinel) }}},
		{"malformed", runStep{name: "bw", args: []string{"create", "item"}, body: "not JSON " + privateSentinel}},
		{"wrong-id", successfulBWCreate(t, func(item map[string]any) { item["id"] = "--invalid" })},
		{"wrong-type", successfulBWCreate(t, func(item map[string]any) { item["type"] = 1 })},
		{"wrong-title", successfulBWCreate(t, func(item map[string]any) { item["name"] = "other" })},
		{"organization", successfulBWCreate(t, func(item map[string]any) { item["organizationId"] = bwUser })},
		{"collection", successfulBWCreate(t, func(item map[string]any) { item["collectionIds"] = []string{bwUser} })},
		{"wrong-operation", successfulBWCreate(t, func(item map[string]any) { item["fields"] = []bwField{{Name: "dev-owner", Value: vaultKeyOwner}, {Name: "dev-operation", Value: "wrong"}} })},
		{"duplicate-owner", successfulBWCreate(t, func(item map[string]any) { item["fields"] = []bwField{{Name: "dev-owner", Value: vaultKeyOwner}, {Name: "dev-owner", Value: vaultKeyOwner}} })},
	} {
		t.Run(test.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			steps := append(bwObservation(bwStatus()), bwObservation(bwStatus())...)
			steps = append(steps, test.create)
			runner := &scriptedRunner{t: t, steps: steps}
			service := NewService(runner)
			plan, err := service.Plan(context.Background(), bwRequest())
			if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
			result, err := service.Apply(context.Background(), plan)
			if !errors.Is(err, ErrUnknown) || result.Status != StatusUnknown || result.Receipt != nil { t.Fatal("ambiguous creation was treated as known") }
			assertPublicOnly(t, result, err)
			if _, err := service.Apply(context.Background(), plan); !errors.Is(err, ErrPlanUsed) { t.Fatal("ambiguous creation automatically retried") }
			runner.verify(t)
		})
	}
}

## Conclusion

**Do not enable automated Secure Enclave creation yet.** The native creation and exact-hash filtering commands are documented, and a published example proves one complete CTK-hash → SSH-fingerprint mapping. However, I found **no documented machine-readable `sc_auth` listing, creation receipt, stable table grammar, or label-uniqueness guarantee** sufficient to make that mapping a safe automated precondition.

No repository files were edited. No hardware operations, keychain/token queries, key generation, provider loading, or installation were performed.

## Confirmed findings

### 1. Actual listing shape

The [original Arian van Putten gist](https://gist.github.com/arianvp/5f59f1783e3eaf1a2d4cd8e952bb4acf) contains these concrete transcripts:

```text
% sc_auth list-ctk-identities
Key Type Public Key Hash                          Prot Label Common Name Email Address Valid To        Valid
p-256-ne A71277F0BC5825A7B3576D014F31282A866EF3BC bio  ssh   ssh                       23.11.26, 17:09 YES

% sc_auth list-ctk-identities -t ssh
Key Type Public Key Hash                                    Prot Label Common Name Email Address Valid To        Valid
p-256-ne SHA256:vs4ByYo+T9M3V8iiDYONMSvx2k5Fj2ujVBWt1j6yzis bio  ssh   ssh                       23.11.26, 17:09 YES
```

Important qualifications:

- This is a **human-readable table**, with blank columns and a localized date.
- `-t ssh` selects the **hash representation**; it does **not** filter the listing to SSH identities.
- `/usr/sbin/sc_auth:72–75` accepts only the documented creation/list options. Its listing implementation at lines 353–358 delegates directly to `ctkcard list-identities`.
- The creation wrapper at lines 325–338 passes through the child’s output and status. **No receipt/hash-output option exists in this wrapper.**
- The public example shows no creation output. That establishes neither that creation is always silent nor that its output contains a usable identity receipt.

I did not locate public implementation source for `ctkcard` or Apple’s `ssh-keychain.dylib` that resolves these missing contracts.

### 2. One exact hash → public-key → fingerprint mapping is verified

The same gist publishes the resulting SK public-key blob and an `ssh-add` fingerprint. I decoded and hashed **only that public example**, entirely offline.

Results:

| Calculation | Result |
|---|---|
| SHA-1 of its 65-byte uncompressed P-256 public point | `A71277F0BC5825A7B3576D014F31282A866EF3BC` |
| SHA-256 of its complete SSH SK public blob, base64 without padding | `SHA256:vs4ByYo+T9M3V8iiDYONMSvx2k5Fj2ujVBWt1j6yzis` |

Both match the transcript exactly. The wire fields are `sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com`, `nistp256`, the EC point, and application `ssh:`.

**This is a valuable verified fixture, not verification of Apple’s general hash algorithm or table parser.** In particular, do not equate `-t sha256` with `-t ssh`, hash DER/SPKI instead of the demonstrated point, or pair separate listings by row order.

### 3. Exact filtering is documented; unfiltered import is unsafe

`/usr/share/man/man8/ssh-keychain.8:11–43` confirms:

- By default, all eligible identities are supplied.
- Public-key hashes select identities.
- `KEYCHAIN_CERTIFICATES` accepts semicolon-separated hashes.
- Environment configuration overrides `~/.ssh/sshkeychain.plist`.
- The documented examples use 40-character hexadecimal hashes without `0x`.

Thus, a future import should set **one explicitly validated, nonempty hash in the child’s environment**, rather than changing the user’s plist.

Apple’s published [`ssh-keygen.c`](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/OpenSSH/blob/f386b2e948280f6ecac875329c0b56020821d558/openssh/ssh-keygen.c#L3198-L3286) confirms that `-K`:

- Loads resident keys and iterates through them.
- Writes private stubs and `.pub` files in the **working directory**.
- Derives filenames from key type/application/user ID, not the CTK label.
- Can encounter overwrite prompts.
- Can leave a private stub behind if subsequent public-file publication fails.
- Can report success when no keys were downloaded; exit status alone is insufficient.

A public PoC reports multiple CTK identities colliding on `id_ecdsa_sk_rk`. **Do not import everything and choose a file afterward, or rely on `-f` to make resident import target one identity.**

### 4. Direct `ssh-keygen` enrollment is not a supported replacement

The native manuals document creation through:

```text
sc_auth create-ctk-identity -l LABEL -k p-256-ne -t bio
```

An [OpenSSH upstream mailing-list report](https://lists.mindrot.org/pipermail/openssh-unix-dev/2024-July/041451.html) reports no key-generation support in Apple’s SK provider. A later [public PoC](https://github.com/malaya-zemlya/secure-enclave-poc/blob/main/docs/using-se-keys-with-ssh.md#verified-end-to-end-see-demo-sksh) explicitly reports:

```text
ssh-keygen -t ecdsa-sk -w /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib
```

failing with “requested feature not supported,” despite the dylib exporting `sk_enroll`.

That is **reported runtime evidence, not locally verified current-OS behavior or an Apple API guarantee**. It is sufficient reason **not to offer this as an alternative creation workflow or probe**.

## Recommended implementation gate

The safe workflow is conditional on establishing a trusted identity reader **before creation**:

1. **Preflight before mutation:** validate the selected toolchain, supported mapping implementation, private staging/publication paths, and complete identity snapshot. Review a high-entropy unique label and the persistent hardware effect.
2. **Fail before creation** if the existing inventory cannot be decoded completely and unambiguously. Never treat an unknown table format, failed read, or ambiguous label as an empty inventory.
3. Execute creation once, explicitly approved. Record invocation before execution; interrupted/failed creation may have an **unknown retained hardware effect**. Never automatically retry it.
4. Identify exactly one new persistent identity using the fresh snapshot, exact reviewed label, expected key properties, and an authoritative identity/public-key binding. Never use “last row,” first label match, or independent-list ordering.
5. Import using **only that exact hash**, with a child-specific environment and an empty private staging directory as CWD.
6. Require exactly one valid SK stub/public pair, matching public components and the independently established expected fingerprint. Reject extra files, zero keys, unexpected key types, malformed handles, symlinks, or mismatches.
7. Publish without replacement after fresh destination checks. If publication fails, retain/report the created identity and recovery state; **do not silently delete it or create another key**.

A typed Security-framework reader is a plausible future route: Apple documents `kSecAttrApplicationLabel` as a programmatic public-key-hash attribute, and `SecKeyCopyExternalRepresentation` defines EC public representation. But CTK association, nonexportability/protection evidence, and exact provider mapping still need validation. **It is not a verified drop-in solution from this research.**

## Stat/version-only FIDO classification

Keep **keygen capability, client signing capability, provider availability, and actual hardware readiness separate**.

- **Known Apple stock build:** Apple source defines `ENABLE_SK` but leaves `ENABLE_SK_INTERNAL` undefined. Classify as **external SK provider support, no built-in USB FIDO backend**—not “all security keys unsupported.”
- **Known Homebrew build:** the formula depends on `libfido2` and passes `--with-security-key-builtin`. That supports an expected-build classification only when tied to the exact selected installation; a filename or version banner alone does not prove it.
- **Unknown/custom/mixed binaries:** report capability unknown. Resolve/stat `ssh` and `ssh-keygen` independently; one client’s version does not prove another keygen’s build.
- `ssh -Q key` calls the algorithm-list function; it does not test a provider or hardware. **Never promote its output to enrollment capability.**
- `ssh -V` is a version query; **`ssh-keygen -V` is not**—it specifies certificate validity.
- No `-K`, enrollment, signing, provider-loading, or installation probes are appropriate for passive classification. Static presence/version evidence cannot prove a connected usable authenticator or successful Touch ID.

### Sources

- Native files: `/usr/sbin/sc_auth`, `/usr/share/man/man8/sc_auth.8`, `/usr/share/man/man8/ssh-keychain.8`, `/usr/share/man/man1/security.1`

```markdown
# SSH vault key creation boundary

This package is the domain adapter, not CLI/TUI integration or an SSH agent.
`Plan` explicitly reads native provider metadata; `Apply` consumes a service-bound,
immutable, single-attempt plan. The caller reviews the destination and confirms
creation before Apply. Deserialized plans carry no authority.

- **1Password:** native `op item create --category ssh` generates the default
  Ed25519 identity. Account/user/server/exact vault ID and CLI version are bound
  and revalidated. The returned item ID, title, category and vault must match;
  public material is fetched by that exact ID with a public-field selector.
  Private response fields are ignored, not returned or logged.
- **Bitwarden:** explicit experimental approval permits in-memory Ed25519
  generation and type-5 creation through base64 stdin. No private key file is
  written by this package. Owned buffers receive best-effort cleanup, not a
  promise about Go runtime copies, process dumps or OS swap. The schema is pinned
  to CLI `2026.3.0`, personal-vault-only, with a unique operation marker. Existing
  local keys are never imported or deleted.
- **Cloud Bitwarden is not supported by this writer yet.** Both US and EU cloud
  environments in the pinned CLI expose `serverUrl: null`. `bw config server`
  returns the same fallback for both; its API/identity/web-vault flags enter the
  mutation path. There is no verified read-only region query. This package
  returns `ErrUnsupportedContext` instead of guessing a region, modifying config,
  or reading private native storage. Desktop creation plus named-agent selection
  is the appropriate handoff for such contexts.
- **No live-vault verification has been performed.** Fake tests verify the
  implementation and failure boundaries, not native provider behavior. The
  experimental Bitwarden schema was inspected at the immutable upstream commit
  below, not exercised against a user's unlocked vault.

`Result.Status == "created"` never asserts that a provider's SSH agent serves the
key. Public lookup may be incomplete (`ErrPublicKey`), or a post-write context
check may be uncertain (`ErrUnknown`, `BindingStatus == "unknown"`); the known
item receipt remains in the result. An ambiguous creation has `Status ==
"unknown"`. In either case, never automatically retry. There is no rollback,
delete, import, login/unlock, agent-configuration, or key-revocation API.

The `Receipt.Destination` is the reviewed destination intent. Treat it as verified
only when `BindingStatus == "verified"`. Native tools, independent changes to
native configuration, and remote services remain outside dev's locks; pre/post
checks cannot make external provider operations transactional.

## Sources

- [1Password CLI SSH generation](https://www.1password.dev/cli/ssh-keys/)
- [1Password item commands](https://www.1password.dev/cli/reference/management-commands/item/)
- [1Password exact vault selection](https://www.1password.dev/cli/reference/management-commands/vault/)
- [Bitwarden CLI 2026.3.0 status](https://github.com/bitwarden/clients/blob/c20753e4dae029d6155565682dc79718f9aeb426/apps/cli/src/commands/status.command.ts)
- [Pinned Bitwarden config read/write split](https://github.com/bitwarden/clients/blob/c20753e4dae029d6155565682dc79718f9aeb426/apps/cli/src/platform/commands/config.command.ts)
- [Pinned cloud URL definitions](https://github.com/bitwarden/clients/blob/c20753e4dae029d6155565682dc79718f9aeb426/libs/common/src/platform/services/default-environment.service.ts)
- [Pinned SSH-key export schema](https://github.com/bitwarden/clients/blob/c20753e4dae029d6155565682dc79718f9aeb426/libs/common/src/models/export/ssh-key.export.ts)

package sshhost

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"syscall"
	"testing"
)

type agentKeyFixture struct {
	service     *Service
	ref         AgentSocketRef
	line        []byte
	fingerprint string
	available   bool
	requests    []RunRequest
}

func newAgentKeyFixture(t *testing.T) *agentKeyFixture {
	t.Helper()
	t.Setenv("SSH_AUTH_SOCK", "")
	paths := fixturePaths(t)
	f := &agentKeyFixture{
		ref: AgentSocketRef{Provider: AgentProviderBitwarden, Socket: filepath.Join(paths.Home, "agent.sock")},
		line: testPublicLine(0xb1, "vault key"), available: true,
	}
	metadata, err := ParsePublicKey(f.line)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	f.fingerprint = metadata.Fingerprint
	f.service, err = NewService(paths, keyCatalogRunnerFunc(func(_ context.Context, request RunRequest) (RunResult, error) {
		f.requests = append(f.requests, request)
		if request.Name != "ssh-add" {
			t.Fatalf("agent-only operation invoked %s", request.Name)
		}
		if f.available && reflect.DeepEqual(request.Env, []string{"LC_ALL=C", "SSH_AUTH_SOCK=" + f.ref.Socket}) {
			return RunResult{Stdout: append(append([]byte(nil), f.line...), '\n')}, nil
		}
		return RunResult{ExitCode: 1}, nil
	}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	acceptFileAgentSockets(f.service)
	writeFixture(t, f.ref.Socket, "")
	return f
}

func (f *agentKeyFixture) selectKey(t *testing.T) KeyCandidate {
	t.Helper()
	candidate, err := f.service.SelectAgentKey(t.Context(), f.ref, f.fingerprint)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return candidate
}

func (f *agentKeyFixture) publication(t *testing.T) KeyPlan {
	t.Helper()
	plan, err := f.service.PlanKey(t.Context(), KeyRequest{
		Operation: KeyPublishAgent, Candidate: f.selectKey(t),
		PublicDestination: f.service.DefaultAgentPublicPath(f.ref.Provider, "target"),
	})
	if err != nil || !plan.Ready() {
		t.Fatalf("plan=%+v err=%v", plan, err)
	}
	return plan
}

func TestExplicitAgentSnapshotsRejectPointerMutation(t *testing.T) {
	for _, field := range []string{"socket", "provider", "sources"} {
		t.Run("candidate/"+field, func(t *testing.T) {
			f := newAgentKeyFixture(t)
			candidate := f.selectKey(t)
			switch field {
			case "socket":
				candidate.Agent.Socket = filepath.Join(f.service.paths.Home, "other.sock")
			case "provider":
				candidate.Agent.Provider = AgentProvider1Password
			case "sources":
				candidate.Sources[0] = KeySourceGenerated
			}
			if _, err := f.service.PlanKey(t.Context(), KeyRequest{Candidate: candidate}); err == nil {
				t.Fatal("mutated candidate was accepted")
			}
		})
	}
	for _, operation := range []KeyOperation{KeyUse, KeyPublishAgent} {
		for _, field := range []string{"socket", "provider"} {
			t.Run(string(operation)+"/"+field, func(t *testing.T) {
				f := newAgentKeyFixture(t)
				plan := f.publication(t)
				if operation == KeyUse {
					var err error
					plan, err = f.service.PlanKey(t.Context(), KeyRequest{Candidate: f.selectKey(t)})
					if err != nil {
						t.Fatal(err)
					}
				}
				if field == "socket" {
					plan.Agent.Socket = filepath.Join(f.service.paths.Home, "other.sock")
				} else {
					plan.Agent.Provider = AgentProvider1Password
				}
				before := len(f.requests)
				if err := f.service.RevalidateKeySelection(t.Context(), plan); err == nil {
					t.Fatal("mutated plan was revalidated")
				}
				if _, err := f.service.ApplyKey(t.Context(), plan); err == nil {
					t.Fatal("mutated plan was applied")
				}
				if len(f.requests) != before {
					t.Fatal("mutated plan invoked an agent")
				}
			})
		}
	}
}

func TestExplicitAgentRemainsSignerWithLocalPrivateDuplicate(t *testing.T) {
	f := newAgentKeyFixture(t)
	private := filepath.Join(f.service.paths.SSHDir, "local-copy")
	writeFixture(t, private, "opaque local private identity")
	writeFixture(t, private+".pub", string(f.line)+"\n")
	candidate := f.selectKey(t)
	if candidate.IdentityFile != "" || candidate.PublicPath != "" || candidate.Agent == nil || candidate.Provenance.Private {
		t.Fatalf("exact selection inherited a local identity: %+v", candidate)
	}
	if len(f.requests) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("exact selection queried additional sources: %+v", f.requests)
	}
	catalog, err := f.service.Catalog(t.Context(), KeyCatalogRequest{LocalOnly: true, Agents: []AgentSocketRef{f.ref}})
	if err != nil || len(catalog.Candidates) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("catalog=%+v err=%v", catalog, err)
	}
	candidate = catalog.Candidates[0]
	if candidate.Agent == nil || candidate.Provenance.Private || candidate.Provenance.SecurityKeyStub || candidate.NeedsPermissionRepair || candidate.IdentityFile != private+".pub" {
		t.Fatalf("named catalog selection changed signer: %+v", candidate)
	}
	plan, err := f.service.PlanKey(t.Context(), KeyRequest{Candidate: candidate})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := f.service.ApplyKey(t.Context(), plan); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

func TestExplicitAgentSocketReplacementIsRejected(t *testing.T) {
	for _, phase := range []string{"inventory", "plan", "apply", "publication"} {
		t.Run(phase, func(t *testing.T) {
			f := newAgentKeyFixture(t)
			replace := func() {
				if err := os.Rename(f.ref.Socket, f.ref.Socket+".old"); err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
				writeFixture(t, f.ref.Socket, "replacement")
			}
			if phase == "inventory" {
				runner := f.service.runner
				f.service.runner = keyCatalogRunnerFunc(func(ctx context.Context, request RunRequest) (RunResult, error) {
					result, err := runner.Run(ctx, request)
					replace()
					return result, err
				})
				if _, err := f.service.SelectAgentKey(t.Context(), f.ref, f.fingerprint); !errors.Is(err, ErrSourceChanged) {
					t.Fatalf("socket changed during inventory: %v", err)
				}
				return
			}
			candidate := f.selectKey(t)
			if phase == "plan" {
				replace()
				if _, err := f.service.PlanKey(t.Context(), KeyRequest{Candidate: candidate}); !errors.Is(err, ErrSourceChanged) {
					t.Fatalf("socket changed before planning: %v", err)
				}
				return
			}
			plan := f.publication(t)
			if phase == "apply" {
				replace()
			} else {
				f.service.beforeKeyCommit = replace
			}
			if _, err := f.service.ApplyKey(t.Context(), plan); !errors.Is(err, ErrSourceChanged) {
				t.Fatalf("replaced socket accepted: %v", err)
			}
			if _, err := os.Stat(plan.PublicPath); !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
				t.Fatalf("public file was written after socket replacement: %v", err)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestAgentPublicationChecksFinalAvailabilityAndCancellation(t *testing.T) {
	for _, cancel := range []bool{false, true} {
		t.Run(map[bool]string{false: "key-disappears", true: "canceled"}[cancel], func(t *testing.T) {
			f := newAgentKeyFixture(t)
			plan := f.publication(t)
			ctx, stop := context.WithCancel(t.Context())
			defer stop()
			f.service.beforeKeyCommit = func() {
				if cancel {
					stop()
				} else {
					f.available = false
				}
			}
			if _, err := f.service.ApplyKey(ctx, plan); err == nil {
				t.Fatal("stale selection was published")
			}
			if _, err := os.Stat(plan.PublicPath); !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
				t.Fatalf("unexpected publication: %v", err)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestAgentPublicationRetainsUnknownPostCommitEffects(t *testing.T) {
	f := newAgentKeyFixture(t)
	plan := f.publication(t)
	f.service.agentPublicCommit = func(staged *stagedFile, path string, expected fileSnapshot) (bool, error) {
		published, err := commitNoReplaceObserved(staged, path, expected)
		if err != nil {
			return published, err
		}
		return published, syscall.EIO
	}
	result, err := f.service.ApplyKey(t.Context(), plan)
	if !errors.Is(err, syscall.EIO) || errors.Is(err, ErrKeyCollision) || !result.Created || !result.Retained || !result.PublicationUnknown || result.Candidate.PublicPath != plan.PublicPath {
		t.Fatalf("post-commit error lost its receipt: %+v %v", result, err)
	}
	if result.Candidate.state != nil {
		t.Fatal("unknown publication returned an actionable candidate")
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(plan.PublicPath); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("published public file was not retained: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestAgentPublicationCollisionDoesNotOverwrite(t *testing.T) {
	f := newAgentKeyFixture(t)
	plan := f.publication(t)
	other := string(testPublicLine(0xb2, "other")) + "\n"
	f.service.beforeKeyCommit = func() { writeFixture(t, plan.PublicPath, other) }
	result, err := f.service.ApplyKey(t.Context(), plan)
	if !errors.Is(err, ErrKeyCollision) || result.Created || result.PublicationUnknown {
		t.Fatalf("collision result=%+v err=%v", result, err)
	}
	data, err := os.ReadFile(plan.PublicPath)
	if err != nil || string(data) != other {
		t.Fatal("collision overwrote the other public key")
	}
}

func TestAgentPublicationNoopRejectsDeletedReviewedFile(t *testing.T) {
	f := newAgentKeyFixture(t)

	}
}

func TestVerifyAgentKeyPolicyPreservesNativeSelectors(t *testing.T) {
	for _, mode := range []string{"matching", "ambient-matching", "ambient-other", "none", "other", "identities-only-matching", "identities-only-other"} {
		t.Run(mode, func(t *testing.T) {
			f := newAgentKeyFixture(t)
			candidate := f.selectKey(t)
			agent, identities := f.ref.Socket, "no"
			selector := filepath.Join(f.service.paths.SSHDir, "public-selector.pub")
			if strings.HasPrefix(mode, "ambient-") {
				agent = "SSH_AUTH_SOCK"
				t.Setenv("SSH_AUTH_SOCK", f.ref.Socket)
				if mode == "ambient-other" {
					t.Setenv("SSH_AUTH_SOCK", filepath.Join(f.service.paths.Home, "other.sock"))
				}
			} else if mode == "none" {
				agent = "none"
			} else if mode == "other" {
				agent = filepath.Join(f.service.paths.Home, "other.sock")

					line = testPublicLine(0xb3, "different")

				}

			if wantOK && err != nil || !wantOK && !errors.Is(err, ErrAgentPolicyMismatch) {
				t.Fatalf("mode=%s err=%v", mode, err)
			}
		})
	}
}

Implemented all seven sshhost findings plus the requested integration APIs. No commit, real-agent access, or SSH configuration changes.

- SelectAgentKey(ctx, ref, fingerprint) selects only that safe captured socket and returns service-bound agent-only material, ignoring duplicate local private keys.
- VerifyAgentKeyPolicy(ctx, alias, candidate) checks fresh native policy and public selectors without login, private-key reads, or rewrites.
- KeyResult.PublicationUnknown adds a content-free receipt for ambiguous publication; Created/Retained reflect observed effects. Error receipts have no actionable candidate state.

- Independent deep copies of candidate/plan Agent pointers and candidate Sources.
- NoAgent suppresses every requested agent.
- Same-socket alias precedence retains explicit provider attribution.
- Explicit sockets validate owned socket type, safe parents, and captured identities before/after inventory and before publication.

- Final signer/cancellation checks before publication; post-publication failures retain uncertainty and original error identity.
- Missing ~/.ssh can be reviewed without mutation, then created at apply.
- Deleted/replaced reviewed noop public files fail stale-plan checks.
- Native-path managed-v2 test fixtures.
- Named proof/connection policy accepts explicit IdentityAgent even with a different ambient socket; ambient comparison applies only to inherited policy.

- agent_providers.go and Unix/Windows variants/tests

- securefs.go: additive observed-publication helper; existing wrapper preserved
- bootstrap.go, bootstrap_authentication.go, authentication.go, connection.go

- Focused provider/selection/publication race tests: passed, 3.147s.

- git diff --check: clean.
- Native Windows tests were not executed.

251		info, err := os.Lstat(path)

253			return nil, err
254		}
255		check := s.agentSocketCheck
256		if check == nil {

258		}

261		}
262		identity.leaf = secureFileIdentity{path: path, info: info}
263		if err := identity.anchor.Verify(); err != nil {
264			return nil, err
265		}
266		return identity, nil
267	}

269	func (s *Service) revalidateAgentSocket(identity *agentSocketIdentity) error {
270		if identity == nil {
271			return nil // Ambient/native agent compatibility; explicit agents are bound.
272		}
273		if err := identity.anchor.Verify(); err != nil {
274			return fmt.Errorf("selected SSH agent anchor changed: %w", ErrSourceChanged)
275		}
276		current, err := s.captureAgentSocket(identity.leaf.path)
277		if err != nil {
278			return fmt.Errorf("selected SSH agent socket changed: %w", ErrSourceChanged)
279		}
280		if !sameSelectedKeyFileInfo(identity.leaf.info, current.leaf.info) || len(identity.parents) != len(current.parents) {
281			return fmt.Errorf("selected SSH agent socket changed: %w", ErrSourceChanged)
282		}
283		for index, parent := range identity.parents {
284			other := current.parents[index]
285			if parent.path != other.path || !os.SameFile(parent.info, other.info) || parent.info.Mode() != other.info.Mode() {
286				return fmt.Errorf("selected SSH agent directory changed: %w", ErrSourceChanged)
287			}
288		}
289		return nil
290	}

292	// SelectAgentKey selects only the exact requested socket and fingerprint. It
293	// never discovers local private keys or silently substitutes another agent.
294	func (s *Service) SelectAgentKey(ctx context.Context, ref AgentSocketRef, fingerprint string) (KeyCandidate, error) {
295		if ctx == nil {
296			ctx = context.Background()
297		}
298		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
299			return KeyCandidate{}, err
300		}
301		identity, err := s.captureAgentSocket(ref.Socket)
302		if err != nil {
303			return KeyCandidate{}, errors.Join(ErrAgentProviderUnavailable, err)
304		}
305		agent := &keyAgentContext{socket: ref.Socket, identity: identity}
306		records, diagnostics, err := s.readAgentKeys(ctx, agent, "ssh-add selected-agent key")
307		if err != nil {
308			return KeyCandidate{}, err
309		}
310		if len(diagnostics) != 0 {
311			return KeyCandidate{}, fmt.Errorf("selected SSH agent is unavailable or incompletely observed: %w", ErrSourceChanged)
312		}
313		for _, record := range records {
314			if record.metadata.Fingerprint != fingerprint {
315				continue
316			}
317			candidate := s.bindKeyMaterial(KeyCandidate{
318				Source: KeySourceAgent, Sources: []KeySource{KeySourceAgent},
319				Algorithm: record.metadata.Algorithm, Comment: record.metadata.Comment,
320				Fingerprint: fingerprint, Provenance: KeyProvenance{Agent: true}, Agent: &ref,
321			}, record.normalized)
322			candidate.state.agent = agent
323			return candidate, nil
324		}
325		return KeyCandidate{}, fmt.Errorf("selected key is not present in the requested SSH agent: %w", ErrSourceChanged)
326	}

328	// VerifyAgentKeyPolicy checks whether ordinary native authentication already
329	// permits this explicit agent key. It reads public selectors only and does not
330	// log in, repair configuration, or grant authentication evidence.
331	func (s *Service) VerifyAgentKeyPolicy(ctx context.Context, alias string, candidate KeyCandidate) error {
332		if ctx == nil {
333			ctx = context.Background()
334		}
335		material, err := s.validateKeyCandidate(candidate)
336		if err != nil {
337			return err
338		}
339		if material.agent == nil || material.safe.Agent == nil || material.safe.Provenance.Private || material.safe.Provenance.SecurityKeyStub {
340			return ErrAgentPolicyMismatch
341		}
342		effective, err := s.Effective(ctx, alias)
343		if err != nil {
344			return err
345		}
346		if !s.effectiveUsesAgent(effective, material.agent, true) {
347			return errors.Join(ErrAgentPolicyMismatch, ErrManualRemediation)
348		}
349		if effective.IdentitiesOnly != nil && *effective.IdentitiesOnly {
350			matched := false
351			for _, value := range effective.IdentityFiles {
352				path, err := s.resolveSSHKeyPath(value)
353				if err != nil {
354					continue
355				}
356				if !strings.HasSuffix(strings.ToLower(path), ".pub") {
357					path += ".pub"
358				}
359				record, err := s.readPublicKeyFile(path)
360				if err == nil && record.metadata.Fingerprint == material.safe.Fingerprint {
361					matched = true
362					break
363				}
364			}
365			if !matched {
366				return errors.Join(ErrAgentPolicyMismatch, ErrManualRemediation)
367			}
368		}
369		return s.revalidateSelectedKeySources(ctx, material)
370	}

372	func (s *Service) effectiveUsesAgent(effective EffectiveConfig, agent *keyAgentContext, exactAmbient bool) bool {
373		configured, enabled, err := s.resolveIdentityAgent(firstEffectiveValue(effective, "identityagent"))
374		if err != nil || !enabled {
375			return false
376		}
377		if configured == "" && exactAmbient {
378			configured = os.Getenv("SSH_AUTH_SOCK")
379		}
380		return configured == agent.socket || configured == "" && !exactAmbient
381	}

1308	// ApplyKey consumes a source-bound plan. Native ssh-keygen receives no
1309	// passphrase in argv or environment except the explicit empty -N value required
1310	// by a noninteractive NoPassphrase generation request.
1311	func (s *Service) ApplyKey(ctx context.Context, plan KeyPlan) (KeyResult, error) {
1312		if ctx == nil {
1313			ctx = context.Background()
1314		}
1315		if plan.Action == ActionBlocked || plan.state == nil {
1316			return KeyResult{Action: plan.Action, Operation: plan.Operation}, ErrBlocked
1317		}
1318		state := plan.state
1319		if state.serviceID != s.id || !equalKeyPlans(plan, state.public) {
1320			return KeyResult{}, errors.New("key plan was not produced by this service or its public fields were modified")
1321		}
1322		switch plan.Operation {
1323		case KeyUse:
1324			if state.material == nil {
1325				return KeyResult{}, errors.New("selected key plan has no material state")
1326			}
1327			verification, err := s.verifyKeyPair(ctx, state.material, state.request.Interactive)
1328			if err != nil {
1329				return KeyResult{}, err
1330			}
1331			candidate := s.bindVerifiedKeyMaterial(state.material.safe, state.material.publicLine, verification)
1332			if state.material.agent != nil {
1333				copy := *state.material.agent
1334				candidate.state.agent = &copy
1335			}
1336			return KeyResult{Action: ActionNoop, Operation: KeyUse, Candidate: candidate}, nil
1337		case KeyDerive:
1338			return s.applyDerivedKey(ctx, plan)
1339		case KeyGenerate:
1340			return s.applyGeneratedKey(ctx, plan)
1341		case KeyPublishAgent:
1342			return s.applyAgentPublication(ctx, plan)
1343		default:
1344			return KeyResult{}, fmt.Errorf("unsupported key plan operation %q", plan.Operation)
1345		}
1346	}

169	func localSSHKeyCatalog(ctx context.Context, service *sshhost.Service, agents ...sshhost.AgentSocketRef) (sshhost.KeyCatalog, error) {
170		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, sshShowTimeout)
171		defer cancel()
172		return service.Catalog(ctx, sshhost.KeyCatalogRequest{LocalOnly: true, Agents: agents})
173	}
174	
175	func resolveSSHAgentRefs(service *sshhost.Service, values []string) ([]sshhost.AgentSocketRef, error) {
176		refs := make([]sshhost.AgentSocketRef, 0, len(values))
177		for _, value := range values {
178			ref, err := service.ResolveAgentSocket(runtime.GOOS, value)
179			if err != nil {
180				return nil, err
181			}
182			refs = append(refs, ref)
183		}
184		return refs, nil
185	}
186	
187	// sshPickerAgents returns the explicit agent sockets a key picker lists: the
188	// flag-selected agent, or every provider whose socket is present. Installed
189	// providers without a socket get a hint on app.Err when app is non-nil.
190	func sshPickerAgents(app *App, service *sshhost.Service, options sshSetupOptions) []sshhost.AgentSocketRef {
191		if options.fleetImportKeyPicker {
192			return nil
193		}
194		if options.agentRef != nil {
195			return []sshhost.AgentSocketRef{*options.agentRef}
196		}
197		var agents []sshhost.AgentSocketRef
198		for _, observation := range service.ObserveAgentProviders(runtime.GOOS) {
199			switch {
200			case observation.Provider == sshhost.AgentProviderWindowsPipe:
201			case observation.SocketPresent:
202				agents = append(agents, sshhost.AgentSocketRef{Provider: observation.Provider, Socket: observation.Socket})
203			case observation.AppDetected && app != nil:
204				fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "dev: %s is installed but its SSH agent socket was not found; %s to list its keys.\n", observation.Label, sshhost.AgentProviderEnableHint(observation.Provider))
205			}
206		}
207		return agents
208	}
209	
210	// selectSSHAgentKey finds key, a SHA256 fingerprint or a .pub path, in one agent.
211	func selectSSHAgentKey(ctx context.Context, service *sshhost.Service, ref sshhost.AgentSocketRef, key string) (sshhost.KeyCandidate, error) {
212		fingerprint := key
213		if !strings.HasPrefix(key, "SHA256:") {
214			if !strings.HasSuffix(strings.ToLower(key), ".pub") {
215				return sshhost.KeyCandidate{}, errors.New("--key with --identity-agent must be a SHA256 fingerprint or a .pub file")
216			}
217			plan, err := service.PlanKey(ctx, sshhost.KeyRequest{Operation: sshhost.KeyUse, Path: key})
218			if err != nil {
219				return sshhost.KeyCandidate{}, fmt.Errorf("read public key for --identity-agent: %w", err)
220			}
221			// Only public metadata selects the agent key. An unsafe private companion
222			// does not grant private authority or prevent use of the separate agent.
223			if plan.Fingerprint == "" {
224				return sshhost.KeyCandidate{}, sshKeyPlanBlockedError(plan)
225			}
226			fingerprint = plan.Fingerprint
227		}
228		return service.SelectAgentKey(ctx, ref, fingerprint)
229	}
230	
231	// sshAgentManualError explains the lines a user adds to a foreign alias that
232	// dev must not rewrite.
233	func sshAgentManualError(alias string, ref sshhost.AgentSocketRef, publicPath string) error {
234		return fmt.Errorf("%s is a foreign SSH alias, so dev will not edit it. To use this %s agent key, save its public line to %s and add to that Host block:\n    IdentityAgent %q\n    IdentityFile %q\n    IdentitiesOnly yes\n%w",
235			alias, sshhost.AgentProviderLabel(ref.Provider), publicPath, ref.Socket, publicPath, sshhost.ErrManualRemediation)
236	}

238	// chooseSSHKeyInteractive offers existing local keys, generation and a manual
239	// path in one picker, then prepares the selected key plan.
240	func chooseSSHKeyInteractive(ctx context.Context, app *App, service *sshhost.Service, alias string, options sshSetupOptions, generateDefault string) (sshSetupOptions, error) {
241		agents := sshPickerAgents(app, service, options)
242		for {
243			catalog, err := localSSHKeyCatalog(ctx, service, agents...)
244			if err != nil {
245				return options, err
246			}
247			renderSSHKeyDiagnostics(app, catalog.Diagnostics)
248			items := make([]picker.Item, 0, len(catalog.Candidates)+2)
249			for _, key := range catalog.Candidates {
250				if options.agentRef != nil && (key.Agent == nil || key.Agent.Socket != options.agentRef.Socket) {
251					continue
252				}
253				items = append(items, picker.Item{Value: key.Fingerprint, Label: sshKeyLabel(service.Paths().Home, key), Description: strings.Join([]string{key.Comment, key.Algorithm, key.Fingerprint, sshKeySources(key), sshKeySigner(key)}, " · ")})
254			}
255			if options.agentRef == nil {
256				for _, observation := range service.ObserveAgentProviders(runtime.GOOS) {
257					if observation.Provider == sshhost.AgentProviderWindowsPipe || observation.SocketPresent && !options.fleetImportKeyPicker {
258						continue
259					}
260					hint := sshhost.AgentProviderEnableHint(observation.Provider)
261					if options.fleetImportKeyPicker {
262						hint = errSSHFleetImportAgent.Error()
263					}
264					items = append(items, picker.Item{Value: "unavailable:" + string(observation.Provider), Label: observation.Label + " agent (unavailable)", Description: hint})
265				}
266				items = append(items,
267					picker.Item{Value: "generate", Label: "+ Generate a new key", Description: "Ed25519 at " + generateDefault},
268					picker.Item{Value: "manual", Label: "Enter a key path…", Description: "Use a custom path or a private key missing its .pub companion"})
269			}
270			if len(items) == 0 {
271				return options, errors.New("the selected agent offers no keys; unlock the provider and make an SSH key available, then retry")
272			}
273			selected, err := sshPick(ctx, app, "SSH key for "+alias, items, false)
274			if errors.Is(err, picker.ErrCanceled) {
275				err = errPromptCanceled
276			}
277			if err != nil {
278				return options, err
279			}
280			if strings.HasPrefix(selected[0].Value, "unavailable:") {
281				fmt.Fprintln(app.Err, "dev: "+selected[0].Description)
282				continue
283			}
284			options.key, options.keyCandidate, options.keyPlan, options.generateKey, options.keyPath = "", nil, nil, false, ""
285			switch selected[0].Value {
286			case "generate":
287				options.generateKey = true
288				prompt := newPrompter(app)
289				options.keyPath, err = prompt.line("New key path (a bare name is placed in ~/.ssh)", generateDefault)
290				if err != nil {
291					return options, err
292				}
293				options.keyPath = normalizeSSHKeyPromptPath(service.Paths().SSHDir, options.keyPath)
294				options.comment, err = prompt.line("Key comment (blank = ssh-keygen default)", "")
295				if err != nil {
296					return options, err
297				}
298				options.comment = strings.TrimSpace(options.comment)
299			case "manual":
300				options.key, err = newPrompter(app).line("Key or public key path", filepath.Join(service.Paths().Home, ".ssh", "id_ed25519"))
301				if err != nil {
302					return options, err
303				}
304			default:
305				for _, key := range catalog.Candidates {
306					if key.Fingerprint == selected[0].Value {
307						if key.Agent != nil {
308							key, err = service.SelectAgentKey(ctx, *key.Agent, key.Fingerprint)
309							if err != nil {
310								return options, err
311							}
312						}
313						options.keyCandidate = &key
314						break
315					}
316				}
317				if options.keyCandidate == nil {
318					return options, errors.New("key picker returned an unknown fingerprint")
319				}
320			}
321			if err := prepareSSHWizardKey(ctx, app, service, &options); err != nil {
322				if errors.Is(err, errPromptCanceled) || errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {

66	// control and Ctrl-C retain native behavior; context cancellation kills only

82		cmd.Dir = request.Dir

Recommended APIs

```go
type KeyType string

const (
    KeyTypeEd25519   KeyType = "ed25519"
    KeyTypeEd25519SK KeyType = "ed25519-sk"
    KeyTypeECDSASK   KeyType = "ecdsa-sk"
)

type SecurityKeyOptions struct {
    Provider       string // "" normalizes to "internal"; otherwise absolute path
    Resident       bool
    VerifyRequired bool
    Application    string // bounded ssh: application; default "ssh:dev"
}
```

Add to KeyRequest:
- Type KeyType, with empty preserving ordinary Ed25519.
- SecurityKey SecurityKeyOptions.

Add content-free KeyPlan fields:
- KeyType
- SecurityKeyProvider
- SecurityKeyOptions
- KeygenPath and SSHClientPath
- Capability diagnostics

All options must be independently copied into the internal plan snapshot. Public plan fields never select execution authority.

Capability boundary

New stat-only ObserveSecurityKeyCapabilities(ctx, request) should report each resolved executable/provider path with a finite status:
- unavailable
- unsupported
- unknown

No ssh-keygen -K, ssh -Q, sc_auth, provider execution, hardware enumeration, or output-string inference during planning.

Specific classifications:
- Known Apple stock ssh-keygen/ssh with provider internal: USB FIDO unsupported.
- Custom builds and merely discovered external provider libraries: unknown, not capable.
- apple-secure-enclave: blocked with experimental/unverified diagnostic before any hardware action.
- Windows: preserve the existing validated filesystem contract, but do not infer FIDO compatibility from executable existence.

Important compatibility limitation: stat/path checks alone cannot prove an arbitrary client, generator, and provider are compatible. Under the instruction requiring compatibility, unknown must block automatic generation. I would not add an “assume capable” bypass or invent a supported classification from an installation path. A later explicit compatibility-attestation mechanism would need separate design; fake capability seams are test-only.

Guarded tool/provider identity

For SK generation, capture:
- The selected PATH ssh-keygen and ssh resolutions.
- Resolved absolute executable paths and file identities.
- The provider’s absolute path and file identity, unless internal.
- Any accepted path-resolution chain needed to reject substitution.

Revalidate before generation, public/private stub publication, and selected-key proof. Execute the captured generator, not a fresh PATH lookup. Bind generated candidate state to the tool/provider identities; later ordinary native SSH remains subject to the user’s environment, which documentation must distinguish.

Preserve the existing Ed25519 argv and behavior byte-for-byte.

Generation backend

Split SK generation from applyGeneratedKey rather than adding hardware cleanup exceptions throughout the ordinary Ed25519 function.

Expected argv:

```text
ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519-sk|ecdsa-sk -f <private staging path>
  -w internal|<absolute provider>
  -O application=ssh:...
  [-O resident]
  [-O verify-required]
  [-C comment]
```

Always supply -w, including internal, and unset inherited SSH_SK_PROVIDER. Do not add a touch-disabling option. Require Interactive; native ssh-keygen owns PIN, touch, and stub-passphrase interaction.

After native success:
1. Secure and inspect staged files using the existing guarded filesystem helpers.
2. Require the exact requested public algorithm.
3. Use the captured native ssh-keygen -y to verify the stub/public pair.
4. Mark SecurityKeyStub provenance, not ordinary private-key provenance.
5. Revalidate source/tool/provider identity and publish with no replacement.
6. Return the provider required in the v2 managed fragment.

Hardware effects and recovery

Add a separate content-free hardware-effect receipt to KeyResult, without overloading Created, which describes local files:

```go
type HardwareKeyEffect struct {
    Kind                 string // "fido"
    Status               string // "unknown" or "created"
    Resident             bool
    RecoveryIdentityPath string
    RecoveryPublicPath   string
}
```

- Before OnStarted: no claimed hardware effect.
- Once the generator starts: possible hardware mutation is unknown.
- Native success plus validated SK output: generation is observed, not authentication proof.
- After any started generation, do not blindly delete potentially useful stub staging files on failure.
- Preserve only safely identified, current-user-owned recovery files; return their paths, never contents.
- Resident credentials are never “rolled back,” overwritten, enumerated, or removed automatically.
- Error results remain non-actionable receipts, consistent with P2’s PublicationUnknown handling.

Selected-key proof changes

The present exact-proof path forces BatchMode=yes and noninteractive execution. SK PIN interaction therefore needs explicit propagation of BootstrapRequest.Interactive through both:
- runSSHProof / prepareExactProofConfig
- bootstrapProof / AuthenticationOperation.runPhase

Enable native interaction only for the selected hardware-backed key when authorized by that request. Preserve:
- publickey-only authentication;
- selected identity and agent restrictions;
- host-key policy;
- no password-broker fallback inside selected-key proof;
- ordinary preflight behavior and ProxyJump policy.

Bounded implementation scope after P2 commit

- New hardware types, passive observations, immutable bindings, and diagnostics.
- Separate FIDO generation backend and retained-effect receipts.
- Native hardware-key proof interaction.
- Regression tests for exact argv, algorithm mismatch, pointer mutation, tool/provider substitution, cancellation, publication collisions/recovery, inherited SSH_SK_PROVIDER, incompatible client/generator combinations, and Secure Enclave refusal.
- No automatic Secure Enclave provisioning, sc_auth parsing, resident-key download, PIV lifecycle, hardware installation, or live hardware tests.

P3 remains incomplete for automatic Secure Enclave creation and any toolchain whose capability cannot be established safely. Those limitations must stay explicit and must not be hidden by prematurely releasing v0.2.38.

729		}

731			return errors.New("--port must be between 1 and 65535")
732		}

734			return errors.New("--fleet-name requires --fleet")

736		if options.configOnly && (options.hasExistingKey() || options.generateKey || options.fleet || options.targetOS != "" || len(options.hopOS) > 0 || options.installOnWorkingJump || options.windowsAdminAuthorizedKeys) {
737			return errors.New("--config-only cannot be combined with key, route, bootstrap, or fleet flags")

742			}
743		}
744		if _, err := parseSSHOSOverrides(options.hopOS); err != nil {

746		}
747		if !interactive && !options.configOnly && !options.dryRun && !options.hasExistingKey() && !options.generateKey && options.auth != "existing" {
748			return errors.New("full setup requires --key or --generate-key outside an interactive terminal")

332	// normalizeSSHKeyPromptPath places a bare prompted key name under the SSH
333	// directory; explicit paths and flags keep their exact meaning.
334	func normalizeSSHKeyPromptPath(sshDir, value string) string {
335		value = strings.TrimSpace(value)
336		if value == "" || value == "." || value == ".." || strings.ContainsAny(value, `/\%$`) || strings.HasPrefix(value, "~") {
337			return value
338		}
339		return filepath.Join(sshDir, value)
340	}

343	func sshKeyPlanBlockedError(plan sshhost.KeyPlan) error {
344		if len(plan.Diagnostics) > 0 {
345			diagnostic := plan.Diagnostics[0]
346			reason := diagnostic.Message
347			if reason == "" {
348				reason = strings.ReplaceAll(diagnostic.Code, "_", " ")
349			}
350			return fmt.Errorf("SSH key plan is blocked: %s: %w", reason, sshhost.ErrBlocked)
351		}
352		return fmt.Errorf("SSH key plan is blocked: %w", sshhost.ErrBlocked)
353	}

394			if !candidate.Provenance.Private && !candidate.Provenance.SecurityKeyStub && !candidate.Provenance.Agent {
395				return errors.New("only the public key was found; load its signer into the SSH agent or choose a private key")
396			}
397		}
398		plan, err := planSSHSetupKey(ctx, app, service, *options, true)
399		if err != nil {
400			return err
401		}
402		if !plan.Ready() {
403			renderSSHKeyDiagnostics(app, plan.Diagnostics)
404			return errors.New("selected key is not ready")
405		}
406		options.keyPlan = &plan
407		return nil
408	}
