    result = subprocess.run(base + flags, env=env, cwd=f, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=35)
    combined = result.stdout + result.stderr
    for forbidden in [sentinel, 'PRIVATE_RESPONSE_MUST_NOT_ESCAPE', 'BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY', 'BEGIN PRIVATE KEY']:
        assert forbidden not in combined, 'sensitive fixture output escaped'
    return result

def contains(value, key, expected):
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return value.get(key) == expected or any(contains(v, key, expected) for v in value.values())
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return any(contains(v, key, expected) for v in value)
    return False

before_files, before_calls = snapshot(), calls()
preview = invoke(['--experimental', '--native-context', '--dry-run'])
assert preview.returncode == 0, preview.stdout + preview.stderr
assert json.loads(preview.stdout)['status'] == 'intent_only'
assert calls() == before_calls and snapshot() == before_files
for flags in [['--yes', '--experimental'], ['--yes', '--native-context']]:
    denied = invoke(flags)
    assert denied.returncode != 0, 'missing approval was accepted'
    assert calls() == before_calls and not (f / 'created').exists(), 'missing approval executed native creation'
created = invoke(['--yes', '--experimental', '--native-context'])
document = json.loads(created.stdout)
assert contains(document, 'status', 'created'), created.stdout + created.stderr
assert contains(document, 'item_id', '22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222'), created.stdout
assert contains(document, 'native_context_status', 'observed_consistent'), created.stdout
assert contains(document, 'endpoint_status', 'unverified'), created.stdout
assert not contains(document, 'binding_status', 'verified'), 'Bitwarden was falsely endpoint-bound'
assert 'public_line' not in created.stdout
assert snapshot() == before_files, 'standalone vault creation changed SSH configuration/key files'
assert (f / 'created').exists(), 'synthetic helper did not observe exactly one create'
print('Real CLI with harmless native Bitwarden fixture passed (exit %s).' % created.returncode)
print(created.stdout)
print('Static dry-run and missing approvals made no provider calls; SSH files unchanged; no real vault or credentials used.')

Architecture

- internal/cli: Cobra assembly/adapters/rendering.
- internal/tui: Bubble Tea state/rendering.
- internal/sshhost: OpenSSH config, source-bound key plans, key generation, public bootstrap and proofs.
- internal/sshflow: onboarding orchestration, immutable review, source/machine/Fleet/Herdr binding and result ledgers.
- internal/sshdiscovery: bounded explicit LAN/Tailscale observations.
- internal/sshcredential: existing password brokerage/providers and bounded native provider command runner.
- NEW internal/sshvault: explicit new SSH vault-key creation, not existing-key migration.
- internal/herdrremote: native Herdr CLI, no catalog rewriting.
- internal/fleet: user remotes.toml plus strict generated remotes.d fragments.
- internal/tuiissue: finite typed guidance/installation actions.

Relevant repository instructions — preserve verbatim

“Persisted intent, observed facts, and guarded action plans are separate layers. Unknown, failed, skipped, loading, or stale observations never become a false clean/closed fact.”

“Filesystem transitions must retain path traversal/symlink, same-filesystem, source revalidation, and rollback/reconciliation checks.”

“The user's OpenSSH configuration is durable connection truth. Ordinary setup/remove own only the exact top-level `Include ~/.ssh/dev.d/*.conf` and structurally valid fragments in `~/.ssh/dev.d`; key bootstrap sends public material only and has no private-key transfer or remote-key revocation lifecycle.”

“SSH initialization is report-before-apply; managed host changes are confined to canonical dev-owned fragments. Full bootstrap requires an explicit existing key or explicit generation, registers fleet only when explicitly selected, and reports interrupted remote installation as unknown rather than pretending to roll it back.”

“SSH wizard permission preflight may separately review and apply metadata-only tightening on exact current-user-owned canonical/selected paths. It never recursively chmods, changes ownership, guesses ACLs, or widens permissions; completed repairs survive later cancellation. Listing and dry-run never repair permissions. Local key listing evaluates OpenSSH only behind explicit `--alias`; selected key material remains service-bound and is revalidated before configuration changes and bootstrap.”

“`dev ssh key doctor` exposes the same permission Plan/Apply with bounded metadata-only key discovery; `--key` restricts the reviewed scope, and `--fix` requires a complete safe plan plus confirmation. Default doctor never mutates, reads private contents, or queries agents/remotes. Batch repairs revalidate the whole reviewed union and retain successful tightening on partial failure.”

“Source-aware SSH setup can use `--auth existing` without installing a key, and registers only explicitly selected `--to fleet|herdr|both` destinations. Tailscale SSH advertisement is advisory; its port-22 endpoint is not an authorized_keys bootstrap target. Preserve the key-authentication guard and never treat Tailscale policy login as proof that a selected public key worked. Names, ports and cached observations never authorize machine merges; binding/source changes invalidate reviewed plans.”

“Fleet-source SSH discovery selects explicit hosts without recursive fleet traversal. Local ProxyJump imports never copy remote identity/agent/trust paths; cached route data cannot authorize apply. `connect --on` is one interactive fixed-helper session with no agent forwarding or arbitrary command payload. Normal SSH errors retain child exit status.”

“Controller password brokerage uses a private per-operation Unix socket or protected Windows pipe, never password argv/environment/files. Exact host/user/port/route contexts gate replies and save evidence. Remote source-to-target credentials remain outside this feature; native key/passphrase interaction is separate.”

“System stores and explicitly selected Bitwarden contain saved passwords; the TOML ledger never does.”

“English and zh-TW MkDocs pages are maintained as a pair.”

“Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change.”

“Never infer complete Windows validation from an advisory step's success conclusion; inspect logs and require the dedicated native gates.”

Ongoing safety constraints

- Never stage the user’s .claude/plans or .specstory changes in feature commits.
- Do not change the user’s real SSH config, keys, vault, agents, hardware or services merely to test code.
- Real vault/hardware experiments require separate consent. None has occurred in this continuation.
- Never ask the user to paste BW_SESSION, master passwords, private keys or passphrases into chat.
- No private/session bytes in logs, errors, public JSON, command arguments or scratch files.
- Bitwarden’s existing session is supplied through its native environment only; private key input goes through stdin.
- “Never written by dev” and best-effort wiping are not guarantees against OS swap, core dumps, native-provider storage or perfect memory erasure.
- No automatic local private-key deletion after import, vault-item deletion, hardware credential revocation, PIV slot overwrite, agent-service disabling or provider configuration change.
- No force push, amend, hook bypass, destructive reset/restore or deleting user files.
- Native Windows operations fail closed where identity/ACL behavior is unsupported.
- Read-only public metadata and owned temporary fixtures are allowed; real vault contents/hardware are not test fixtures.
- Do not read raw agent .output transcripts. They are symlinks to full conversation JSONL.
- Automatic agent/task notifications are not human approval.

Bitwarden native-context mode:
- Schema version pinned to 2026.3.0.
- Personal vault only, no implicit organization/collection.
- Requires Experimental AND NativeContextApproved.
- Endpoint-attested mode stays unsupported.
- Current user/session/profile/tool context is delegated native authority, not an endpoint pin.
- BW_SESSION is a decryption credential, not account/server identity.
- Plan-time metadata commands use the captured explicit environment/cwd.
- Plan retains private comparison material, not session-bearing environment or public session hash.
- Apply captures a fresh context, compares session/profile/tool/execution environment, and all calls use that same frozen context.
- No os.Setenv swapping.
- All BW metadata/create calls force --nointeraction, preventing private JSON stdin from becoming an unlock response.
- No login/unlock/configuration update or native vault-data parsing.
- Native binary and narrowly recognized @bitwarden/cli Node entrypoints supported; arbitrary wrappers/runtime shims fail closed.
- Captures canonical entrypoint/runtime/package manifest/version/root and requested resolution.
- PATH is resolved from frozen context, not late ambient state.
- Portable bw-data beside process.execPath takes precedence even over APPDATA override; for Node this is beside the bound node executable. Presence/absence and actual profile are bound.
- Profile/data.json checks are metadata-only.
- ServerURL is sanitized advisory display; EndpointStatus always unverified and legacy BindingStatus stays unknown.
- NativeContextStatus observed_consistent is not transactional native config or supply-chain attestation.
- Internal native configuration can change without session/user changing; this is a disclosed delegation boundary, not solved by hashing a session.

- Rejects permits, audit, unknown flags, inheritance-control/deferred/generic/interop semantics, malformed buffers.

- Separate vault prepare/review/apply before returning selected key to normal SSH form.

- No passive provider queries in key picker; dependency presence is stat-only.
- Static standalone dry-run executes no native provider/agent.

- Crypto-random controller attempt_id once per prepared vault action.

- B completion matched by attempt ID exits running even not_started/no receipt.
- Merge ledger into cancellation and SSH completion reports.
- Late results/ledger never grant key-selection authority.
- Preserve monotonic created/item ID/FP facts, but do not let old consistent context overwrite later uncertainty; conflicting nonempty identities must not silently overwrite.
- Tests planned for all event interleavings and two identical-shaped unknown attempts.

Research conclusions

Secure Enclave:
- Native man page confirms:
    sc_auth create-ctk-identity -l LABEL -k p-256-ne -t bio
    sc_auth list-ctk-identities [-t sha1|sha256|ssh] [-e hex|b64]
- Listing is human-readable, localized, arbitrary labels/blank columns.
- No documented machine-readable create receipt/stable listing grammar.
- -t ssh changes hash representation; does not filter SSH identities.
- Original public gist mapping was verified offline:
  SHA1 of 65-byte EC point matches CTK hash;
  SHA256 of complete SK public blob matches SSH fingerprint.
  This is one fixture, not general API proof.
- KEYCHAIN_CERTIFICATES exact hash filtering is documented.
- -K writes files, can overwrite/prompt, can return success with zero keys.
- Direct Apple sk_enroll is reported unsupported; not a substitute.
- Automatic creation remains blocked.
- Sources in guide/backlog:
  https://gist.github.com/arianvp/5f59f1783e3eaf1a2d4cd8e952bb4acf
  https://keith.github.io/xcode-man-pages/sc_auth.8.html
  https://keith.github.io/xcode-man-pages/ssh-keychain.8.html
  Apple OpenSSH source and upstream report.

Bitwarden:
- Pinned CLI source commit:
    c20753e4dae029d6155565682dc79718f9aeb426
- status.serverUrl is only base, null for both US/EU.
- Read-only config server cannot distinguish cloud regions.
- Independent API/identity overrides can differ even with non-null base.
- Explicit native-context mode therefore has distinct authority and permanent endpoint-unverified status.
- This machine’s bw was inspected with file only, not executed:
    /Users/zhouhanru/.local/share/mise/installs/node/lts/bin/bw
    /usr/bin/env node script
- Thus Node package/runtime support was necessary; native-only binary support would exclude the user’s installation.
- No real session/unlock data was read.

Other recommendations:
- Secretive: Secure Enclave-backed agent, no dev provisioning.
- Apple Passwords: no documented SSH-key/agent backend.
- Keychain passphrase storage does not eliminate private-key file.
- KeePassXC: encrypted DB/native agent integration, not non-exportability guarantee.
- ssh-tpm-agent: Linux-oriented TPM2/sealed local files, generic agent only.
- gpg-agent/OpenPGP/PIV: separate native lifecycle; no provisioning by dev.
- Windows upstream FIDO/U2F docs do not establish Windows Hello storage support.

150	// Lines renders only the public projection shared by terminal and dashboard.

152		lines := []string{"Provider: " + p.Request.Provider, "Title: " + p.Request.Title}

154			lines = append(lines, "Controller attempt ID: "+p.AttemptID)
155		}
156		if p.IntentOnly {
157			lines = append(lines, "Intent-only preview: account, vault, native context and agent are UNOBSERVED. This is not an apply-ready service plan.", "Requested account ID: "+p.Request.AccountID, "Requested vault ID: "+p.Request.VaultID)
158		} else if !p.Request.Desktop {
159			lines = append(lines, "Reviewed account ID: "+p.AccountID, "Reviewed user ID: "+p.UserID, "Reviewed vault: "+p.VaultID+" "+p.VaultName, "Advisory server label: "+p.ServerLabel, "CLI path observed: "+p.ToolPath, "CLI version: "+p.Version)
160		}
161		if p.NativeProfilePath != "" {
162			lines = append(lines, "Native profile: "+p.NativeProfilePath, "Native entrypoint: "+p.NativeEntrypoint, "Native runtime: "+p.NativeRuntime, "Native package root: "+p.NativePackageRoot, "Native working directory: "+p.NativeCWD)
163		}
164		if p.Request.Provider == "bitwarden" && !p.Request.Desktop {
165			lines = append(lines, fmt.Sprintf("Experimental approval: %t; native-context delegation approval: %t", p.Request.Experimental, p.Request.NativeContextApproved))
166		}
167		if p.EndpointStatus != "" {
168			lines = append(lines, "Endpoint status: "+p.EndpointStatus)
169		}
170		return append(lines, p.Notes...)
171	}

173	func (r VaultKeyReceipt) Lines() []string {
174		lines := []string{fmt.Sprintf("Vault item/attempt retained: %s · %s · %s", r.Provider, r.Title, r.Status), "Reviewed account/vault: " + r.AccountID + " / " + r.VaultID}
175		if r.AttemptID != "" {
176			lines = append(lines, "Controller attempt ID: "+r.AttemptID)
177		}
178		if r.ItemID != "" {
179			lines = append(lines, "Item ID: "+r.ItemID)
180		} else if len(r.ConflictingIdentities) > 0 {
181			lines = append(lines, "No unambiguous primary item ID; conflicting observations are retained below.")
182		} else {
183			lines = append(lines, "No item ID was observed; inspect the native vault before any new creation attempt.")
184		}
185		if r.Fingerprint != "" {
186			lines = append(lines, "Fingerprint: "+r.Fingerprint)
187		}
188		if r.BindingStatus != "" {
189			lines = append(lines, "Destination binding: "+r.BindingStatus)
190		}
191		if r.NativeContextStatus != "" {
192			lines = append(lines, "Native context: "+r.NativeContextStatus)
193		}
194		if r.EndpointStatus != "" {
195			lines = append(lines, "Endpoints: "+r.EndpointStatus)
196		}
197		if r.ProfilePath != "" {
198			lines = append(lines, "Native profile: "+r.ProfilePath)
199		}
200		for _, conflict := range r.ConflictingIdentities {
201			lines = append(lines, fmt.Sprintf("Conflicting identity observed for this attempt: %s account=%s vault=%s item=%s fingerprint=%s; reconcile the native vault.", conflict.Provider, conflict.AccountID, conflict.VaultID, conflict.ItemID, conflict.Fingerprint))
202		}
203		return lines
204	}

216	func CloneVaultKeyReceipt(receipt VaultKeyReceipt) VaultKeyReceipt {
217		receipt.ConflictingIdentities = append([]VaultKeyIdentity(nil), receipt.ConflictingIdentities...)
218		return receipt

221	func CloneVaultKeyReceipts(receipts []VaultKeyReceipt) []VaultKeyReceipt {
222		if receipts == nil {
223			return nil
224		}
225		result := make([]VaultKeyReceipt, len(receipts))
226		for i, receipt := range receipts {
227			result[i] = CloneVaultKeyReceipt(receipt)
228		}

232	// RetainVaultKeyReceipt is a display/reconciliation ledger, never key authority.
233	// IDs/created existence are monotonic; context observations follow controller
234	// ordering, so delayed consistent replies cannot erase later uncertainty.
235	func RetainVaultKeyReceipt(receipts []VaultKeyReceipt, receipt *VaultKeyReceipt) []VaultKeyReceipt {
236		result := CloneVaultKeyReceipts(receipts)
237		if receipt == nil {
238			return result
239		}
240		if receipt.AttemptID != "" {
241			for i, existing := range result {
242				if existing.AttemptID == receipt.AttemptID {
243					result[i] = mergeVaultKeyReceipt(existing, *receipt)
244					return result
245				}
246			}
247		}
248		// Missing controller identity never authorizes structural deduplication.
249		return append(result, CloneVaultKeyReceipt(*receipt))
250	}

254	}

256	func vaultIdentitiesConflict(a, b VaultKeyIdentity) bool {
257		for _, pair := range [][2]string{{a.Provider, b.Provider}, {a.AccountID, b.AccountID}, {a.VaultID, b.VaultID}, {a.ItemID, b.ItemID}, {a.Fingerprint, b.Fingerprint}} {
258			if pair[0] != "" && pair[1] != "" && pair[0] != pair[1] {
259				return true
260			}
261		}
262		return false
263	}
264	
265	func mergeVaultKeyReceipt(existing, incoming VaultKeyReceipt) VaultKeyReceipt {
266		conflict := vaultIdentitiesConflict(vaultReceiptIdentity(existing), vaultReceiptIdentity(incoming))
267		addConflict := func(value VaultKeyIdentity) {
268			for _, known := range existing.ConflictingIdentities {
269				if known == value {
270					return
271				}
272			}
273			existing.ConflictingIdentities = append(existing.ConflictingIdentities, value)
274		}
275		if conflict {
276			addConflict(vaultReceiptIdentity(incoming))
277		}
278		for _, value := range incoming.ConflictingIdentities {
279			addConflict(value)
280		}
281		fill := func(target *string, value string) {
282			if *target == "" {
283				*target = value
284			}
285		}
286		if !conflict {
287			fill(&existing.Provider, incoming.Provider)
288			fill(&existing.AccountID, incoming.AccountID)
289			fill(&existing.VaultID, incoming.VaultID)
290			fill(&existing.ItemID, incoming.ItemID)
291			fill(&existing.Fingerprint, incoming.Fingerprint)
292		}
293		fill(&existing.Title, incoming.Title)
294		fill(&existing.ProfilePath, incoming.ProfilePath)
295		rank := func(status string) int {
296			switch status {
297			case "created":
298				return 2
299			case "unknown":
300				return 1
301			}
302			return 0
303		}
304		if rank(incoming.Status) > rank(existing.Status) {
305			existing.Status = incoming.Status
306		}
307		if incoming.Observation > existing.Observation {
308			if incoming.BindingStatus != "" {
309				existing.BindingStatus = incoming.BindingStatus
310			}
311			if incoming.NativeContextStatus != "" {
312				existing.NativeContextStatus = incoming.NativeContextStatus
313			}
314			if incoming.EndpointStatus != "" {
315				existing.EndpointStatus = incoming.EndpointStatus
316			}
317			existing.Observation = incoming.Observation
318		} else if incoming.Observation == existing.Observation {
319			fill(&existing.BindingStatus, incoming.BindingStatus)
320			fill(&existing.NativeContextStatus, incoming.NativeContextStatus)
321			fill(&existing.EndpointStatus, incoming.EndpointStatus)
322			if incoming.BindingStatus == "unknown" {
323				existing.BindingStatus = "unknown"
324			}
325			if incoming.NativeContextStatus == "unknown" {
326				existing.NativeContextStatus = "unknown"
327			}
328			if incoming.EndpointStatus == "unverified" {
329				existing.EndpointStatus = "unverified"
330			}
331		}
332		if len(existing.ConflictingIdentities) > 0 {
333			existing.BindingStatus, existing.NativeContextStatus = "unknown", "unknown"
334		}
335		return existing
336	}
337

35	func newSSHKeyCreateCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
36		var options sshVaultCreateOptions
37		cmd := &cobra.Command{Use: "create", Short: "Create a new SSH key in an explicitly reviewed vault", Args: cobra.NoArgs,
38			Long: `Create a new SSH key in 1Password, or explicitly opt into experimental
39	Bitwarden in-memory generation under a reviewed native profile. Bitwarden needs
40	both --experimental and --native-context; --yes never substitutes for either.
41	--desktop is a separate interactive Bitwarden GUI handoff: it reports newly
42	visible agent keys, not vault item creation. No existing private key is imported
43	and no item is deleted. No SSH configuration or remote key installation occurs.
44	--dry-run emits unobserved intent only and never invokes op, bw, node or agents.`,
45			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
46				options.experimentalSet = cmd.Flags().Changed("experimental")
47				options.nativeContextSet = cmd.Flags().Changed("native-context")
48				ctx := cmd.Context()
49				if options.json || !app.interactive() {
50					var cancel context.CancelFunc
51					ctx, cancel = context.WithTimeout(ctx, 2*time.Minute)
52					defer cancel()
53				}
54				_, err := runSSHVaultCreation(ctx, app, options)
55				return err
56			},

73	func collectSSHVaultRequest(ctx context.Context, app *App, options sshVaultCreateOptions) (sshflow.VaultKeyRequest, error) {
74		request := options.request
75		interactive := app.interactive() && !options.json
76		wizard := request.Provider == ""
77		if wizard {
78			if !interactive {
79				return request, errors.New("--provider is required outside the interactive vault wizard")
80			}
81			service, err := app.sshHosts()
82			if err != nil {
83				return request, err
84			}
85			var choices []picker.Item
86			for _, choice := range sshVaultKeyChoices(service, false) {
87				value := choice.VaultAction
88				if choice.UnavailableReason != "" {
89					value = "unavailable:" + value
90				}
91				choices = append(choices, picker.Item{Value: value, Label: choice.Label, Description: choice.Description})
92			}
93			for {
94				selected, err := sshPick(ctx, app, "Choose SSH vault key creation", choices, false)
95				if err != nil {
96					return request, err
97				}
98				if strings.HasPrefix(selected[0].Value, "unavailable:") {
99					fmt.Fprintln(app.Err, selected[0].Description)
100					continue
101				}
102				choice, err := sshVaultRequestForAction(selected[0].Value, request.Title)
103				if err != nil {
104					return request, err
105				}
106				request.Provider, request.Desktop = choice.Provider, choice.Desktop
107				break
108			}
109		}
110		if request.Desktop {
111			return request, nil
112		}
113		prompt := newPrompter(app)
114		if interactive && !options.yes {
115			var err error
116			if request.AccountID == "" {
117				request.AccountID, err = prompt.line("Exact native account/user ID (blank reviews the current account)", "")
118				if err != nil {
119					return request, err
120				}
121			}
122			if request.Provider == "1password" && request.VaultID == "" {
123				request.VaultID, err = prompt.line("Exact 1Password vault ID (not its display name)", "")
124				if err != nil {
125					return request, err
126				}
127			}
128			if wizard || options.forPicker {
129				request.Title, err = prompt.line("New vault SSH key title", request.Title)
130				if err != nil {
131					return request, err
132				}
133			}
134		}
135		if !options.dryRun && (options.yes || !interactive) && request.AccountID == "" {
136			return request, errors.New("an exact --account ID is required for unattended/--yes vault creation; use the interactive wizard to review the current account")
137		}
138		if request.Provider == "bitwarden" {
139			if !request.Experimental {
140				if !interactive || options.yes || options.experimentalSet {
141					return request, sshvault.ErrExperimental
142				}
143				approved, err := prompt.confirm("Approve experimental in-memory key generation? Private bytes briefly enter process memory/native input; no guarantee covers swap, core dumps, native persistence or perfect erasure", false)
144				if err != nil {
145					return request, err
146				}
147				if !approved {
148					return request, errPromptCanceled
149				}
150				request.Experimental = true
151			}
152			if !request.NativeContextApproved {
153				if !interactive || options.yes || options.nativeContextSet {
154					return request, sshvault.ErrUnsupportedContext
155				}
156				approved, err := prompt.confirm("Separately approve delegating endpoints/configuration to the reviewed Bitwarden native profile? Endpoint status stays unverified and destination binding stays unknown", false)
157				if err != nil {
158					return request, err
159				}
160				if !approved {
161					return request, errPromptCanceled
162				}
163				request.NativeContextApproved = true
164			}
165		}
166		return request, nil
167	}
168	
169	func runSSHVaultCreation(ctx context.Context, app *App, options sshVaultCreateOptions) (sshflow.VaultKeyResult, error) {
170		if _, native := app.In.(fileDescriptor); !native {
171			app.In = bufio.NewReader(app.In)
172		}
173		document := sshVaultCreateDocument{SchemaVersion: 1, Kind: "ssh_key_create", Status: "not_started", DryRun: options.dryRun}
174		finish := func(result sshflow.VaultKeyResult, err error) (sshflow.VaultKeyResult, error) {
175			if err != nil {
176				document.ErrorCode = sshVaultErrorCode(err)
177			}
178			if options.json {
179				if encodeErr := writeSSHJSON(app, document); encodeErr != nil {
180					return result, encodeErr
181				}
182			} else if document.Result != nil {
183				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, strings.Join(document.Result.Lines(), "\n"))
184			} else if document.Preview != nil {
185				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Vault action: "+document.Status)
186			}
187			return result, err
188		}
189		request, err := collectSSHVaultRequest(ctx, app, options)
190		if err != nil {
191			document.Status = "blocked"
192			return finish(sshflow.VaultKeyResult{}, err)
193		}
194		request, _, err = normalizeSSHVaultRequest(request)
195		if err != nil {
196			document.Status = "blocked"
197			return finish(sshflow.VaultKeyResult{}, publicSSHVaultError(err))
198		}
199		if options.dryRun {
200			preview := sshflow.VaultKeyPreview{Request: request, IntentOnly: true, Notes: []string{"Account, vault, native context and agent are UNOBSERVED. No provider/client/agent was queried. Actual creation requires a fresh service-bound native account/vault plan and separate approval; no readiness or creation is implied."}}
201			if request.Provider == "bitwarden" && !request.Desktop {
202				preview.EndpointStatus = sshvault.EndpointUnverified
203				preview.Notes = append(preview.Notes, "Experimental native-profile mode never attests endpoints or promises complete memory erasure.")
204			}
205			document.Status, document.Preview = "intent_only", &preview
206			if !options.json {
207				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, strings.Join(preview.Lines(), "\n"))
208			}
209			return finish(sshflow.VaultKeyResult{Status: "intent_only", Context: preview, AgentStatus: "unobserved"}, nil)
210		}
211		if request.Desktop && (!app.interactive() || options.json) {
212			document.Status = "blocked"
213			return finish(sshflow.VaultKeyResult{}, errors.New("Bitwarden desktop handoff requires an interactive terminal and explicit fingerprint selection"))
214		}
215		prepared, err := prepareSSHVaultKey(ctx, app, request)
216		if err != nil {
217			document.Status = "blocked"
218			return finish(sshflow.VaultKeyResult{}, err)
219		}
220		preview := prepared.Preview()

14	func (m Model) openSSHVaultKeyForm(parent sshDialog, action string) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
15		if m.actions.SSH.PrepareVaultKey == nil || m.actions.SSH.Workflow == nil {
16			parent.err = errors.New("Vault-key creation is unavailable in this dashboard")
17			m.sshUI.dialog = parent
18			return m, nil
19		}
20		m.pauseSSHBackground()
21		m.mergeSSHVaultReceipts(parent.onboarding.VaultReceipts)
22		alias := parent.value("alias")
23		if parent.onboarding.Profile != nil {
24			alias = parent.onboarding.Profile.Alias
25		}
26		request := sshflow.VaultKeyRequest{Title: "SSH key for " + alias}
27		switch action {
28		case "1password":
29			request.Provider = "1password"
30		case "bitwarden-native":
31			request.Provider, request.VaultID = "bitwarden", "personal"
32		case "bitwarden-desktop":
33			request.Provider, request.Desktop, request.Title = "bitwarden", true, "Bitwarden desktop handoff"
34		default:
35			parent.err = errors.New("Choose a supported vault action")
36			m.sshUI.dialog = parent
37			return m, nil
38		}
39		form := sshDialog{kind: "vault-form", title: "Separate vault key creation", parent: &parent, vaultRequest: request}
40		if !request.Desktop {
41			form.addField("vaultaccount", "Account ID", "")
42			form.addField("vaultid", "Vault ID", request.VaultID)
43			form.addField("vaulttitle", "Item title", request.Title)
44			if request.Provider == "bitwarden" {
45				form.addField("vaultexperimental", "Experimental", "no")
46				form.addField("vaultnative", "Native context", "no")
47			}
48		}
49		m.sshUI.dialog = form
50		if request.Desktop {
51			return m.prepareSSHVaultKey()
52		}
53		return m, m.focusSSHField(0)
54	}

56	func (m Model) prepareSSHVaultKey() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {

63			if r.Provider == "bitwarden" && (!r.Experimental || !r.NativeContextApproved) {
64				d.err = errors.New("Bitwarden requires two separate approvals: experimental in-memory generation and native-profile endpoint delegation. Endpoints remain unverified")
65				return m, nil
66			}
67		}
68		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(m.baseContext())
69		d.vaultRequest, d.vaultCancel, d.kind, d.err = r, cancel, "vault-preparing", nil
70		d.body = "Reading the explicitly selected native vault context or captured agent baseline; no item is being created."

81	func (m Model) finishSSHVaultPreparation(msg sshEventMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
82		d := &m.sshUI.dialog
83		if d.kind != "vault-preparing" {
84			return m, nil
85		}
86		d.vaultCancel = nil
87		if msg.err != nil || msg.vaultPlan == nil {
88			d.err = msg.err
89			if d.err == nil {
90				d.err = errors.New("Vault preparation returned no reviewed plan")
91			}
92			if d.vaultRequest.Desktop {
93				d.kind, d.body = "vault-result", "No complete Bitwarden agent baseline was obtained; no vault item was created by dev."
94				return m, nil
95			}
96			d.kind = "vault-form"
97			return m, m.focusSSHField(d.index)
98		}
99		d.vaultPlan, d.kind = msg.vaultPlan, "vault-review"
100		d.body = strings.Join(msg.vaultPlan.Preview().Lines(), "\n")
101		return m, nil
102	}
103	
104	func (m Model) applySSHVaultKey() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
105		d := m.sshUI.dialog
106		if d.kind != "vault-review" || d.vaultPlan == nil {
107			return m, nil
108		}
109		attemptID := d.vaultPlan.Preview().AttemptID
110		if attemptID == "" || m.sshUI.vaultCompleted[attemptID] {
111			m.sshUI.dialog.err = errors.New("Prepare a new vault action; this reviewed attempt is missing or already completed")
112			return m, nil
113		}
114		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(m.baseContext())
115		workflow, err := m.actions.SSH.Workflow(ctx, SSHWorkflowRequest{Action: "vault-key", Vault: d.vaultPlan})
116		if err != nil {
117			cancel()
118			m.sshUI.dialog.err = err
119			return m, nil
120		}
121		m.sshUI.generation++
122		generation := m.sshUI.generation
123		parent := d.parent
124		m.sshUI.dialog = sshDialog{kind: "vault-running", title: "Vault key action running", body: "Cancellation waits for the actual creation receipt; no SSH setup is being applied.", parent: parent, vaultPlan: d.vaultPlan, vaultAttemptID: attemptID, vaultCancel: cancel}
125		return m, tea.Exec(workflow, func(err error) tea.Msg {
126			cancel()
127			return afterExec(sshEventMsg{kind: "vault-result", generation: generation, vaultAttemptID: attemptID, vaultPlan: d.vaultPlan, vaultResult: workflow.Result().Vault, vaultParent: parent, err: err})
128		})
129	}
130	
131	func copySSHVaultResult(result sshflow.VaultKeyResult) sshflow.VaultKeyResult {
132		result.Keys = append([]sshflow.VaultAgentKey(nil), result.Keys...)
133		result.Notes = append([]string(nil), result.Notes...)
134		result.Context.Notes = append([]string(nil), result.Context.Notes...)
135		if result.Receipt != nil {
136			receipt := sshflow.CloneVaultKeyReceipt(*result.Receipt)
137			result.Receipt = &receipt
138		}
139		return result
140	}
141	
142	func (m Model) finishSSHVaultResult(msg sshEventMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
143		attemptID := msg.vaultAttemptID
144		if attemptID == "" && msg.vaultPlan != nil {
145			attemptID = msg.vaultPlan.Preview().AttemptID
146		}
147		if attemptID == "" && msg.vaultResult != nil {
148			attemptID = msg.vaultResult.AttemptID
149		}
150		if attemptID == "" && msg.vaultResult != nil && msg.vaultResult.Receipt != nil {
151			attemptID = msg.vaultResult.Receipt.AttemptID
152		}
153		if msg.vaultResult == nil {
154			preview := sshflow.VaultKeyPreview{}
155			if msg.vaultPlan != nil {
156				preview = msg.vaultPlan.Preview()
157			}
158			unknown := sshflow.VaultKeyResult{AttemptID: attemptID, Status: "unknown", Context: preview, AgentStatus: "not_checked", Notes: []string{"The started workflow returned no outcome. Inspect the native vault before another creation attempt; do not retry automatically."}}
159			if !preview.Request.Desktop {
160				unknown.Receipt = &sshflow.VaultKeyReceipt{AttemptID: attemptID, Observation: sshflow.NextVaultObservation(), Provider: preview.Request.Provider, Title: preview.Request.Title, AccountID: preview.AccountID, VaultID: preview.VaultID, Status: "unknown", BindingStatus: "unknown", NativeContextStatus: "unknown", EndpointStatus: preview.EndpointStatus, ProfilePath: preview.NativeProfilePath}
161			}
162			msg.vaultResult = &unknown
163		}
164		result := copySSHVaultResult(*msg.vaultResult)
165		result.AttemptID = attemptID
166		if result.Receipt != nil {
167			result.Receipt.AttemptID = attemptID
168		}
169		before := m.sshUI.vaultReceipts
170		m.sshUI.vaultReceipts = sshflow.RetainVaultKeyReceipt(before, result.Receipt)
171		changed := !reflect.DeepEqual(before, m.sshUI.vaultReceipts)
172		completed := m.sshUI.vaultCompleted[attemptID]
173		active := attemptID != "" && !completed && m.sshUI.dialog.kind == "vault-running" && m.sshUI.dialog.vaultAttemptID == attemptID
174		if attemptID != "" {
175			if m.sshUI.vaultCompleted == nil {
176				m.sshUI.vaultCompleted = map[string]bool{}
177			}
178			m.sshUI.vaultCompleted[attemptID] = true
179		}
180		if !active {
181			// A completion from A must never cancel, replace or restore B's dialog.
182			// Late receipts are model-owned facts only, never fresh key selection.
183			if changed {
184				m.status = "Vault receipt retained for attempt " + attemptID + "; current action and SSH fields are unchanged"
185				if (m.sshUI.dialog.kind == "vault-result" || m.sshUI.dialog.kind == "vault-keys") && m.sshUI.dialog.vaultAttemptID == attemptID && m.sshUI.dialog.vaultResult != nil {
186					m.sshUI.dialog.vaultResult.Keys = nil
187					m.sshUI.dialog.vaultResult.AgentStatus = "not_selected"
188					m.sshUI.dialog.options = nil
189					m.sshUI.dialog.kind = "vault-result"
190				}
191				m.refreshSSHVaultReceiptBody()
192			}
193			return m, nil
194		}
195		parent := m.sshUI.dialog.parent
196		if result.Status != "created" && result.Status != "observed" {
197			result.Keys = nil
198		}
199		m.sshUI.generation++
200		m.sshUI.dialog = sshDialog{kind: "vault-result", title: "Vault action receipt — separate from SSH setup", err: msg.err, parent: parent, vaultAttemptID: attemptID, vaultResult: &result}
201		m.refreshSSHVaultReceiptBody()
202		m.status = "Vault action result retained; no SSH setup was applied"
203		return m, nil
204	}
205	
206	func (m *Model) mergeSSHVaultReceipts(receipts []sshflow.VaultKeyReceipt) []sshflow.VaultKeyReceipt {
207		for _, receipt := range receipts {
208			m.sshUI.vaultReceipts = sshflow.RetainVaultKeyReceipt(m.sshUI.vaultReceipts, &receipt)
209		}
210		return sshflow.CloneVaultKeyReceipts(m.sshUI.vaultReceipts)
211	}
212	
213	func (m *Model) refreshSSHVaultReceiptBody() {
214		d := &m.sshUI.dialog
215		if d.kind != "vault-result" || d.vaultResult == nil {
216			return
217		}
218		for _, receipt := range m.sshUI.vaultReceipts {
219			if receipt.AttemptID != "" && receipt.AttemptID == d.vaultAttemptID {
220				copy := sshflow.CloneVaultKeyReceipt(receipt)
221				d.vaultResult.Receipt = &copy
222				d.vaultResult.BindingStatus, d.vaultResult.NativeContextStatus, d.vaultResult.EndpointStatus = copy.BindingStatus, copy.NativeContextStatus, copy.EndpointStatus
223				if copy.Status == "created" || copy.Status == "unknown" {
224					d.vaultResult.Status = copy.Status
225				}
226				break
227			}
228		}
229		lines := d.vaultResult.Lines()
230		for _, receipt := range m.sshUI.vaultReceipts {
231			if receipt.AttemptID != "" && receipt.AttemptID == d.vaultAttemptID {
232				continue
233			}
234			lines = append(lines, "Other retained vault item/attempt:")
235			lines = append(lines, receipt.Lines()...)

docs/reference/compatibility.md:68:`dev mcp list` reads documented static files for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode. An absolute `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` relocates Claude user sources; local Claude rows retain their project key, and documented user/project/local/managed project approvals annotate declaration state. That narrow approval calculation is not a general runtime merge. The scanner does not start servers, execute helpers, contact endpoints, query health, or resolve credentials. Plugin caches, hosted connectors, remote organization configuration, inline `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, and command-line-only inputs are omitted. Keep the JSON `coverage` object, additive `local_project_path`, and scope-qualified duplicate rows when automating against this inventory.
docs/reference/compatibility.md:146:approval prompts, or parse the response into an action.
docs/reference/compatibility.md:216:Windows payloads remain disabled until ACL, reparse-point, held-root, and atomic
docs/reference/compatibility.md:222:`dev` compiles and runs on `windows/amd64` and `windows/arm64`, and every release ships a `.zip` for each. Core repository/task/worktree operations and the SSH host domain are native: static discovery, protected-DACL managed fragments, reparse-point rejection, native `ssh-keygen.exe`, Windows Job Object cancellation, and POSIX/Windows remote bootstrap are covered. Fleet can also target Windows OpenSSH through its encoded PowerShell launcher. What still differs:
docs/reference/compatibility.md:234:Public-key bootstrap requires an explicit key or explicit Ed25519 generation and installs public material only. Config-only and existing-auth setup do not install a key. Bootstrap supports bounded ProxyJump forms plus fixed POSIX and Windows OpenSSH installers; `ProxyCommand`, custom `AuthorizedKeysFile`, forced-shell policy, and ACL-incapable filesystems require manual remediation. Once a remote installer starts, cancellation/failure is `unknown` because the key may have been appended. Dev retains local config/generated keys and never attempts key revocation, private-key deletion/copying, `known_hosts` cleanup, or automatic credential rollback. Password saving is a separate explicitly selected credential flow. Ordinary setup preserves foreign directives; source-aware onboarding and the SSH dashboard use the reviewed workflows described below.
docs/reference/compatibility.md:439:actions, approval requirements, color meanings, CLI flags and JSON stay intact.

222	### Create a vault key, then select its agent identity
223	
224	`dev ssh key create` is a separate vault-creation workflow. It does not install an
225	SSH key remotely, rewrite SSH configuration, register fleet/Herdr, import an old
226	private key, or delete any source/vault item. Setup key pickers also offer vault
227	creation and return to the SSH form only after a key is explicitly selected.
228	Creating the vault item has its own review/approval; canceling the later SSH form
229	does **not** undo that completed creation.
230	
231	`--dry-run` validates and displays intent only: no provider CLI or agent is queried,
232	and account/vault/agent observations remain unknown. It is not a reusable guarded
233	provider plan. Actual creation obtains a fresh service-bound provider plan first.
234	Use an exact vault ID for 1Password. Interactive creation may review the current
235	native account; actual RPC creation with `--yes` or outside a terminal must specify
236	an exact `--account` ID. The title (default `SSH key`) is a label, never duplicate
237	detection or identity. There are no positional arguments.
238	
239	**1Password:** native `op` 2.20+ generates the default Ed25519 item in the selected
240	vault. Dev retains the exact returned item ID and checks its public key separately.
241	The item may exist before the desktop agent exposes it: unlock/sync the native app
242	and configure its agent vault selection yourself, then select the fingerprint.
243	Dev does not edit `agent.toml`, retry an ambiguous create, or silently substitute
244	another identity.
245	
246	**Bitwarden desktop handoff:** choose it in the picker or use `dev ssh key create
247	--provider bitwarden --desktop`. It cannot be combined with account/vault scopes,
248	experimental/native-context flags, or actual JSON execution. Even `--yes` still
249	requires interactive GUI-completion confirmation and explicit fingerprint selection
250	(`--dry-run --json` remains allowed). First obtain a complete public-key inventory from
251	one exact Bitwarden agent socket. Create a key using the native desktop UI, then
252	explicitly refresh and choose a newly **visible** fingerprint. This is not proof
253	that a new vault item was created: an existing key may have become visible. An
254	unavailable baseline is not an empty vault, and an agent restart/socket change
255	invalidates the comparison. Dev neither automates the GUI nor invents an item ID.
256	
257	**Bitwarden in-memory native-context mode (experimental):** CLI schema support is
258	pinned to `2026.3.0`. Two separate approvals are required:
259	
260	- `--experimental`: allow a new Ed25519 private key to exist briefly in dev's
261	  process memory and be supplied to the native CLI over stdin.
262	- `--native-context`: delegate endpoint/configuration authority to the reviewed
263	  native Bitwarden account/profile. This is **not endpoint attestation**.
264	
265	Generic `--yes` does not replace either approval. Review shows the observed user,
266	profile, CLI entrypoint/runtime and working directory. `BW_SESSION` comes only
267	from the native environment; never paste a session, master password or key into
268	agent/chat input. A session is a decryption credential, not an account/server ID.
269	The Plan retains only private comparison material, not an exported session value
270	or hash. Apply recaptures/revalidates the execution context, then runs all metadata,
271	creation and post-check commands with the same explicit frozen environment/cwd.
272	No global environment changes, login/unlock, provider configuration edits or native
273	vault-data parsing occur. Metadata/create commands use native no-interaction mode
274	so private JSON stdin cannot become a credential-prompt answer.
275	
276	The supported entrypoint/profile must be safely bound, including the documented
277	Node package/runtime form and portable-profile precedence where applicable.
278	Unsupported wrappers, runtime shims, unsafe/changed profiles or unsupported native
279	Windows attestation fail closed. This does not attest every dependency in the
280	native installation or make native configuration transactional. Bitwarden's base
281	`serverUrl` is only an advisory display value: cloud regions and independent API
282	settings cannot be inferred from it. Results therefore keep `endpoint=unverified`
283	and distinguish `native_context=observed_consistent` from creation status. The
284	endpoint-attested Bitwarden mode remains unsupported.
285	
286	Private key generation/encoding uses memory and stdin, never a plaintext key file,
287	clipboard or private-key argv. Owned buffers are wiped best-effort; that is not a
288	perfect RAM/swap/core-dump erasure guarantee, and native provider storage remains
289	its own responsibility. Public CLI/TUI results contain metadata, fingerprints and
290	item IDs—not private/session bytes or the complete public-key line.
291	
292	A created item with missing agent visibility remains **created**, with its receipt
293	and guidance. A lost response, malformed public result or changed post-check may
294	leave an item with uncertain readiness/context; retain the known item ID and inspect
295	before starting a fresh creation plan. A controller-local attempt ID distinguishes
296	two unknown attempts even when their account, vault and title are identical; it is
297	not an inferred provider item ID. Receipts live outside transient UI dialogs so late
298	results cannot cancel another action or disappear when a form is replaced.
299	Plans are single-attempt. Neither item creation nor public agent listing is an SSH authentication proof or password-save
300	authority. Only the subsequent normal SSH setup review/proof authorizes its own
301	configuration, bootstrap and optional registrations.
302	
303	Real Bitwarden type-5 and 1Password native integration checks are separate,
304	user-consented validation; fake runners do not replace them. No live vault item
305	creation or deletion is implicit in diagnostics, docs checks or test suites.
306	
307	### Choosing where a signing key lives
308	
309	| Backend | Key storage / interaction | Dev boundary |
310	|---|---|---|
311	| Bitwarden | Encrypted vault; unlocked agent/CLI can use decrypted material in memory | Named Unix agent; explicit desktop handoff or separately approved experimental native-context creation |
312	| 1Password | Encrypted vault; native approval/session and agent policy | Named Unix agent and explicit native vault creation; agent visibility remains a separate observation |
313	| YubiKey / FIDO2 | Authenticator-backed signing; protected local handle, optionally resident | Explicit interactive FIDO generation on supported controllers; no existing-private-key import or automatic credential removal |
314	| Secretive (macOS) | Secure Enclave-backed non-exportable key; native UI/approval | Select the existing Secretive agent; dev does not provision it |
315	| Apple CTK / Secure Enclave | Non-exportable P-256 CTK identity with a local SK handle | Existing native configuration/stubs only; automatic creation is blocked pending verified identity mapping |
316	| Apple Passwords / Keychain | Passwords is not a documented SSH agent; Keychain can store a key-file passphrase | Native passphrase integration is not a hardware-only or no-private-file solution |
317	| KeePassXC | Encrypted database plus its SSH-agent integration | Configure the native tool, then use an existing validated agent socket; not a non-exportability guarantee |
318	| ssh-tpm-agent (Linux-oriented) | TPM 2.0 key generation and local sealed `.tpm` files | Existing custom agent socket only; no TPM provisioning or migration by dev |
319	| gpg-agent / OpenPGP card | Software or card-backed key, depending on native configuration | Existing custom agent socket; no OpenPGP provisioning |
320	| YubiKey PIV | Separate generation/import and slot lifecycle | No slot writes/overwrites or PIV provisioning; use existing native authentication |
321	| Windows OpenSSH / Hello | Native support depends on the installed build and provider | Follow upstream native guidance; Windows Hello is not claimed as a dev key backend, and explicit dev agent/hardware creation gates remain closed pending native attestation |
322	
323	Vault keys are generally exportable by their native provider; “no private file
324	written by dev” is not the same as non-exportability. Agent memory, OS swap/crash
325	handling and native provider storage remain outside a perfect-erasure guarantee.
326	Never import an old key and automatically delete its local source as a substitute
327	for hardware generation. Unattended operation also depends on native PIN/touch and
328	agent approval policy, not just where the key is stored.
329	
330	References: [Bitwarden SSH agent](https://bitwarden.com/help/ssh-agent/),
331	[1Password SSH](https://www.1password.dev/ssh/agent/),
332	[KeePassXC agent integration](https://keepassxc.org/docs/KeePassXC_UserGuide#_ssh_agent_integration),
```

404	## Security boundary and deferred scope
405	
406	Implemented safety properties include source-bound plans, no-follow/reparse checks, private Unix modes or protected Windows DACLs, atomic/no-replace publication, concurrent-source revalidation, post-write plain-`ssh -G` verification for managed config, rollback only while the just-written local identity is still provably owned, process-group/Job-Object cancellation, and material-safe structured output.
407	
408	Deliberately deferred:
409	
410	- key rotation, expiry, revocation, or deletion from remote `authorized_keys`;
411	- deletion of local keys or `known_hosts` repair/removal;
412	- alias rename/adoption, managed wildcards/`Match`, arbitrary SSH directives, or an SSH config editor;
413	- automated `ProxyCommand`, certificates/CAs, forwarding, custom `AuthorizedKeysFile`, or forced-shell policy;
414	- password/vault storage, automatic password fallback, private-key copying, direct Bitwarden integration, or weakened host-key checks;
415	- cloud/chezmoi fleet import, mDNS, IPv6 range scanning, or background probing.
416	
417	When a server policy falls outside the verified POSIX/Windows installer contract, dev reports manual remediation rather than silently weakening it.

927	## SSH vault-key creation
928	
929	`ssh key create` takes no positional arguments. Flags are `--provider
930	1password|bitwarden`, `--title` (default `SSH key`), `--account`, `--vault`,
931	`--desktop`, `--dry-run`, `--yes` and `--json`, plus Bitwarden's `--experimental`
932	and `--native-context`. An interactive run may review the current account; actual
933	RPC creation with `--yes` or outside a terminal requires an exact `--account` ID.
934	1Password requires an exact vault ID; Bitwarden normalizes the personal vault and
935	needs BOTH approvals. Native-context delegates profile/configuration authority,
936	not endpoint attestation; `--yes` cannot substitute for either approval.
937	
938	`--desktop` requires `--provider bitwarden` and rejects account/vault/experimental/
939	native-context scopes. It always requires interactive GUI-completion confirmation
940	and explicit fingerprint selection, even with `--yes`. Actual desktop handoff
941	cannot use `--json`; intent-only `--dry-run --json` is allowed. The native GUI owns
942	the title and creation, so dev does not invent an item ID or creation receipt.
943	
944	Vault-create dry-run validates static intent only, executing no provider/agent and
945	leaving account/vault/agent observations unknown. Actual creation obtains a fresh
946	service-bound plan. Native-context metadata contains the reviewed profile/tool,
947	not session values or hashes; Bitwarden endpoints remain unverified even on success.
948	Public output preserves item IDs/fingerprints and created/unknown/context state,
949	not private material or full public-key lines. Created items are not rolled back
950	when agent visibility or later SSH setup fails. No auto-retry, import, native
951	configuration rewrite, or item deletion is implied. Desktop handoff uses a complete
952	same-socket public inventory and explicit newly-visible-key selection, not guessed
953	vault item IDs. JSON uses `schema_version: 1`, `kind: ssh_key_create`. Dry-run is
954	`status: intent_only` with `preview.intent_only: true`, not apply-ready. Pre-effect
955	statuses include `blocked`, `confirmation_required`, `canceled` and `not_started`;
956	RPC outcomes are `created` or `unknown`, and a created receipt may accompany a
957	nonzero partial/context error. Desktop states are `observed`, `no_new_visible_keys`
958	or `unavailable`. `result.agent_status` is `not_checked`, `not_selected`,
959	`unavailable`, `not_visible` or `offered`; offered means listing, not signing proof.
960	`result.receipt` carries public item/attempt metadata with no `public_line`.
961	A controller-local `attempt_id` distinguishes separately reviewed creation attempts,

    print('VAULT REVIEW\n' + value)
    assert 'a' * 26 in value and 'c' * 26 in value
    assert 'Synthetic SSH vault' in value
    new_calls = calls()[len(before_calls):]

    assert snapshot() == before
    run('send-keys', '-t', 'vault', 'Enter')
    value = wait('Vault action receipt')
    print('VAULT RECEIPT\n' + value)
    assert 'd' * 26 in value and 'created' in value and 'unavailable' in value
    assert 'SYNTHETIC_PRIVATE_VALUE_MUST_NOT_APPEAR' not in value
    assert 'ssh-ed25519 AAAA' not in value
    run('send-keys', '-t', 'vault', 'Enter')
    value = wait('Remote OS')
    assert 'vault attempt receipts retained independently' in value
    run('send-keys', '-t', 'vault', 'Escape')
    value = wait('SSH setup canceled')
    print('CANCELED SSH — RETAINED VAULT RECEIPT\n' + value)
    assert 'd' * 26 in value and 'created' in value
    new_calls = calls()[len(before_calls):]
    assert sum(call[:2] == ['item', 'create'] for call in new_calls) == 1, 'vault action was retried'
    assert snapshot() == before, 'vault flow or canceled SSH form changed SSH files'
finally:
    run('kill-session', '-t', 'vault')
print('Real TUI vault review/create/receipt/return/cancel passed with one fake item; SSH files unchanged.')

1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.
4	
5	The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and releases use [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
6	
7	## [Unreleased]
8	
9	### Added
10	
11	- Generated SSH keys can use a custom name and folder under `~/.ssh`: one missing
12	  folder directly under `~/.ssh` is created with mode `0700` and shown in the plan,
13	  and blocked paths name their reason. The terminal key picker and the dashboard's
14	  **+ Generate a new key** now ask for the key path and an optional comment.
15	- SSH keys held by Bitwarden, 1Password or Secretive agents (or a validated custom socket) can be
16	  listed with `dev ssh key list --agent` and selected in the setup key pickers or
17	  with `dev ssh setup --identity-agent`, so no private key file is needed. Dev
18	  publishes only the public key and writes a v2 managed alias with `IdentityAgent`;
19	  `dev doctor` warns when a provider is installed but no usable socket is found.
20	  dev v0.2.37 and older refuse setup/remove on v2 aliases. Explicit named/custom
21	  agent selection currently fails closed on native Windows and during remote
22	  fleet-source imports; normal registration to fleet/Herdr remains supported.
23	- Explicit interactive FIDO SSH key generation adds `ed25519-sk` / `ecdsa-sk`,
24	  provider, resident, verify-required and application options to CLI/dashboard
25	  setup. Native touch/PIN interaction retains selected-key and host-key guards;
26	  preview names the toolchain and uncertainty, and failures report retained or
27	  unknown hardware effects separately from local files. Known incompatible tools
28	  block without probing hardware. Automatic Secure Enclave creation, native
29	  Windows-controller hardware generation and new hardware generation during
30	  remote fleet-source imports remain unavailable.
31	- Explicit vault-key creation adds a standalone `dev ssh key create` workflow and
32	  setup-picker handoffs for 1Password, Bitwarden desktop and experimental
33	  Bitwarden in-memory/native-context creation. Bitwarden requires separate memory
34	  and native-profile approvals, freezes its actual execution context, and never
35	  claims endpoint attestation. Exact public receipts survive missing agent
36	  visibility or later SSH cancellation; creation and SSH authentication stay
37	  separate, with no automatic retry, key import or vault-item deletion.
38	
39	### Fixed
40	
41	- The dashboard FLEET view reloads its host list after SSH setup registers a
42	  fleet or Herdr host, instead of showing it only after restarting the CLI. A
43	  partial SSH setup now names the unfinished steps, such as `lab herdr: unknown`.
44	- SSH key-setup previews label inherited endpoint values as native configuration
45	  instead of displaying port `0`, and omit empty managed-directory headings.
46	- SSH agent inventory distinguishes a genuine empty response from an agent query
47	  failure. Provider command capture also bounds inherited-pipe cleanup after exit
48	  or cancellation instead of waiting indefinitely for descendants to close output.
49	
50	## [0.2.37] - 2026-09-14
51	
52	### Added
53	
54	- `dev ssh setup <alias>` on a terminal without `--key` or `--generate-key` opens
55	  one key picker listing local keys, `+ Generate a new key` and a manual path; the
56	  setup wizard, fleet imports and per-hop keys use the same picker. The `dev ssh`
57	  menu adds "Set up or install an SSH key for a host". Scripts still pass a flag.
58	- The dashboard SSH view's Ctrl+O offers "set up this discovered target…" with a
59	  form prefilled from the selected LAN/Tailscale observation, and "set up / install
60	  an SSH key…" for configured profiles without editing their connection settings.
61	  The setup form's Key field opens a key picker, and choice fields show every option.
62	
63	### Fixed
64	
65	- Interactive prompts with fixed answers list their choices, such as
66	  `Remote OS for lab (posix/windows) [posix]`, instead of revealing them only after
67	  an invalid answer. The discovery wizard's Target OS answer is now validated.
68	- LAN discovery no longer hides blocked connections behind `ready` with zero
69	  candidates. Reports add `probes` outcome counts and a `no_reachable_endpoints`
70	  warning, and `dev ssh discover`, the `dev ssh` wizard and the dashboard explain
71	  that macOS may be denying Local Network access to the terminal app. The wizard
72	  rescans instead of reusing an empty cached LAN scan. Status values and existing
73	  JSON fields are unchanged.

```text
1	# SSH vault key creation boundary
2	
3	This package is the domain adapter, not CLI/TUI integration or an SSH agent.
4	`Plan` explicitly reads native provider metadata; `Apply` consumes a service-bound,
5	immutable, single-attempt plan. The caller reviews the destination and confirms
6	creation before Apply. Deserialized plans carry no authority. `ValidateRequest`
7	is a syntax-only, zero-provider-execution check for static dry-run previews; it
8	never establishes native-context readiness or substitutes for Plan/Apply.
9	
10	## Provider modes
11	
12	- **1Password:** native `op item create --category ssh` generates the default
13	  Ed25519 identity. Account/user/server/exact vault ID and CLI version are bound
14	  and revalidated. The returned item ID, title, category and vault must match;
15	  public material is fetched by that exact ID with a public-field selector.
16	  Private response fields are ignored, not returned or logged. The selected
17	  public-field JSON shapes remain native-unverified and covered by fixtures only.
18	- **Bitwarden endpoint-attested mode remains unsupported.** Its native status and
19	  read-only `config server` expose only a base/display URL, while effective API
20	  and identity endpoints may be independently overridden. US/EU cloud both expose
21	  a null base. A non-null self-hosted-looking URL is not stronger endpoint proof.
22	  Missing native-context approval returns `ErrUnsupportedContext`; it never
23	  authorizes guessed endpoints, native storage parsing, or configuration changes.
24	- **Optional Bitwarden native-profile mode:** callers must separately set both
25	  `Experimental` and `NativeContextApproved`. This explicitly delegates endpoint
26	  and internal configuration authority to the reviewed native CLI profile. It is
27	  not endpoint attestation. A session key is a decryption credential, not a server
28	  or account ID. Even unchanged session/user observations cannot prove native
29	  internal endpoints or settings did not change. This residual delegation must
30	  be visible in the preview and approval, not hidden behind a generic key choice.
31	
32	## Frozen native execution
33	
34	Native-profile planning captures the complete environment and working directory,
35	including `BW_SESSION`, HOME/XDG paths, explicit app-data overrides and PATH. Only
36	private comparison hashes and filesystem identities remain in a plan; the
37	session-bearing environment is released afterwards. No session or comparison
38	hash belongs in public JSON, logs, error text or a persisted plan.
39	
40	Apply captures again, compares the reviewed context and revalidates before any
41	private generation. All metadata/create/postcheck calls use that same explicit
42	frozen child environment and cwd, never later ambient inheritance or `os.Setenv`
43	tricks. A custom runner without the frozen-execution contract fails closed.
44	Every Bitwarden command receives `--nointeraction` and a child-only
45	`BW_NOINTERACTION=true`; becoming locked cannot redirect key JSON into a native
46	master-password prompt. No login, unlock, config update or automatic retry occurs.
47	
48	Existing profiles must resolve to current-user-owned private directories with
49	existing private regular `data.json` metadata; no vault contents are read.
50	Resolution is component-by-component: every requested path, intermediate symlink
51	and target directory, final path, filesystem identity and ACL observation is
52	captured and rechecked. Unsafe intermediate components are not erased by `..`
53	normalization or hidden behind a protected outer link and safe final target.
54	Relative explicit profile paths are refused. The selected canonical app-data
55	directory is pinned in the child.
56	The pinned CLI's portable `bw-data` beside `process.execPath` takes precedence
57	over even an explicit override, so its presence/absence is separately bound.
58	For Node distributions this means beside the bound Node binary, not the script.
59	The default macOS and Linux HOME/XDG mappings follow the pinned native source.
60	
61	Darwin checks opened-inode extended security with `fgetattrlist`, using the
62	`getattrlist(2)` / SDK `sys/kauth.h` and `sys/acl.h` structures rather than parsing
63	`ls` or chmod text. Supported forms are absent/empty ACLs and well-formed deny-only
64	ACEs with non-null principal GUIDs, the DENY tag, optional INHERITED marker, and
65	only documented vnode rights from READ_DATA through TAKE_OWNERSHIP. ACL flags may
66	be zero or NO_INHERIT. The standard protective `everyone deny delete` home-style
67	ancestor ACL is therefore supported without exempting the ancestor from review.
68	Deny-only entries cannot grant access beyond the already-validated POSIX modes.
69	
70	Allow/grant, audit/alarm, deferred or inheritance-control flags, generic/Windows
71	rights, unknown tags/bits/layouts, malformed/truncated data and unexpected owner/
72	group fields remain unsupported. Linux performs bounded ACL/security-xattr
73	metadata checks and currently accepts ACL absence only. Unsupported queries and
74	security-policy attributes fail closed. Every resolution component and existing
75	`data.json` is checked without reading vault contents; the entire accepted Darwin
76	metadata is privately fingerprinted and revalidated, so even a changed accepted
77	deny-only ACL invalidates the reviewed context. There are no trusted-ancestor
78	exemptions and no runtime ACL repair/removal. Owned temporary fixtures cover the
79	protective form, additional grants, metadata-only changes and malformed buffers;
80	no actual user's home ACL was inspected. Native desktop creation plus agent
81	selection remains the alternative for unsupported permission policies—do not
82	strip home protections to satisfy the adapter.
83	
84	Supported execution surfaces are owned, protected native ELF/Mach-O entrypoints,
85	or the documented `#!/usr/bin/env node` entrypoint from an exact `@bitwarden/cli`
86	package. The latter binds the public package manifest/name/version/bin mapping,
87	installation directory, script, complete manifest-bin resolution path, and exact
88	native Node binary found through the frozen PATH/cwd. Common `build/bw.js` and
89	leading `./build/bw.js` bin forms are supported: only harmless leading `./` is
90	removed relative to the bound package directory, while the original manifest
91	value and actual path remain bound. Parent traversal, embedded dot cleanup,
92	absolute bin paths and ambiguous PATH forms are refused rather than silently
93	normalized. Clean absolute/relative PATH directories and an explicit current-
94	directory marker are resolved against the captured cwd. Execution uses the
95	bound Node binary with the pinned script prefix.
96	Arbitrary shell wrappers, unknown shebangs, unresolved runtime shims and extra
97	runtime-code loading through NODE_OPTIONS/NODE_PATH/preload variables fail closed.
98	The proof covers these named files/directories, resolution components, ownership,
99	modes and supported ACL observations; it does
100	not attest every dependency or the whole provider supply chain. Native Windows
101	profile execution is unavailable pending its identity/ACL contract.
102	
103	## Generation and outcomes
104	
105	Experimental Bitwarden generation creates Ed25519 only in process memory and
106	passes the pinned CLI `2026.3.0` type-5 schema through base64 stdin. It is limited
107	to the personal-vault schema with a unique operation marker. No existing key is
108	imported or deleted, and dev does not write private-key files. Owned buffers receive
109	best-effort cleanup, not a promise about Go runtime copies, dumps or OS swap.
110	
111	Creation, native-context consistency, endpoints and SSH agent readiness are
112	separate facts:
113	
114	- `status: created` means a matching creation receipt was verified.
115	- Bitwarden `native_context_status: observed_consistent` means the frozen context,
116	  tool/profile identities and native account observations remained consistent.
117	- Bitwarden always reports `endpoint_status: unverified` and keeps the legacy
118	  `binding_status: unknown`; it never turns native delegation into endpoint proof.
119	- None of these results proves that a provider agent lists or can sign with the key.
120	
121	`CanSelectAgentKey(plan, result)` centralizes the provider-specific eligibility
122	matrix for matching a receipt to fresh agent inventory. It requires the unchanged,
123	source-bound result of successful Apply, including matching canonical public key
124	and fingerprint; fabricated, serialized or modified receipts cannot authorize it.
125	It performs no agent lookup and never substitutes for signer/authentication proof.
126	
127	A wrong public-field type or failed lookup keeps the exact created item ID and
128	returns `ErrPublicKey`. An unexpected sharing scope, failed/changed postcheck or
129	other uncertainty retains any verified receipt with unknown context. A lost or
130	unverifiable creation response remains `status: unknown`; an item ID is never
131	invented. No creation is automatically retried, including interrupted operations.
132	There is no rollback, delete, import, login/unlock, agent-configuration or key-
133	revocation API. `Receipt.Destination` is reviewed intent; pre/post checks cannot
134	make native tools and remote services transactional.
135	
136	The shared `sshcredential.NativeRunner` caps output, discards stderr, applies a
137	15-second command timeout and a two-second `WaitDelay` for inherited-pipe cleanup.
138	Failures remain sanitized. It does not terminate whole process groups; bounded
139	wait is not proof that every descendant exited.
140	
141	## Validation status
142	
143	No real vault/key creation or installed provider execution has been performed for
144	this implementation. Native-context tests use copies of their own harmless Go
145	test executable, inert Node entrypoints and synthetic profiles; they verify

Dev will not compete with its existing definition. New dev-managed aliases use a portable lowercase exact-name grammar and one deterministic file containing `HostName`, optional `User`, `Port`, `ProxyJump`, `IdentityFile`, and `IdentitiesOnly`. A file that also needs `IdentityAgent` or `SecurityKeyProvider` uses the `v2` header instead; dev v0.2.37 and older treat a v2 file as not dev-owned and refuse setup/remove on it, so upgrade every dev that shares `~/.ssh` before selecting agent keys. Arbitrary directives and wildcard/`Match` blocks are not managed.

243	- `--native-context`：將 endpoint／設定 authority 委由審閱過的原生 Bitwarden account／

246	一般 `--yes` 不能代替其中任何一項。審閱會列出觀測到的 user、profile、CLI entrypoint／
247	runtime 與工作目錄。`BW_SESSION` 只來自原生 environment；不要把 session、master password

250	然後 metadata、create、post-check 都使用同一份明確固定的 environment／cwd。

252	Metadata／create 強制原生 no-interaction，避免把 private JSON stdin 當成 credential prompt

280	
281	| Backend | Key 儲存／互動 | Dev 的支援邊界 |
282	|---|---|---|
283	| Bitwarden | 加密 vault；解鎖後 agent／CLI 可在記憶體使用解密資料 | Named Unix agent；明確 desktop handoff，或另行同意的 experimental native-context creation |
284	| 1Password | 加密 vault；原生 approval／session 與 agent policy | Named Unix agent 與明確的原生 vault creation；agent 是否可見仍是另外的觀測 |
285	| YubiKey／FIDO2 | Authenticator 簽章；本機保護 handle，可選 resident | 受支援 controller 的明確互動 FIDO generation；不匯入舊私鑰，也不自動移除 credential |
286	| Secretive（macOS） | Secure Enclave non-exportable key；原生 UI／approval | 選取既有 Secretive agent；dev 不替它 provisioning |
287	| Apple CTK／Secure Enclave | Non-exportable P-256 CTK identity 與本機 SK handle | 使用已配置的原生 stub；自動建立須先驗證 identity mapping，目前停用 |
288	| Apple Passwords／Keychain | Passwords 沒有文件化 SSH agent；Keychain 可存 key-file passphrase | 原生 passphrase 整合不等於 hardware-only，也不會消除 private-key file |
289	| KeePassXC | 加密資料庫與 SSH-agent integration | 先設定原生工具，再選取已驗證 socket；不代表私鑰不可匯出 |
290	| ssh-tpm-agent（Linux-oriented） | TPM 2.0 key generation 與本機 sealed `.tpm` files | 只整合既有 custom agent socket；dev 不做 TPM provisioning／migration |
291	| gpg-agent／OpenPGP card | 依原生設定使用軟體或卡片 key | 既有 custom agent socket；不做 OpenPGP provisioning |
292	| YubiKey PIV | 獨立的 generation／import 與 slot lifecycle | 不寫入／覆蓋 slot、不做 PIV provisioning；使用既有原生認證 |
293	| Windows OpenSSH／Hello | 依已安裝 build／provider 決定原生支援 | 遵循 upstream 原生指引；不宣稱 Windows Hello 是 dev backend，明確 agent／hardware creation 仍須 native attestation 才能開放 |
294	
295	Vault key 通常仍可由原生 provider 匯出；「dev 不寫 private file」不等於不可匯出。
296	Agent 記憶體、OS swap／crash 處理與原生 provider 儲存，也不在完美抹除保證內。
297	不要把匯入舊 key 後自動刪除本機來源，當成硬體產生的替代方案；能否無人值守運作，
298	還取決於 PIN／touch 與 agent approval policy，而不只是 key 放在哪裡。

551	
552	Named Bitwarden/1Password/Secretive or custom agents use validated Unix sockets,

574	closed without permission repair or native configuration changes. Created items

576	private-key import/source deletion or hardware/vault revocation is introduced.
