1	# SSH key provider helpers
2	
3	Status: partially implemented in the unreleased v0.2.38 work; existing-key migration, endpoint-attested Bitwarden writes and automatic Secure Enclave provisioning remain separate/unresolved. Do not mark the milestone shipped before its verification and release gates close.
4	
5	Research updated: 2026-09-14.
6	
7	## Remaining safe-automation gates
8	
9	The approved key-provider increment covers custom local destinations, named SSH
10	agents, explicit FIDO generation and separately approved vault creation. It does
11	not authorize importing existing private keys, deleting vault items or credentials,
12	changing provider configuration, or executing live hardware/vault tests implicitly.
13	
14	- **Secure Enclave identity binding:** native `sc_auth create-ctk-identity` is
15	  documented, but there is no verified machine-readable creation receipt or stable
16	  listing contract. `list-ctk-identities -t ssh` changes the hash format; it is not
17	  an SSH-only filter. Human tables contain blank fields, arbitrary labels and
18	  localized dates. An original public example confirms one SHA-1 EC-point /
19	  SHA-256 SK-wire fingerprint mapping, not a general parser guarantee. Establish
20	  an exact identity reader before creation; unknown/ambiguous input must fail
21	  before any hardware effect. Never select the last row or rely on label uniqueness.
22	  `ssh-keygen -K` writes resident handle files and is never a passive capability
23	  probe. Any future import must filter one verified identity using child-scoped
24	  `KEYCHAIN_CERTIFICATES`, use private staging, and retain/report uncertain effects.
25	- **Bitwarden endpoint-attested mode:** pinned CLI 2026.3.0 reports only a base
26	  `serverUrl`, null for both US/EU cloud accounts. A non-null base may coexist with
27	  independent API/identity overrides; read-only `config server` does not prove the
28	  effective endpoints. Do not label the base URL as a verified destination or
29	  mutate configuration to discover it. An explicitly approved native-context mode
30	  is a different authority: it delegates endpoint configuration to a reviewed
31	  native profile and keeps endpoint status unverified. It must separately approve
32	  transient memory generation and native-context delegation, freeze the actual
33	  command environment, bind/revalidate user/session/profile/tool context, use
34	  no-interaction commands, and retain exact item receipts on uncertainty. A
35	  `BW_SESSION` hash is comparison material, not an account/server identifier.
36	  Internal native configuration is not made transactional by pre/post checks.
37	- **Native Windows:** explicit provider pipes, hardware tools and vault profiles
38	  need verified identity/ACL/reparse-point contracts. Cross-compilation is not a
39	  substitute for dedicated native gates. Existing native OpenSSH authentication
40	  remains a separate supported boundary.
41	- **Fleet-source imports:** controller-selected agents/hardware provider settings
42	  must become part of immutable shared-hop authority before those generation paths
43	  can be enabled. Never copy remote provider paths or append new authentication
44	  intent after an import plan was reviewed. Registration *to* fleet is distinct
45	  from importing connection profiles *from* fleet.
46	
47	Sources: [original CTK example](https://gist.github.com/arianvp/5f59f1783e3eaf1a2d4cd8e952bb4acf),
48	[`sc_auth` manual](https://keith.github.io/xcode-man-pages/sc_auth.8.html),
49	[`ssh-keychain` manual](https://keith.github.io/xcode-man-pages/ssh-keychain.8.html),
50	[pinned Bitwarden status](https://github.com/bitwarden/clients/blob/c20753e4dae029d6155565682dc79718f9aeb426/apps/cli/src/commands/status.command.ts),
51	[pinned endpoint resolution](https://github.com/bitwarden/clients/blob/c20753e4dae029d6155565682dc79718f9aeb426/libs/common/src/platform/services/default-environment.service.ts).
52	No live keychain enumeration, hardware enrollment or vault item creation was used
53	for this research.
54	
55	## Existing migration research
56	
57	The existing chezmoi `ssh-to-bitwarden` helper already imports SSH key items and
58	its shell configuration selects Bitwarden's agent. Reuse a native handoff before
59	building another vault writer. A future implementation must show key fingerprints
60	and provider state without logging key bytes, vault unlock data or credentials.
61	Audit the existing helper's name-based duplicate detection and Secure Note fallback
62	before treating it as a dev-supported credential transfer protocol.
63	
64	YubiKey is a separate design: FIDO2-generated hardware credentials, PIV imports
65	and OpenPGP agent integration have different lifecycle and recovery semantics.
66	Do not present them as equivalent destinations for uploading an existing key.
67	Public key installation can reuse sshhost once a provider exposes a supported
68	public identity and ordinary OpenSSH authentication works.
69	
70	Suggested first increment: agent/socket diagnostics, public fingerprint listing,
71	provider-specific prerequisites and an explicit native-tool handoff. Vault import,
72	hardware provisioning and credential revocation need their own reviewable plans.
73	No new provider execution belongs in passive SSH or fleet inventory.
74	
75	Sources: [Bitwarden SSH agent](https://bitwarden.com/help/ssh-agent/),
76	[Yubico SSH approaches](https://developers.yubico.com/SSH/).
77	
78	Herdr integration also has an upstream opportunity: metadata-only registration
79	and structured dry-run/apply outcomes would avoid native preparation during add.
80	The implemented adapter uses the current native CLI; it does not edit Herdr's
81	private endpoint catalog or silently answer server-replacement approvals.
82	
83	
84	## Distinct future workflows
85	
86	The user requested these as later helpers, not additions to the current SSH
87	password-save feature. Default to explicit native-tool handoff and metadata
88	preview. An approved transfer may process private material in memory, but normal
89	setup/discovery must retain its no-private-key-transfer contract. Keep names,
90	public fingerprints, destination identity and verification results reviewable;
91	never log key bytes, passphrases, vault sessions or exported account passwords.
92	
93	### Existing SSH private key to Bitwarden
94	
95	Bitwarden accepts OpenSSH and PKCS#8 private-key import; its documented agent
96	supports Ed25519 and RSA SHA-256/SHA-512, and PuTTY input is unsupported. The SDK
97	can decrypt supported encrypted input with an explicit passphrase and normalize
98	it to OpenSSH; vault representation is encrypted. A future helper must detect
99	format/algorithm support rather than promise arbitrary PEM conversion.
100	
101	The CLI documents SSH item type 5, but its current template switch has no SSH-key
102	case. Do not assume `bw get template item.sshkey` exists, or fall back silently to
103	Secure Note after template failure. Audit the existing chezmoi helper, pin the
104	supported CLI schema, use stdin rather than secret argv/clipboard where possible,
105	and retain the exact returned item ID and public fingerprint. Duplicate names
106	are not identity. Verify provider agent signing before offering separate local
107	key-file cleanup; import never implies source deletion or remote revocation.
108	
109	Sources: [Bitwarden About SSH](https://bitwarden.com/help/about-ssh/),
110	[SDK import](https://sdk-api-docs.bitwarden.com/bitwarden_wasm_internal/ssh/fn.import_ssh_key.html),
111	[CLI schema](https://bitwarden.com/help/cli/),
112	[CLI template source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitwarden/clients/main/apps/cli/src/commands/get.command.ts).
113	
114	### YubiKey: generate versus import
115	
116	FIDO2 SSH creates a new `ed25519-sk` or `ecdsa-sk` credential and a local handle;
117	it is not a route for uploading the same ordinary OpenSSH private key. PIV can
118	import supported asymmetric private keys into selected slots, while OpenPGP uses
119	its own existing-PGP-key import flow. Supported algorithms depend on firmware
120	and application. Occupied PIV slots can irrecoverably replace an existing key,
121	so device/firmware/slot inventory, explicit replacement scope and recovery need
122	their own reviewed plan. Do not label all three paths “move this SSH key”.
123	
124	Sources: [Yubico FIDO2 SSH](https://developers.yubico.com/SSH/Securing_SSH_with_FIDO2.html),
125	[PIV compatibility](https://docs.yubico.com/hardware/yubikey/yk-tech-manual/yk5-apps-piv.html),
126	[PIV import/replacement](https://docs.yubico.com/yesdk/users-manual/application-piv/commands.html),
127	[OpenPGP import](https://developers.yubico.com/PGP/Importing_keys.html).
128	
129	### Apple Passwords to Bitwarden
130	
131	On Mac, use Passwords' native selected/all-password CSV export and Bitwarden's
132	Safari/macOS importer. CSV is unencrypted and has export exclusions (including
133	Wi-Fi, some shared-group credentials and Sign in with Apple); it is not an SSH-key
134	or passkey archive. Bitwarden imports do not deduplicate repeated imports.
135	A helper should show selected scope, record completion/uncertainty and guide
136	explicit cleanup of the export artifact, without claiming secure erasure.
137	
138	Bitwarden separately documents app-to-app Credential Exchange from Apple
139	Passwords on iOS 26+, including passwords and passkeys. This research did not
140	establish macOS CXP support: detect native capability at implementation time,
141	otherwise describe the supported CSV route. Never substitute a Keychain dump or
142	scripted vault read for the user's native export authorization. Website passkeys,
143	account passwords and SSH private keys are different data types and migration
144	contracts.
145	
146	Sources: [Apple Mac export](https://support.apple.com/guide/passwords/export-passwords-to-a-file-mchl35b12625/mac),
147	[Bitwarden macOS migration](https://bitwarden.com/help/import-from-safari/),
148	[Credential Exchange import](https://bitwarden.com/help/import-data/).

315	
316	A private/security-key identity passed to `--key` must have a validated
317	`.pub` companion; dev may derive a missing public companion with confirmed
318	`ssh-keygen -y`. Bootstrap transfers only public material; passive catalog/doctor
319	checks do not read private-key contents. Explicit generation separately validates
320	its newly staged files before publication.
321	
322	Inspect available identities before choosing one:
323	
324	```bash
325	dev ssh key list                    # local public-key metadata plus the current agent
326	dev ssh key list --no-agent --json  # file metadata only; no OpenSSH evaluation
327	dev ssh key list --alias lab        # explicitly evaluate lab's identity/agent settings
328	dev ssh key list --agent bitwarden  # explicitly query a validated named agent
329	dev ssh key doctor                 # metadata-only permission report; no agents or ssh
330	dev ssh key doctor --fix            # preview exact repairs, then confirm
331	dev ssh key doctor --key ~/.ssh/custom-key --fix --yes --json
332	```
333	
334	Bitwarden, 1Password, Secretive and validated custom agents can keep the signing key
335	out of local private-key files. Select them in a key picker or use
336	`ssh setup --identity-agent <provider-or-socket> --key <fingerprint-or-.pub>`.
337	Dev publishes only a public selector and writes managed v2 `IdentityAgent` /
338	`IdentityFile` / `IdentitiesOnly` settings; already-matching foreign aliases are
339	preserved. Both terminal and dashboard retain the exact selected fingerprint/socket.
340	Provider-location discovery and doctor are stat-only, while explicit key listing
341	queries the agent. Native Windows named-agent selection and fleet-source imports
342	remain guarded/unavailable; ordinary registration **to** fleet/Herdr is supported.
343	Binaries v0.2.37 and older refuse management of v2 fragments.
344	
345	`dev ssh key create` creates a new vault key separately from SSH installation.
346	Choose 1Password with an exact vault ID, or experimental Bitwarden memory generation
347	with both `--experimental` and `--native-context`. Bitwarden's reviewed native
348	profile/account and execution environment are bound, but API endpoints remain
349	explicitly unverified; a base URL or session is not endpoint identity. `--dry-run`
350	is intent-only and executes no provider. Actual RPC creation with --yes or outside
351	a terminal requires an exact --account ID. Creation has its own review, and public
352	item receipts survive missing agent visibility or later SSH-form cancellation.
353	The picker and `ssh key create --provider bitwarden --desktop` also offer native
354	desktop handoff, requiring interactive completion/fingerprint selection and observing
355	newly visible keys rather than claiming a new item was created. No private-key file,
356	implicit import, source deletion or automatic mutation retry is introduced.
357	See [vault key creation and backend choices](docs/guides/ssh-hosts.md#create-a-vault-key-then-select-its-agent-identity).
358	
359	The setup wizard offers a key picker with paths, comments, fingerprints and signer
360	availability, plus **+ Generate a new key** and manual path entry. `dev ssh` also
361	has a **Set up or install an SSH key for a host** menu entry. It checks basic SSH directory/configuration
362	permissions early and offers separately confirmed, narrowly scoped tightening.
363	Completed permission repairs remain if setup is canceled later; aliases, registry
364	bindings, local key generation and remote actions still wait for the main SSH
365	preview. Vault creation is a distinct approved stage and is retained if that later
366	SSH preview is canceled.
367	
368	`key doctor` scans public-key companions and exact standard private-key names
369	under `~/.ssh`, without reading private contents. Repeat `--key` to restrict it to
370	selected paths plus canonical SSH setup paths, including a custom private key
371	without a `.pub`. A normal report never writes; `--fix` applies one reviewed plan
372	and verifies the result. Blocked or incomplete scans authorize no repairs. Setup
373	continues to check only its baseline paths and chosen key, not every unselected key.
374	
375	Use selected fleet machines as SSH profile sources, or run their native SSH:
376	
377	```bash
378	dev ssh discover --source fleet --host gateway --refresh
379	dev ssh list --fleet                         # cached profiles; no remote refresh
```

import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import subprocess
import sys

repo = Path('/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/dev-cli')
root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
record = json.loads((root / 'artifact-prefix-before-p4.json').read_text())


def lines(data):
    parts = data.split(b'\n')
    return [p + b'\n' for p in parts[:-1]] + ([parts[-1]] if parts[-1] else [])


for name, expected in record.items():
    current = (repo / name).read_bytes().replace(b'\r\n', b'\n')
    assert hashlib.sha256(current[:expected['length']]).hexdigest() == expected['sha256'], 'original artifact prefix changed: ' + name
print('All three original normalized artifact prefixes retained.')
for patch_path in sys.argv[1:]:
    patch = Path(patch_path).read_bytes().replace(b'\r\n', b'\n')
    verified = 0
    for part in patch.split(b'diff --git ')[1:]:
        plines = lines(part)
        name = next((line[6:].strip().decode() for line in plines if line.startswith(b'+++ b/')), None)
        if name not in record:
            continue
        old = lines(subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', 'HEAD:' + name], cwd=repo).replace(b'\r\n', b'\n'))
        rebuilt, cursor, active = [], 0, False
        for line in plines:
            match = re.match(rb'^@@ -(\d+)(?:,\d+)? \+\d+(?:,\d+)? @@', line)
            if match:
                start = max(0, int(match.group(1)) - 1)
                rebuilt.extend(old[cursor:start])
                cursor, active = start, True
            elif active:
                if line.startswith((b' ', b'-')):
                    assert cursor < len(old) and old[cursor] == line[1:], 'backup context mismatch: ' + name
                    if line.startswith(b' '):
                        rebuilt.append(line[1:])
                    cursor += 1
                elif line.startswith(b'+'):
                    rebuilt.append(line[1:])
                elif line.startswith(b'\\ No newline'):
                    raise AssertionError('unexpected non-newline backup; retain for manual verification')
        rebuilt.extend(old[cursor:])
        expected = b''.join(rebuilt)
        current = (repo / name).read_bytes().replace(b'\r\n', b'\n')
        assert current.startswith(expected), 'stashed artifact content not fully retained: ' + name
        verified += 1
    assert verified == 2, 'expected both tracked artifact backups'
    print(Path(patch_path).name + ': both full stashed artifact prefixes retained.')
changed = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'diff', '--name-only', '-z'], cwd=repo).decode().split('\0')
assert all(not p or p in record for p in changed), 'unexpected product changes after hook'
print('Product worktree matches index; no artifact contents printed.')

100	### Scoop (Windows)
101

105	```
106	
107	The manifest for each release is also attached to the GitHub release as

109	
110	### Go or source
111	
112	```bash
113	go install github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/cmd/dev@latest
114	# Pin @v0.2.37 instead when you need a reproducible install.
115	# Or from a checkout: make install  # also installs the bundled agent skill
116	```
117	
118	Source checkouts include `mise.toml`, pinning the repository toolchain to Go
119	1.26.4. With mise installed, `mise install` selects the same compiler used by
120	the module and CI instead of relying on a possibly mismatched global GOROOT.
121	
122	Every release also publishes `darwin/arm64`, `darwin/amd64`, `linux/amd64`,
123	`linux/arm64` (`.tar.gz`) and `windows/amd64`, `windows/arm64` (`.zip`) archives
124	with a `SHA256SUMS` file, so a binary can be verified without a Go toolchain.
125	
126	To find out whether the binary you have is current, and to update it:
127	
128	```bash
129	dev version           # what this build is, and whether it is a published release
130	dev version --check    # also ask GitHub for the newest release (cached for a day)
131	dev doctor            # reports the running version, install owner/path, and PATH collisions
132	dev upgrade --check    # report whether a newer release exists
133	dev upgrade            # delegate to its owner, or verify and replace a standalone binary
134	```
135	
136	For a standalone install, `dev upgrade` checks the release's actual asset list.
137	If this platform has an archive, it downloads and verifies `SHA256SUMS`. If the
138	platform is absent (including Android/Termux today), it offers to build the exact
139	release tag with native Go. New releases include a compact
140	`dev-cli_<tag>_source.tar.gz`, verified against `SHA256SUMS` and excluding
141	conversation history. Older releases without this asset use Go's configured
142	module verification and may download a much larger archive. Both paths use
143	two build workers and the installed toolchain; they may take several minutes
144	on the first run. The candidate must build and report the expected version before
145	replacing the old executable. Download or checksum failures stop the upgrade.
146	
147	On Termux, prepare the native tools with `pkg install golang clang git`.
148	Android builds use `GOOS=android`, CGO and Clang; Linux archives are not Android
149	substitutes. Go must satisfy that release's `go.mod`; automatic toolchain downloads
150	are disabled for source upgrades. To recover an older `dev` whose upgrade command
151	only attempts the missing Android archive, build the published version separately:
152	
153	```bash
154	pkg update && pkg upgrade -y && pkg install golang clang git curl
155	stage="$(mktemp -d "$HOME/.local/bin/.dev-build.XXXXXX")" && (
156	  trap 'rm -rf "$stage"' EXIT
157	  set -e
158	  version=v0.2.37
159	  asset="dev-cli_${version}_source.tar.gz"
160	  base="https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/releases/download/$version"
161	  cd "$stage"
162	  curl -fL "$base/$asset" -o "$asset"
163	  curl -fL "$base/SHA256SUMS" -o SHA256SUMS
164	  awk -v asset="$asset" '$2 == asset { print }' SHA256SUMS > source.sha256
165	  test -s source.sha256
166	  sha256sum -c source.sha256
167	  mkdir source
168	  tar -xzf "$asset" -C source
169	  cd source
170	  GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOWORK=off GOFLAGS= GOOS=android GOARCH=arm64 \

228	## Key-provider authority and validation boundaries (2026-09-15)
229	
230	Custom destinations, named agents/v2 fragments and FIDO generation are defined by
231	`internal/sshhost`, the CLI/TUI SSH adapters and their source-bound fixtures.
232	Filesystem replacement, permission hardening, partial publication, independent
233	native login gates and same-socket inventory refresh have dedicated regressions.
234	The vault boundary is `internal/sshvault` plus the frozen-environment provider
235	runner in `internal/sshcredential`; schema/version gates, dual Bitwarden approval,
236	profile/tool binding, single-attempt writes and retained public receipts are distinct
237	from agent visibility and SSH proof. Interface claims must follow the code and
238	final test results, not merely an approved design or a passing cross-build.
239	
240	Vendor references include Bitwarden CLI `2026.3.0` source, 1Password SSH-key CLI
241	creation docs, Yubico FIDO2 guidance, native Apple sc_auth/ssh-keychain manuals,
242	and the original public CTK example linked in the SSH guide/backlog. The CTK example
243	is a fixture, not a general mapping contract; automatic provisioning remains blocked.
244	Bitwarden base URLs/session values never attest effective endpoints. The explicit
245	native-context mode delegates configuration authority and retains endpoint-unverified
246	status; it is not a transactional native-config snapshot or supply-chain attestation.
247	Real vault-item creation/deletion, YubiKey/Touch ID interaction and native Windows
248	attestation need separate evidence/consent; automated fakes do not supply it.
249

28	      - name: Validate stable release tag

36	        run: |
37	          make build
38	          test "$(./dev --version)" = "dev version $VERSION"

40	      - name: Verify exported source package
41	        run: python3 scripts/check-source-archive.py --version "$VERSION"

43	      # modernc.org/sqlite is pure Go, so every target cross-compiles from one
44	      # runner with CGO disabled and ships as a static binary. Windows ships a
45	      # .zip with dev.exe; every other platform a .tar.gz with dev.
46	      - name: Build release archives
47	        run: |
48	          mkdir -p dist
49	          ldflags="-s -w -X github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/cli.Version=$VERSION"
50	          for target in darwin/arm64 darwin/amd64 linux/amd64 linux/arm64 windows/amd64 windows/arm64; do
51	            os="${target%/*}"; arch="${target#*/}"
52	            bin=dev; [ "$os" = windows ] && bin=dev.exe
53	            CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS="$os" GOARCH="$arch" \
54	              go build -ldflags "$ldflags" -o "dist/$bin" ./cmd/dev
55	            if [ "$os" = windows ]; then
56	              ( cd dist && zip -q "dev-cli_${VERSION}_${os}_${arch}.zip" "$bin" )
57	            else
58	              tar -czf "dist/dev-cli_${VERSION}_${os}_${arch}.tar.gz" -C dist "$bin"
59	            fi
60	            rm "dist/$bin"
61	          done
62	          # git archive honors export-ignore, keeping conversation history out
63	          # of the source package used for native upgrades (e.g. Termux).
64	          git archive --format=tar.gz --output="dist/dev-cli_${VERSION}_source.tar.gz" "$GITHUB_SHA"
65	          ( cd dist && sha256sum -- *.tar.gz *.zip > SHA256SUMS )
66	          ls -l dist
67	
68	      # The changelog is the account a human wrote; generated notes are the
69	      # fallback for a tag whose section is missing.
70	      - name: Extract release notes
71	        run: |
72	          awk -v ver="${VERSION#v}" '
73	            $0 ~ "^## \\[" ver "\\]" { found = 1; next }
74	            found && /^## \[/ { exit }
75	            found { print }
76	          ' CHANGELOG.md > notes.md
77	          if [ ! -s notes.md ]; then
78	            echo "no CHANGELOG section for $VERSION; falling back to generated notes"

92	          else

94	          fi

1	# Keep every text file LF on checkout, on every platform. Without this the
2	# Windows CI runner (core.autocrlf=true in the image) checks out CRLF, and both

13	
14	func nativeSameChangeTime(a, b fs.FileInfo) bool {
15		left, lok := a.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t)
16		right, rok := b.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t)
17		return lok && rok && left.Ctim == right.Ctim
18	}
19	
20	func captureNativeACL(path string, expected fs.FileInfo) (nativeACLObservation, error) {
21		var file *os.File
22		list := func(buffer []byte) (int, error) { return unix.Llistxattr(path, buffer) }
23		if expected.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink == 0 {
24			fd, err := unix.Open(path, unix.O_RDONLY|unix.O_CLOEXEC|unix.O_NONBLOCK|unix.O_NOFOLLOW, 0)
25			if err != nil {
26				return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrNativeContext
27			}
28			file = os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), path)
29			defer file.Close()
30			opened, err := file.Stat()
31			if err != nil || !nativePermissionIdentity(expected, opened) {
32				return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrStale
33			}
34			list = func(buffer []byte) (int, error) { return unix.Flistxattr(fd, buffer) }
35		}
36		// Like SSH's bounded metadata policy, reject access/default/NFS ACLs and
37		// other system/security policy attributes. Never read private file contents.
38		// Unsupported metadata queries are unknown, not an empty ACL observation.
39		size, err := list(nil)
40		if err != nil || size < 0 || size > 64<<10 {
41			return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrNativeContext
42		}
43		names := make([]byte, size)
44		if size > 0 {
45			n, err := list(names)
46			if err != nil || n < 0 || n > len(names) {
47				return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrNativeContext
48			}
49			names = names[:n]
50		}
51		for _, name := range strings.Split(string(names), "\x00") {
52			if strings.HasPrefix(name, "system.") || strings.HasPrefix(name, "security.") {
53				return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrNativeContext
54			}
55		}
56		current, err := os.Lstat(path)
57		if err != nil || !nativePermissionIdentity(expected, current) {
58			return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrStale
59		}
60		if file != nil {
61			after, err := file.Stat()
62			if err != nil || !nativePermissionIdentity(expected, after) {
63				return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrStale
64			}
65		}
66		return nativeACLObservation{safe: true}, nil
67	}

11	func nativeOwned(info fs.FileInfo, private bool) bool {
12		stat, ok := info.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t)
13		if !ok || info.Mode()&(os.ModeSetuid|os.ModeSetgid) != 0 {
14			return false
15		}
16		if private {
17			return int(stat.Uid) == os.Geteuid() && info.Mode().Perm()&0o077 == 0 && (info.IsDir() || stat.Nlink == 1)
18		}
19		if int(stat.Uid) != os.Geteuid() && stat.Uid != 0 {
20			return false
21		}
22		return info.Mode().Perm()&0o022 == 0 || info.IsDir() && stat.Uid == 0 && info.Mode()&os.ModeSticky != 0
23	}
24	
25	func nativeSameOwner(a, b fs.FileInfo) bool {
26		left, lok := a.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t)
27		right, rok := b.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t)
28		return lok && rok && left.Uid == right.Uid && left.Gid == right.Gid
29	}
30	
31	func nativeLinkOwned(info fs.FileInfo) bool {
32		stat, ok := info.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t)
33		return ok && (int(stat.Uid) == os.Geteuid() || stat.Uid == 0)
34	}

package sshhost

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"reflect"
	"testing"
)

// Agent-protocol parsing remains portable even where explicit socket/pipe
// attestation is unavailable. These fixtures never execute ssh-add or attest a
// synthetic Unix socket on Windows.
func TestAgentReaderDistinguishesKnownEmptyFromFailure(t *testing.T) {
	for _, test := range []struct {
		name string
		result RunResult
		runErr error
		complete bool
	}{
		{"success-empty", RunResult{}, nil, true},
		{"native-empty", RunResult{ExitCode:1, Stdout:[]byte("The agent has no identities.\n")}, nil, true},
		{"generic-exit-one", RunResult{ExitCode:1}, nil, false},
		{"fetch-failed", RunResult{ExitCode:1, Stderr:[]byte("error fetching identities")}, nil, false},
		{"empty-plus-error", RunResult{ExitCode:1, Stdout:[]byte("The agent has no identities.\n"), Stderr:[]byte("error")}, nil, false},
		{"stderr-only-empty", RunResult{ExitCode:1, Stderr:[]byte("The agent has no identities.\n")}, nil, false},
		{"unavailable", RunResult{ExitCode:2}, nil, false},
		{"truncated-empty", RunResult{ExitCode:1, Stdout:[]byte("The agent has no identities.\n"), StdoutTruncated:true}, nil, false},
		{"truncated-stderr", RunResult{StderrTruncated:true}, nil, false},
		{"invalid-record", RunResult{Stdout:[]byte("invalid public record")}, nil, false},
		{"launch-failed", RunResult{}, errors.New("native launch failed"), false},
	} {
		t.Run(test.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			calls:=0
			s:=&Service{runner:keyCatalogRunnerFunc(func(_ context.Context, request RunRequest) (RunResult,error) {
				calls++
				if request.Name!="ssh-add" || !reflect.DeepEqual(request.Args,[]string{"-L"}) || !reflect.DeepEqual(request.Env,[]string{"LC_ALL=C","SSH_AUTH_SOCK="}) { t.Fatalf("unexpected native request: %+v",request) }
				return test.result,test.runErr
			})}
			records,diagnostics,err:=s.readAgentKeys(t.Context(),&keyAgentContext{},"fixture inventory")
			if err!=nil || calls!=1 || (len(diagnostics)==0)!=test.complete || len(records)!=0 { t.Fatalf("records=%d diagnostics=%v err=%v calls=%d",len(records),diagnostics,err,calls) }
		})
	}
}

func TestAgentReaderCancellationPreventsExecution(t *testing.T) {
	ctx,cancel:=context.WithCancel(t.Context())
	cancel()
	s:=&Service{runner:panicRunner{}}
	if _,_,err:=s.readAgentKeys(ctx,&keyAgentContext{},"fixture inventory"); !errors.Is(err,context.Canceled) { t.Fatalf("canceled query=%v",err) }
}

func TestExplicitWindowsAgentsFailClosedWithoutPipeAttestation(t *testing.T) {
	paths := fixturePaths(t)
	s := newFixtureService(t, paths, DiscoverOptions{}) // Any runner invocation panics.
	path := filepath.Join(paths.Home, "not-a-pipe")
	writeFixture(t, path, "unchanged fixture")
	info, err := os.Lstat(path)
	if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
	if err := platformAgentSocket(path, info); !errors.Is(err, ErrManualRemediation) {
		t.Fatalf("regular Windows file accepted as an agent: %v", err)
	}

	// Use token-free native syntax to exercise attestation refusal itself. The
	// CI temporary path can contain RUNNER~1 and correctly fail syntax earlier.
	for _, socket := range []string{windowsOpenSSHAgentPipe, `C:\dev-agent-fixture\agent.sock`} {
		if err := ValidateAgentSocketPath(socket); err != nil { t.Fatalf("invalid test path %q: %v", socket, err) }
		if _, err := s.ResolveAgentSocket("windows", socket); !errors.Is(err, ErrManualRemediation) { t.Fatalf("unattested Windows path resolved: %v", err) }
		ref := AgentSocketRef{Provider:AgentProviderCustom, Socket:socket}
		if _, err := s.SelectAgentKey(t.Context(), ref, "SHA256:unknown"); !errors.Is(err, ErrManualRemediation) { t.Fatalf("unattested Windows agent queried: %v", err) }
		inventory, err := s.ObserveAgentKeys(t.Context(), ref)
		if !errors.Is(err, ErrManualRemediation) || inventory.Complete || inventory.state != nil { t.Fatalf("unattested Windows baseline=%+v err=%v", inventory, err) }
		catalog, err := s.Catalog(t.Context(), KeyCatalogRequest{LocalOnly:true, Agents:[]AgentSocketRef{ref}})
		if !errors.Is(err, ErrManualRemediation) || catalog.Complete || len(catalog.Candidates)!=0 { t.Fatalf("unattested Windows catalog=%+v err=%v", catalog, err) }
		if _, err := s.RefreshAgentKeys(t.Context(), AgentInventory{Agent:ref, Complete:true}); !errors.Is(err, ErrBlocked) { t.Fatalf("fabricated Windows baseline refreshed: %v", err) }
	}
	if got := s.ObserveAgentProviders("windows"); len(got) != 0 { t.Fatalf("unattested Windows pipe offered: %+v", got) }
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil || string(data)!="unchanged fixture" { t.Fatalf("agent refusal modified a file: %v", err) }
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(paths.SSHDir)
	if err != nil || len(entries)!=0 { t.Fatalf("agent refusal wrote SSH files: %v %v", entries, err) }
}

func TestWindowsAgentTokenPathsFailBeforeAttestation(t *testing.T) {
	s := newFixtureService(t, fixturePaths(t), DiscoverOptions{})
	for _, path := range []string{`C:\Users\RUNNER~1\agent.sock`, `C:\Users\%USERNAME%\agent.sock`, `C:\Users\${USER}\agent.sock`, `~\agent.sock`, "relative.sock"} {

		if _, err := s.ResolveAgentSocket("windows", path); !errors.Is(err, ErrUnsafePath) { t.Fatalf("unsafe path reached attestation: %q %v", path, err) }
	}
}

//go:build darwin || linux

package sshvault

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

func TestNativeACLDirectoryChurnKeepsSecuritySnapshot(t *testing.T) {
	directory:=t.TempDir()
	before,err:=os.Lstat(directory)
	if err!=nil { t.Fatal("stat owned directory fixture") }
	acl,err:=captureNativeACL(directory,before)
	if err!=nil { t.Fatal(err) }
	time.Sleep(5*time.Millisecond)
	if os.Mkdir(filepath.Join(directory,"unrelated-child"),0o700)!=nil { t.Fatal("create only unrelated owned sibling") }
	after,err:=os.Lstat(directory)
	if err!=nil||!os.SameFile(before,after)||before.Mode()!=after.Mode()||!nativeSameOwner(before,after) { t.Fatal("sibling fixture changed directory authority") }
	if nativeSameChangeTime(before,after) { t.Skip("filesystem did not expose the directory ctime transition") }
	observed,err:=captureNativeACL(directory,before)
	if err!=nil||observed!=acl { t.Fatalf("unrelated child creation invalidated unchanged directory security: %v",err) }
}

func TestNativeACLRegularFileChangeTimeRemainsGuarded(t *testing.T) {
	path:=filepath.Join(t.TempDir(),"owned-file")
	if os.WriteFile(path,[]byte("public fixture"),0o600)!=nil { t.Fatal("create owned file fixture") }
	before,err:=os.Lstat(path)
	if err!=nil { t.Fatal("stat owned file fixture") }
	time.Sleep(5*time.Millisecond)
	if os.Chmod(path,0o700)!=nil||os.Chmod(path,0o600)!=nil { t.Fatal("change and restore only owned fixture mode") }
	after,err:=os.Lstat(path)
	if err!=nil||!os.SameFile(before,after)||before.Mode()!=after.Mode() { t.Fatal("file fixture identity was not preserved") }
	if nativeSameChangeTime(before,after) { t.Skip("filesystem did not expose the file ctime transition") }
	if _,err:=captureNativeACL(path,before);!errors.Is(err,ErrStale) { t.Fatal("regular file ctime protection was weakened") }
}

func TestBitwardenNativeContextToleratesUnrelatedSiblingChurn(t *testing.T) {
	fixture:=newNativeFixture(t,false)
	stop,done:=make(chan struct{}),make(chan struct{})
	failures:=make(chan error,1)
	sibling:=filepath.Join(fixture.root,"unrelated-sibling")
	go func(){
		defer close(done)
		for {
			select { case <-stop:return;default: }
			if err:=os.Mkdir(sibling,0o700);err!=nil { failures<-err;return }
			if err:=os.Remove(sibling);err!=nil { failures<-err;return }
			time.Sleep(100*time.Microsecond)
		}
	}()
	t.Cleanup(func(){
		close(stop)
		<-done
		select { case <-failures:t.Error("owned sibling churn fixture failed");default: }
	})
	service,_:=countedNativeService(nil)
	plan,err:=service.Plan(context.Background(),nativeRequest())
	if err!=nil { t.Fatalf("unchanged native authority rejected during sibling churn: %v",err) }
	result,err:=service.Apply(context.Background(),plan)
	if err!=nil||!CanSelectAgentKey(plan,result) { t.Fatalf("sibling churn made unchanged native context uncertain: %v",err) }
}

```

14	
15	func nativeSameChangeTime(a, b fs.FileInfo) bool {
16		left, lok := a.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t)
17		right, rok := b.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t)
18		return lok && rok && left.Ctimespec == right.Ctimespec
19	}
20	
21	func captureNativeACL(path string, expected fs.FileInfo) (nativeACLObservation, error) {
22		flags := unix.O_RDONLY | unix.O_CLOEXEC | unix.O_NONBLOCK | unix.O_NOFOLLOW
23		if expected.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
24			// O_SYMLINK obtains the link's own inode rather than following it.
25			flags = unix.O_RDONLY | unix.O_CLOEXEC | unix.O_NONBLOCK | unix.O_SYMLINK
26		}
27		fd, err := unix.Open(path, flags, 0)
28		if err != nil {
29			return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrNativeContext
30		}
31		file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), path)
32		defer file.Close()
33		before, err := file.Stat()
34		if err != nil || !nativePermissionIdentity(expected, before) {
35			return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrStale
36		}
37		// Darwin ACLs are not reliably listed as xattrs. Use the same opened-inode
38		// ATTR_CMN_EXTENDED_SECURITY query as sshhost permissionCheckACL, not file
39		// contents or executable chmod/ACL text. Only documented deny-only metadata
40		// is accepted beyond the existing absence-only policy.
41		attributes := struct {
42			BitmapCount                           uint16
43			Reserved                              uint16
44			Common, Volume, Directory, File, Fork uint32
45		}{BitmapCount: 5, Common: unix.ATTR_CMN_EXTENDED_SECURITY}
46		var buffer [8192]byte
47		_, _, errno := unix.Syscall6(unix.SYS_FGETATTRLIST, file.Fd(), uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(&attributes)), uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(&buffer[0])), uintptr(len(buffer)), 0, 0)
48		runtime.KeepAlive(file)
49		runtime.KeepAlive(attributes)
50		if errno != 0 {
51			return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrNativeContext
52		}
53		observation, err := parseDarwinNativeACL(buffer[:])
54		if err != nil {
55			return nativeACLObservation{}, err
56		}
57		after, err := file.Stat()
58		current, pathErr := os.Lstat(path)
59		if err != nil || pathErr != nil || !nativePermissionIdentity(before, after) || !nativePermissionIdentity(after, current) {
60			return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrStale
61		}
62		return observation, nil
63	}

import (

func TestNativeACLReadRequiresTwoEqualSafeObservations(t *testing.T) {
	first:=nativeACLObservation{safe:true,digest:[32]byte{1}}
	changed:=nativeACLObservation{safe:true,digest:[32]byte{2}}
	for _, test:=range []struct{
		name string
		observations []nativeACLObservation
		failure error
		want error
	}{
		{"stable",[]nativeACLObservation{first,first},nil,nil},
		{"changed",[]nativeACLObservation{first,changed},nil,ErrStale},
		{"unknown-second",[]nativeACLObservation{first,{}},nil,ErrNativeContext},
		{"unknown-first",[]nativeACLObservation{{}},nil,ErrNativeContext},
		{"failed-read",[]nativeACLObservation{first},ErrUnavailable,ErrNativeContext},
	} {
		t.Run(test.name,func(t *testing.T){
			reads:=0
			result,err:=readStableNativeACL(func()(nativeACLObservation,error){
				if reads>=len(test.observations){t.Fatal("unexpected metadata retry")}
				value:=test.observations[reads]
				reads++
				return value,test.failure
			})
			if !errors.Is(err,test.want)||reads!=len(test.observations){t.Fatal("ACL observation stability was not enforced")}
			if err==nil&&result!=first||err!=nil&&result.safe{t.Fatal("unstable or unknown ACL became a safe observation")}
		})
	}
}

12	)
13	
14	func nativeSameChangeTime(a, b fs.FileInfo) bool {
15		left, lok := a.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t)
16		right, rok := b.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t)
17		return lok && rok && left.Ctim == right.Ctim
18	}
19	
20	func captureNativeACL(path string, expected fs.FileInfo) (nativeACLObservation, error) {
21		var file *os.File
22		list := func(buffer []byte) (int, error) { return unix.Llistxattr(path, buffer) }
23		if expected.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink == 0 {
24			fd, err := unix.Open(path, unix.O_RDONLY|unix.O_CLOEXEC|unix.O_NONBLOCK|unix.O_NOFOLLOW, 0)
25			if err != nil {
26				return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrNativeContext
27			}
28			file = os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), path)
29			defer file.Close()
30			opened, err := file.Stat()
31			if err != nil || !nativePermissionIdentity(expected, opened) {
32				return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrStale
33			}
34			list = func(buffer []byte) (int, error) { return unix.Flistxattr(fd, buffer) }
35		}
36		observation, err := readStableNativeACL(func() (nativeACLObservation, error) { return readLinuxNativeACL(list) })
37		if err != nil {
38			return nativeACLObservation{}, err
39		}
40		current, err := os.Lstat(path)
41		if err != nil || !nativePermissionIdentity(expected, current) {
42			return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrStale
43		}
44		if file != nil {
45			after, err := file.Stat()
46			if err != nil || !nativePermissionIdentity(expected, after) {
47				return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrStale
48			}
49		}
50		return observation, nil
51	}
52	
53	func readLinuxNativeACL(list func([]byte) (int, error)) (nativeACLObservation, error) {
54		// Like SSH's bounded metadata policy, reject access/default/NFS ACLs and
55		// other system/security policy attributes. Never read private file contents.
56		// Unsupported metadata queries are unknown, not an empty ACL observation.
57		size, err := list(nil)
58		if err != nil || size < 0 || size > 64<<10 {
59			return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrNativeContext
60		}
61		names := make([]byte, size)
62		if size > 0 {
63			n, err := list(names)
64			if err != nil || n < 0 || n > len(names) {
65				return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrNativeContext
66			}
67			names = names[:n]
68		}
69		for _, name := range strings.Split(string(names), "\x00") {
70			if strings.HasPrefix(name, "system.") || strings.HasPrefix(name, "security.") {
71				return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrNativeContext
72			}
73		}
74		return nativeACLObservation{safe: true}, nil
75	}

19	}
20	
21	func captureNativeACL(path string, expected fs.FileInfo) (nativeACLObservation, error) {
22		flags := unix.O_RDONLY | unix.O_CLOEXEC | unix.O_NONBLOCK | unix.O_NOFOLLOW
23		if expected.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
24			// O_SYMLINK obtains the link's own inode rather than following it.
25			flags = unix.O_RDONLY | unix.O_CLOEXEC | unix.O_NONBLOCK | unix.O_SYMLINK
26		}
27		fd, err := unix.Open(path, flags, 0)
28		if err != nil {
29			return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrNativeContext
30		}
31		file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), path)
32		defer file.Close()
33		before, err := file.Stat()
34		if err != nil || !nativePermissionIdentity(expected, before) {
35			return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrStale
36		}
37		observation, err := readStableNativeACL(func() (nativeACLObservation, error) { return readDarwinNativeACL(file) })
38		if err != nil {
39			return nativeACLObservation{}, err
40		}
41		after, err := file.Stat()
42		current, pathErr := os.Lstat(path)
43		if err != nil || pathErr != nil || !nativePermissionIdentity(before, after) || !nativePermissionIdentity(after, current) {
44			return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrStale
45		}
46		return observation, nil
47	}
48	
49	func readDarwinNativeACL(file *os.File) (nativeACLObservation, error) {
50		// Darwin ACLs are not reliably listed as xattrs. Use the same opened-inode
51		// ATTR_CMN_EXTENDED_SECURITY query as sshhost permissionCheckACL, not file
52		// contents or executable chmod/ACL text. Only documented deny-only metadata
53		// is accepted beyond the existing absence-only policy.
54		attributes := struct {
55			BitmapCount                           uint16
56			Reserved                              uint16
57			Common, Volume, Directory, File, Fork uint32
58		}{BitmapCount: 5, Common: unix.ATTR_CMN_EXTENDED_SECURITY}
59		var buffer [8192]byte
60		_, _, errno := unix.Syscall6(unix.SYS_FGETATTRLIST, file.Fd(), uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(&attributes)), uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(&buffer[0])), uintptr(len(buffer)), 0, 0)
61		runtime.KeepAlive(file)
62		runtime.KeepAlive(attributes)
63		if errno != 0 {
64			return nativeACLObservation{}, ErrNativeContext
65		}
66		return parseDarwinNativeACL(buffer[:])
67	}
68
```

這版包含：
- 自訂產生 key 的名稱、位置與 comment；可建立 `~/.ssh` 下一層資料夾。
- Bitwarden、1Password、Secretive／自訂 SSH agent 選取，僅保存 public selector。

- SSH onboarding 後立即刷新 FLEET，partial 結果列出未完成步驟。
